sentences.zh: 許譽卿

translations.literal: Xu Yuqing
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuqing

sentences.zh: 許譽卿，字公實，華亭人。

translations.literal: Xu Yuqing, styled Gongshi, was a native of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuqing, whose courtesy name was Gongshi, came from Huating.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士，授金華推官。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he became a jinshi and was appointed investigating censor of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign and was posted as magistrate of Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年，徵拜吏科給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi he was summoned and appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1623 he was called to court and made a supervising secretary in the personnel division of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 疏言錦衣世職，不當濫畀保姆閹尹。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said that hereditary posts in the Embroidered Uniform Guard ought not be lavished on wet nurses and eunuch stewards.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that hereditary offices in the Embroidered Uniform Guard should not be handed out indiscriminately to imperial wet nurses and eunuch attendants.

sentences.zh: 織造中官李實誣劾蘇州同知楊姜侵撫按職。

translations.literal: The weaving eunuch Li Shi falsely impeached Yang Jiang, vice prefect of Suzhou, for encroaching on the duties of the grand coordinator and regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, the eunuch superintendent of the weaving bureau, falsely accused Yang Jiang, the vice prefect of Suzhou, of usurping the authority of the provincial governor and censor.

sentences.zh: 中旨謂姜賄譽卿出疏，停譽卿俸半年。

translations.literal: An edict from within stated that Jiang had bribed Yuqing to submit the memorial, and Yuqing's salary was suspended for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript from the inner court claimed that Yang had bribed Xu to file the memorial, and Xu's salary was withheld for six months.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾魏忠賢，譽卿亦抗疏極論忠賢大逆不道：「視漢之朋結趙嬈，唐之勢傾中外，宋之典兵矯詔、謀間兩宮何異！」

translations.literal: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Yuqing also submitted a defiant memorial vehemently denouncing Zhongxian's monstrous treason: "How is this different from the Han clique around Zhao Feiyan, Tang power tilting inside and out, or Song usurpation of the army with forged edicts and plots between the two palaces!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Xu Yuqing likewise filed a bold memorial fiercely condemning Wei's capital crime of treason: "What difference is there from the Han faction that rallied around Zhao Feiyan, from Tang eunuchs whose power eclipsed court and countryside, or from Song generals who seized the army, forged edicts, and schemed between the two palaces!"

sentences.zh: 忠賢大怒。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was furious.

sentences.zh: 又言：「內閣政本重地，而票擬大權拱手授之內廷。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Grand Secretariat is the weighty seat of government, yet the great power of drafting rescripts has been handed over to the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "The Grand Secretariat is the vital center of government, yet the authority to draft and endorse memorials has been surrendered to the inner court.

sentences.zh: 廠衛一奉打問之旨，五毒備施。

translations.literal: Once the Brocade Guard and Eastern Depot receive an order to interrogate, all five tortures are applied.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the Brocade Guard and Eastern Depot receive a warrant for interrogation, every form of torture is brought to bear.

sentences.zh: 邇復用立枷法，士民槁項斃者不知凡幾。

translations.literal: Recently the standing-cangue method has been revived, and scholars and commoners who died with withered necks are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the standing cangue has been revived as well, and countless scholars and commoners have perished with their necks broken in the stocks.

sentences.zh: 又行數十年不行之廷杖，流毒縉紳，豈所以昭君德哉！

translations.literal: Court flogging, unused for decades, has again been imposed, its poison spreading among the gentry—how is this the way to display the ruler's virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Court flogging, abandoned for decades, has been revived, spreading terror through the official class—is this how the sovereign's virtue is to be shown!

sentences.zh: 祖制，宦官不典兵。

translations.literal: By ancestral regulation, eunuchs do not command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral law forbade eunuchs from holding military command.

sentences.zh: 今禁旅日繁，內操未罷，聚虎狼於蕭墻之內，逞金革於禁闥之中，不為早除，必貽後患。」

translations.literal: Now the palace guard grows daily, internal drilling has not ceased, tigers and wolves are gathered within the inner wall, and arms are brandished inside the forbidden gates—if not removed early, calamity will surely be left to posterity."
translations.idiomatic: Today the palace armies swell daily, internal drill has not ceased, wolves are massed within the palace walls, and weapons are exercised inside the forbidden gates—unless they are removed soon, disaster is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 於是忠賢怒益甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongxian's rage grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: At this Wei Zhongxian's fury only deepened.

sentences.zh: 會趙南星、高攀龍被逐，譽卿偕同列論救，遂鐫秩歸。

translations.literal: When Zhao Nanxing and Gao Panlong were driven out, Yuqing joined his colleagues in memorializing for their rescue and was consequently demoted in rank and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Nanxing and Gao Panlong were expelled, Xu joined his colleagues in pleading for them and was in turn stripped of rank and sent home.

sentences.zh: 七年起故官，歷工科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was restored to his former office and served as chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works section.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he was reinstated and rose to chief supervising secretary in the works division.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，流賊陷潁州，譽卿請急調五千人守鳳陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the roving bandits took Yingzhou; Yuqing requested that five thousand men be urgently transferred to defend Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, rebel armies captured Yingzhou, and Xu Yuqing urged that five thousand troops be rushed to defend Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 疏入而鳳陽已陷，皇陵毀焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Fengyang had already fallen and the imperial mausoleums were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time his memorial reached the throne, Fengyang had already fallen and the imperial tombs lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 譽卿痛憤，直發本兵張鳳翼固位失事，及大學士溫體仁、王應熊玩寇速禍罪。

translations.literal: Yuqing, in grief and rage, directly charged the Minister of War Zhang Fengyi with clinging to office and failing in duty, and the grand secretaries Wen Tiren and Wang Yingxiong with treating the bandits lightly and hastening disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Grief-stricken and furious, Xu openly accused Minister of War Zhang Fengyi of clinging to his post and bungling the campaign, and Grand Secretaries Wen Tiren and Wang Yingxiong of treating the rebels lightly and bringing calamity on the realm.

sentences.zh: 言：「賊在秦、晉時，早設總督，遏其渡河，禍止西北一隅耳，乃侍郎彭汝楠避不肯行。

translations.literal: He said: "When the bandits were in Qin and Jin, a supreme commander should have been appointed early to block their crossing of the Yellow River, and the disaster would have been confined to one corner of the northwest—but Vice Minister Peng Runan shrank from going.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "While the rebels were still in Shaanxi and Shanxi, a supreme commander should have been appointed at once to stop them from crossing the Yellow River, and the damage would have been confined to the northwest alone—but Vice Minister Peng Runan refused to take the post.

sentences.zh: 及賊入楚、豫，人言交攻，然後不得已而議設之。

translations.literal: When the bandits entered Chu and Yu, public criticism converged, and only then was it reluctantly discussed and established.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the rebels entered Hubei and Henan, when criticism from every quarter converged, was the post grudgingly created.

sentences.zh: 侍郎汪慶百又避不行，乃推極邊之陳奇瑜。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Qingbai again avoided going, and so Chen Qiyu of the far frontier was pushed forward.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Qingbai likewise declined to go, and Chen Qiyu, posted on the remotest frontier, was pushed forward instead.

sentences.zh: 鞭長不及，釀成今日之禍，非樞臣之固位失事乎？

translations.literal: The whip could not reach—today's disaster was brewed; is this not the fault of key ministers clinging to office and failing in their duties?
translations.idiomatic: Authority could not reach far enough, and today's catastrophe was brewed—is this not the fruit of senior ministers clinging to their posts and failing in their duties?

sentences.zh: 流寇發難已久，樞臣因東南震鄰，始有淮撫操江移鎮之疏，識者已恨其晚。

translations.literal: The roving bandits had risen long ago; only when the southeast was shaken by neighboring alarm did key ministers submit a memorial on moving the Huai governor and river-defense posts—those who understood already lamented how late it was.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel armies had been active for years; only when alarm spread in the southeast did senior ministers propose transferring the Huai governor and river-defense command—and informed observers already deplored how late that was.

sentences.zh: 及奉旨，則曰不必移鎮。

translations.literal: When the imperial order came, it said there was no need to move the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial edict arrived, it declared that no transfer was necessary.

sentences.zh: 臣觀各地方稍有兵力，賊即不敢輕犯。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that wherever a region has even a little military strength, the bandits do not dare lightly invade.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that wherever a province has even modest forces in place, the rebels do not dare attack lightly.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽何地，使巡撫早移，豈有今日！

translations.literal: What place is Fengyang! Had the grand coordinator moved early, how could there be today!
translations.idiomatic: What region is Fengyang! Had the governor transferred there in time, how could we have come to this!

sentences.zh: 今樞臣以曾請移鎮藉口，撫臣以不必移鎮為詞，則輔臣欲諱玩寇速禍，其可得哉！」

translations.literal: Now key ministers take having once requested a transfer as their excuse, and the grand coordinator takes "no need to transfer" as his plea—then can the assisting ministers conceal treating the bandits lightly and hastening disaster?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the senior ministers cite their earlier request to transfer troops, while the governor cites the edict that no transfer was needed—how can the grand secretaries still hide their negligence in treating the rebels lightly and hastening disaster?"

sentences.zh: 帝以苛求責之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for excessive demands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached him for making excessive demands.

sentences.zh: 而是時言官吳履中等復交章劾體仁、應熊交相贊美，「其擬旨慰留曰忠悃，曰藎畫，曰絕私奉公，曰弘濟時艱。

translations.literal: At this time the censor Wu Luzhong and others again submitted successive memorials impeaching Tiren and Yingxiong for mutual praise: "Their drafted edicts to retain them say 'loyal devotion,' 'faithful counsel,' 'utter selflessness in public service,' and 'greatly relieving the times' hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile censors such as Wu Luzhong filed further memorials impeaching Wen and Wang for praising each other: "The draft rescripts urging them to stay speak of loyal devotion, faithful counsel, selfless public service, and relieving the empire's hardships.

sentences.zh: 不知時事至此，忠藎安在，而奉公濟艱者何事也？」

translations.literal: They do not know that affairs have come to this—where is the loyal devotion, and what have those who serve the public and relieve hardship done?"
translations.idiomatic: Do they not see that affairs have come to this—where is their loyal devotion, and what have they done to serve the public or relieve the empire's distress?"

sentences.zh: 譽卿再疏論，帝仍不問。

translations.literal: Yuqing memorialized again, but the emperor still took no action.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuqing memorialized again, but the emperor still paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 譽卿曰：「皇上臨馭有年，法無假貸，獨於誤國輔臣不一問。

translations.literal: Yuqing said: "Your Majesty has ruled for many years; the law grants no indulgence—yet toward assisting ministers who have harmed the state you make not a single inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuqing wrote: "Your Majesty has reigned for many years, and the law knows no mercy—yet toward the grand secretaries who have harmed the state you have not asked a single question.

sentences.zh: 今者巡撫楊一鵬、巡按吳振纓且相繼就逮矣。

translations.literal: Now the grand coordinator Yang Yipeng and regional inspector Wu Zhenyong are about to be arrested in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Already Grand Coordinator Yang Yipeng and Regional Inspector Wu Zhenyong are being arrested one after another.

sentences.zh: 輔臣顧從容入直，退食委蛇，謂可超然事外乎？」

translations.literal: Yet the assisting ministers calmly enter duty, retire to eat at ease—do they think they can stand aloof from affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the grand secretaries stroll calmly into the palace, dine at leisure, and retire—do they imagine they can stand above these affairs?"

sentences.zh: 帝終不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 譽卿在天啟時，謝升方為文選郎。

translations.literal: During Tianqi, Yuqing knew Xie Sheng when Sheng was a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign Xu Yuqing had known Xie Sheng when the latter was a clerk in the personnel selection bureau.

sentences.zh: 及是，升長吏部，譽卿猶滯垣中。

translations.literal: By this time Sheng headed the Ministry of Personnel, while Yuqing still languished in the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: By now Xie headed the Ministry of Personnel, while Xu Yuqing still remained stuck in the censorate.

sentences.zh: 以資深當擢京卿，升希體仁意，出之南京。

translations.literal: By seniority he should have been promoted to a capital minister; Sheng, wishing to please Tiren, posted him to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: By seniority he should have been promoted to a capital ministry post, but Xie, eager to please Wen Tiren, sent him to Nanjing instead.

sentences.zh: 大學士文震孟慍語侵升，升亦慍。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wen Zhenmeng spoke in anger, his words encroaching on Sheng, and Sheng too was angered.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wen Zhenmeng spoke angrily in terms that slighted Xie, and Xie was offended in turn.

sentences.zh: 適山東布政使勞永嘉賄營登萊巡撫，主給事中宋之普家，升等列之舉首，為給事中張第元所發。

translations.literal: Just then Shandong provincial administration commissioner Lao Yongjia bribed to secure the Deng-Lai grand coordinator post; the chief supervising secretary Song Zhipu hosted him, and Sheng and others listed him first in the nomination—this was exposed by supervising secretary Zhang Diyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shandong provincial commissioner Lao Yongjia bribed his way toward the Dengzhou-Laizhou governorship; Chief Supervising Secretary Song Zhipu hosted him at home, and Xie and others placed his name first on the nomination list—until Supervising Secretary Zhang Diyuan exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 帝以詰升，言路因欲攻升及都御史唐世濟。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Sheng on it, and the censorial route therefore sought to attack Sheng and Censor-in-Chief Tang Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Xie about it, and the censorial corps then moved to attack both Xie and Censor-in-Chief Tang Shiji.

sentences.zh: 譽卿以世濟恃體仁，惡尤甚，當先去之。

translations.literal: Yuqing held that Shiji, relying on Tiren, was the worse evil and should be removed first.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuqing argued that Tang Shiji, who relied on Wen Tiren, was the greater evil and ought to be removed first.

sentences.zh: 御史張纘曾乃獨劾升，升疑出譽卿及震孟意，之普又構之升。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Zuanzeng alone impeached Sheng; Sheng suspected this came from Yuqing and Zhenmeng's intent, and Zhipu also framed matters for Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Zuanzeng alone impeached Xie; Xie suspected this sprang from Xu Yuqing and Wen Zhenmeng, while Song Zhipu also fed Xie false charges.

sentences.zh: 先是，福建布政使申紹芳亦欲得登萊巡撫，譽卿曾言之升。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fujian provincial administration commissioner Shen Shaofang had also wished to obtain the Deng-Lai grand coordinator post, and Yuqing had once spoken of it to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fujian provincial commissioner Shen Shaofang had also sought the Dengzhou-Laizhou post, and Xu Yuqing had once mentioned him to Xie.

sentences.zh: 升遂疏攻譽卿，謂其營求北缺，不欲南遷，為把持朝政地，並及囑紹芳事。

translations.literal: Sheng then memorialized attacking Yuqing, saying he schemed for a northern vacancy, did not wish to move south, and sought a foothold to manipulate court politics, also involving the matter of recommending Shaofang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie then filed a memorial attacking Xu Yuqing, charging that he had lobbied for a northern post, refused to accept transfer to the south, and sought leverage to dominate court politics, and he also implicated Xu in the Shen Shaofang affair.

sentences.zh: 體仁從中主之，譽卿遂削籍，紹芳逮問遣戍。

translations.literal: Tiren backed it from within, and Yuqing was consequently struck from the rolls; Shaofang was arrested, questioned, and banished to military service.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren backed the attack from within, and Xu Yuqing was struck from the official rolls; Shen Shaofang was arrested, tried, and exiled to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 十五年，御史劉逵及給事中楊枝起相繼論薦，竟不果用。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Censor Liu Kui and supervising secretary Yang Zhiqi successively recommended him in memorials, but he was ultimately not employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Censor Liu Kui and Supervising Secretary Yang Zhiqi successively recommended him, but he was never reappointed.

sentences.zh: 福王立，起光祿卿，不赴。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Xu was appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 國變，發為僧，久之卒。

translations.literal: When the dynasty fell, he took the tonsure and became a monk; after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he became a monk, and many years later he died.

sentences.zh: 華允誠

translations.literal: Hua Yuncheng
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yuncheng

sentences.zh: 華允誠，字汝立，無錫人。

translations.literal: Hua Yuncheng, styled Ruli, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yuncheng, whose courtesy name was Ruli, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖舜欽，瑞州知府。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shunqin was prefect of Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shunqin had served as prefect of Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖啟直，四川參政。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qizhi was administration vice commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qizhi had been administration vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 允誠舉天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: Yuncheng passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 從同里高攀龍講學首善書院，先後旋裏，遂受業為弟子，傳其主靜之學。

translations.literal: He followed his fellow townsman Gao Panlong in lecturing at the Shoushan Academy; when Panlong later returned home, Yuncheng became his disciple and transmitted his learning of preserving stillness.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under his fellow townsman Gao Panlong at the Shoushan Academy; when Gao later returned home, Hua became his disciple and carried on his doctrine of cultivating inner stillness.

sentences.zh: 四年春，從攀龍入都，授都水司主事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he followed Panlong to the capital and was appointed director in the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he followed Gao Panlong to the capital and was appointed a director in the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 攀龍去官，允誠亦告歸。

translations.literal: When Panlong left office, Yuncheng also requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Panlong resigned, Hua Yuncheng likewise asked to retire home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，起營繕主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Chongzhen he was recalled as director of construction and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as a construction director and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，京師戒嚴，分守德勝門，四十余日不懈，帝微行察知之，賜白金，敘功，加俸一年，改職方員外郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year the capital was placed under martial law; he was assigned to defend Desheng Gate and for more than forty days did not slacken; the emperor, making a secret inspection, learned of it, bestowed white silver, recorded his merit, added one year's salary, and transferred him to vice director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year, when the capital was placed under martial law, he was assigned to defend Desheng Gate and for more than forty days never slackened; the emperor learned of this on a secret inspection tour, rewarded him with silver, recorded his merit, granted an extra year's salary, and transferred him to the Bureau of Military Appointments as vice director.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，以溫體仁、閔洪學亂政，疏陳三大可惜、四大可憂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, on the grounds that Wen Tiren and Min Hongxue were disordering government, he submitted a memorial setting forth three great regrets and four great worries.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year he memorialized that Wen Tiren and Min Hongxue were corrupting government, setting forth three grave regrets and four grave worries.

sentences.zh: 略言：

translations.literal: In summary he said:
translations.idiomatic: In summary he wrote:

sentences.zh: 當事借皇上剛嚴，而佐以舞文擊斷之術，倚皇上綜核，而騁其訟逋握算之能，遂使和恒之世競尚刑名，清明之躬浸成叢脞。

translations.literal: Those in power borrow the emperor's stern severity and assist it with the arts of twisting texts and harsh judgment; they rely on his comprehensive scrutiny and display their skill in litigation, arrears, and reckoning—thus in an age that should be harmonious and constant, punishment and statutes are competitively honored, and upon a clear-sighted personage, pettifogging gradually forms.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power exploit the emperor's stern severity and reinforce it with legalistic severity and harsh judgments; they lean on his demand for comprehensive scrutiny and parade their skill in lawsuits, tax arrears, and accounts—so that in what should be an age of harmony, punitive law is exalted, and upon a ruler of clarity, petty administration takes hold.

sentences.zh: 以聖主圖治之盛心，為諸臣鬥智之捷徑。

translations.literal: The sage ruler's great intent to bring order through government becomes a shortcut for ministers' contests of wits.
translations.idiomatic: The sage ruler's earnest desire to govern well has become a shortcut for ministers' contests of wits.

sentences.zh: 可惜一。

translations.literal: The first regret.
translations.idiomatic: The first regret.

sentences.zh: 帥屬大僚，驚魂於回奏認罪；

translations.literal: Commanders and great officials are terrified souls in replying to memorials and confessing guilt;
translations.idiomatic: Field commanders and senior officials live in terror of drafting replies and confessing guilt;

sentences.zh: 封駁重臣，奔命於接本守科。

translations.literal: those who remonstrate and seal rescripts rush about receiving drafts and guarding regulations.
translations.idiomatic: while remonstrating ministers exhaust themselves receiving drafts and guarding procedural rules.

sentences.zh: 遂使直指風裁徒征事件，長吏考課惟問錢糧。

translations.literal: Thus censorial integrity is reduced to investigating isolated incidents, and the evaluation of chief officials asks only about taxes and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Thus censorial integrity is reduced to chasing isolated cases, and the evaluation of senior officials asks only about taxes and grain.

sentences.zh: 以多士靖共之精神，為案牘鉤較之能事。

translations.literal: The spirit by which many scholars should bring peace and harmony together becomes the chief talent for checking documents and comparing figures.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit by which the empire's scholars should work in harmony has become chiefly a talent for checking documents and comparing figures.

sentences.zh: 可惜二。

translations.literal: The second regret.
translations.idiomatic: The second regret.

sentences.zh: 廟堂不以人心為憂，政府不以人才為重。

translations.literal: The court does not take popular sentiment as its worry, and the government does not take talent as its weight.
translations.idiomatic: The court does not worry about the people's hearts, and the government does not value talent.

sentences.zh: 四海漸成土崩瓦解之形，諸臣但有角戶分門之念。

translations.literal: Within the four seas the form of earth collapsing and tiles breaking apart gradually appears, while ministers have only thoughts of contending households and divided factions.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is gradually taking the shape of collapse, while ministers think only of factional rivalry and divided cliques.

sentences.zh: 意見互犄，議論滋擾。

translations.literal: Opinions clash against one another, and debate grows ever more turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Opinions clash, and debate grows ever more turbulent.

sentences.zh: 遂使剿撫等於築舍，用舍有若舉棋。

translations.literal: Thus suppression and appeasement are like building a house in the air, and appointment and dismissal are like moving chess pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Thus suppression and appeasement are like building on sand, and appointments and dismissals are like moving pieces on a chessboard.

sentences.zh: 以興邦啟聖之歲時，為即聾從昧之舉動。

translations.literal: In years meant to raise the state and inaugurate sage rule, actions are those of the deaf following the blind.
translations.idiomatic: In years meant to revive the state and inaugurate sage rule, the court acts like the blind leading the blind.

sentences.zh: 可惜三。

translations.literal: The third regret.
translations.idiomatic: The third regret.

sentences.zh: 人主所以總一天下者，法令也。

translations.literal: What the ruler uses to bring all under Heaven together is law and command.
translations.idiomatic: What binds the empire together under the sovereign is law.

sentences.zh: 喪師誤國之王化貞，與楊鎬異辟；

translations.literal: Wang Huazhen, who lost the army and harmed the state, received a different penalty from Yang Hao;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huazhen, who lost armies and harmed the state, was punished differently from Yang Hao;

sentences.zh: 潔己愛民之余大成，與孫元化並逮。

translations.literal: Yu Dacheng, who kept himself pure and loved the people, was arrested together with Sun Yuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: while Yu Dacheng, who kept himself pure and loved the people, was arrested together with Sun Yuanhua.

sentences.zh: 甚至一言一事之偶誤，執訊隨之。

translations.literal: Even a single mistaken word or act brings immediate arrest and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Even a single mistaken word or act brings immediate arrest and interrogation.

sentences.zh: 遂使刑罰不中，鈇鉞無威。

translations.literal: Thus punishments miss the mark, and axe and halberd have no authority.
translations.idiomatic: Thus punishments miss their mark, and the instruments of execution lose their authority.

sentences.zh: 一可憂也。

translations.literal: The first worry.
translations.idiomatic: The first worry.

sentences.zh: 國家所恃以為元氣者，公論也。

translations.literal: What the state relies on as its vital breath is public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: What the state relies on as its vital breath is public opinion.

sentences.zh: 直言敢諫之士一鳴輒斥，指佞薦賢之章目為奸黨，不惟不用其言，並錮其人，又加之罪。

translations.literal: Men who speak plainly and dare remonstrate are expelled at the first sound; memorials denouncing flatterers and recommending the worthy are labeled factions of traitors—not only are their words unused, but the men are imprisoned and further charged with crime.
translations.idiomatic: Men who speak plainly and dare remonstrate are expelled at the first word; memorials denouncing flatterers and recommending the worthy are labeled traitorous factions—not only are their words ignored, but the men are imprisoned and further charged with crimes.

sentences.zh: 遂使喑默求容，是非共蔽。

translations.literal: Thus silence and seeking favor prevail, and right and wrong are together obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Thus silence and self-preservation prevail, and right and wrong are obscured together.

sentences.zh: 二可憂也。

translations.literal: The second worry.
translations.idiomatic: The second worry.

sentences.zh: 國家所賴以防維者，廉恥也。

translations.literal: What the state relies on for defense and preservation is integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: What the state relies on to hold itself together is integrity and shame.

sentences.zh: 近者中使一遣，妄自尊大，群僚趨走，惟恐後時。

translations.literal: Lately when a palace envoy is dispatched once, he arrogantly sets himself above others, and the host of officials rush about, fearing only to be late.
translations.idiomatic: Lately whenever a palace envoy is dispatched, he arrogantly sets himself above others, and officials rush to attend him, fearing only to be late.

sentences.zh: 皇上以近臣可倚，而不知幸竇已開；

translations.literal: Your Majesty thinks palace intimates can be relied upon, but does not know the gate of favoritism has been opened;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty believes palace intimates can be relied upon, but does not see that the gate of favoritism has been opened;

sentences.zh: 以操縱惟吾，而不知屈辱士大夫已甚。

translations.literal: that manipulation is yours alone, but does not know how greatly the scholar-officials have already been humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: that all control rests in your hands, but does not see how deeply the scholar-officials have already been humiliated.

sentences.zh: 遂使阿諛成風，羞惡盡喪。

translations.literal: Thus flattery becomes the fashion, and shame and revulsion are altogether lost.
translations.idiomatic: Thus flattery becomes the fashion, and shame and moral revulsion are altogether lost.

sentences.zh: 三可憂也。

translations.literal: The third worry.
translations.idiomatic: The third worry.

sentences.zh: 國家所藉以進賢退不肖者，銓衡也。

translations.literal: What the state uses to advance the worthy and dismiss the unworthy is the balance of selection.
translations.idiomatic: What the state uses to advance the worthy and dismiss the unworthy is the personnel selection system.

sentences.zh: 我朝罷丞相，以用人之權歸之吏部，閣臣不得侵焉。

translations.literal: Our dynasty abolished the chief counselor and returned the power of employing men to the Ministry of Personnel, which grand secretaries may not encroach upon.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty abolished the chief counselor and returned the power of appointment to the Ministry of Personnel, which grand secretaries may not encroach upon.

sentences.zh: 今次輔體仁與冢臣洪學，同邑朋比，惟異己之驅除。

translations.literal: Now the second grand secretary Tiren and the head minister Hongxue, fellow townsmen in league, seek only to drive out those unlike themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now Second Grand Secretary Wen Tiren and Minister Hongxue, fellow townsmen in league, seek only to drive out those unlike themselves.

sentences.zh: 閣臣兼操吏部之權，吏部惟阿閣臣之意，造門請命，夜以為常。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries also wield the Ministry of Personnel's power; the Ministry of Personnel only follows the grand secretaries' wishes—visiting their doors to receive orders has become normal by night.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries now wield the Ministry of Personnel's power as well; the ministry follows only their wishes, and visiting their doors for orders at night has become routine.

sentences.zh: 黜陟大柄，只供報復之私。

translations.literal: The great handle of dismissal and promotion serves only private revenge.
translations.idiomatic: The great power of appointment and dismissal serves only private revenge.

sentences.zh: 甚至庇同鄉，則逆黨公然保舉，而白簡反為罪案；

translations.literal: Even to shield a fellow townsman, traitor-faction members are openly recommended, while impeachment memorials in turn become criminal cases;
translations.idiomatic: To shield a fellow townsman, members of the opposing faction are openly recommended, while impeachment memorials in turn become criminal cases;

sentences.zh: 排正類，則講官借題逼逐，而薦剡遂作爰書。

translations.literal: To drive out upright men, lecturing officials seize pretexts to hound them out, and recommendation tablets in turn become criminal indictments.
translations.idiomatic: To purge upright officials, lecturing officials seize pretexts to drive them out, and letters of recommendation in turn become criminal indictments.

sentences.zh: 欺莫大於此矣，擅莫專於此矣，黨莫固於此矣。

translations.literal: No deception is greater than this, no usurpation more exclusive than this, no faction more solid than this.
translations.idiomatic: No deception is greater than this, no usurpation more absolute than this, and no faction more entrenched than this.

sentences.zh: 遂使威福下移，舉措倒置。

translations.literal: Thus authority and favor shift downward, and measures are turned upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Thus power and favor have shifted downward, and government measures are turned upside down.

sentences.zh: 四可憂也。

translations.literal: The fourth worry.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth worry.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝詰其別有指使。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor questioned whether he had been directed by someone else.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor demanded to know who had put him up to it.

sentences.zh: 允誠乃列上洪學徇私數事，且曰：「體仁生平，紾臂塗顏，廉隅掃地。

translations.literal: Yuncheng then listed several instances of Hongxue's favoritism and said: "Throughout his life Tiren has been one who would strangle an arm and smear a face—his integrity swept clean from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng then listed several instances of Hongxue's favoritism and wrote: "Throughout his career Wen Tiren has been a man who would strangle an arm and smear a face—his integrity utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 陛下排眾議而用之，以其悻直寡諧，豈知包藏禍心，陰肆其毒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty set aside the multitude's objections and employed him, taking him for obstinately upright and ill-suited to harmony—how could you know he harbored a treacherous heart and secretly unleashed his poison?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty overrode widespread opposition to appoint him, thinking him stubbornly upright and hard to get along with—who could have known he harbored treacherous intent and secretly unleashed his poison?

sentences.zh: 又有如洪學者，為之羽翼，遍植私人，戕盡善類，無一人敢犯其鋒者，臣復受何人指使？」

translations.literal: Moreover there are men like Hongxue who serve as his wings, planting private followers everywhere, destroying all the good—not one dares meet their edge—so from whom could your servant receive direction?"
translations.idiomatic: Men like Hongxue serve as his wings, planting private followers everywhere and destroying every worthy man, so that no one dares challenge them—so from whom could I possibly be taking orders?"

sentences.zh: 帝以體仁純忠亮節，而摘疏中「握定機關」語，再令陳狀。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Tiren was purely loyal with bright integrity, seized the phrase "grasping the levers of power" in the memorial and ordered him to state his case again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, convinced that Wen Tiren was purely loyal and upright, seized on the phrase "grasping the levers of power" in the memorial and ordered Hua to elaborate further.

sentences.zh: 允誠復上言：「二人朋比，舉朝共知。

translations.literal: Yuncheng memorialized again: "The two men are in league—this the whole court knows.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yuncheng memorialized again: "The two men are in league—this the whole court knows.

sentences.zh: 溫育仁不識一丁，以家貲而首拔。

translations.literal: Wen Yuren could not recognize a single character and was first promoted because of family wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yuren could not recognize a single character and was promoted first because of family wealth.

sentences.zh: 鄧英以論沈演而謫，羅喻義以『左右非人』一語而逐。

translations.literal: Deng Ying was demoted for criticizing Shen Yan; Luo Yuyi was driven out for the single phrase 'those at your side are not proper men.'
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ying was demoted for criticizing Shen Yan; Luo Yuyi was expelled for the single phrase "those at your side are not proper men."

sentences.zh: 此非事之章明較著者乎？」

translations.literal: Are these not matters clear and evident?"
translations.idiomatic: Are these not matters clear for all to see?"

sentences.zh: 帝亦悟兩人同里有私，乃奪允誠俸半年，而洪學亦旋罷去。

translations.literal: The emperor also perceived that the two men, fellow townsmen, had private ties, and so withheld Yuncheng's salary for half a year, while Hongxue was soon dismissed as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also saw that the two men, fellow townsmen, had private ties, and so withheld Hua's salary for six months, while Hongxue was soon dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 其冬，以省親歸，孝養母。

translations.literal: That winter he returned home to visit his parents and dutifully cared for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he returned home on leave to visit his parents and devoted himself to caring for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母年八十三而終。

translations.literal: His mother died at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 後為福王驗封員外郎，十餘日即引疾歸。

translations.literal: Later, under the Prince of Fu, he was made a verification-seal vice director, but after little more than ten days he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under the Prince of Fu, he was appointed verification-seal vice director, but after little more than ten days he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 允誠踐履篤實，不慕榮達。

translations.literal: Yuncheng's conduct was earnest and solid; he did not covet glory or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yuncheng's conduct was earnest and solid; he did not covet glory or advancement.

sentences.zh: 延儒再召，遣人以京卿啖之，允誠拒不應。

translations.literal: When Yan Ruzhi was recalled again, he sent someone to tempt Yuncheng with a capital ministry post, but Yuncheng refused to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yanru was recalled again, he sent someone to tempt Hua with a capital ministry post, but Hua refused to respond.

sentences.zh: 入南都，士英先造請，亦不報謝。

translations.literal: Entering the Southern Capital, Ma Shiying was the first to call on him, but he did not return the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered the Southern Capital, Ma Shiying was the first to call on him, but he did not return the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 國變後，屏居墓田，不肯發，與從孫尚濂駢斬於南京。

translations.literal: After the dynastic collapse he secluded himself on his family's tomb lands and would not come forth; he and his nephew Shang Lian were executed together at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he secluded himself on his family's tomb lands and would not emerge; he and his nephew Shang Lian were executed together at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 魏呈潤

translations.literal: Wei Chengrun
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chengrun

sentences.zh: 魏呈潤，字中嚴，龍溪人。

translations.literal: Wei Chengrun, styled Zhongyan, was a native of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chengrun, whose courtesy name was Zhongyan, came from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the first year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士改兵科給事中。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Ministry of War section.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he was transferred to supervising secretary in the war division of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，疏陳兵屯之策：「請敕順天、保定兩巡撫簡所部壯士，大邑五百人，小邑二三百人，分營訓練。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he memorialized on the policy of military colonies: "I request an edict ordering the grand coordinators of Shuntian and Baoding to select stalwart men from their jurisdictions—five hundred for large districts, two or three hundred for small ones—and train them in separate camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he memorialized on military colonies: "I request that the grand coordinators of Shuntian and Baoding be ordered to select able-bodied men from their jurisdictions—five hundred for large districts, two or three hundred for small ones—and train them in separate camps.

sentences.zh: 而天津翟鳳翀、通州範景文、昌平侯恂並建節鉞，宜令練兵之外兼營屯田。」

translations.literal: Zhai Fengchong at Tianjin, Fan Jingwen at Tongzhou, and Marquis Hou Xun at Changping all hold military commissions—they should be ordered, besides drilling troops, also to establish garrison farms."
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Fengchong at Tianjin, Fan Jingwen at Tongzhou, and Marquis Hou Xun at Changping all hold military commissions—they should be ordered, in addition to drilling troops, to establish garrison farms as well."

sentences.zh: 又陳閩海剿撫機宜六事。

translations.literal: He also set forth six points on the proper measures for suppressing and appeasing the Fujian coast.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth six points on the proper measures for suppressing and appeasing the Fujian coast.

sentences.zh: 並議行。

translations.literal: All were discussed and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，久旱求言。

translations.literal: The next summer, after prolonged drought, the court sought advice.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer, after a prolonged drought, the court solicited advice.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「驛站所裁，才六十萬，未足充軍餉十一，而郵傳益疲，勢必再編裏甲。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The cuts to courier stations amount to only six hundred thousand, not enough to supply one part in eleven of military pay, while the postal relay grows ever more exhausted—inevitably the lijia registers will have to be reorganized again.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The cuts to courier stations amount to only six hundred thousand taels, not enough to supply even a tenth of military pay, while the postal relay grows ever more exhausted—the lijia registers will inevitably have to be reorganized again.

sentences.zh: 是猶剜肉醫瘡，瘡未瘳而肉先潰。

translations.literal: This is like cutting flesh to treat a sore—the sore is not healed while the flesh first putrefies.
translations.idiomatic: This is like cutting flesh to treat a sore—the sore is not healed while the flesh rots first.

sentences.zh: 關外舊兵十八萬，額餉七百余萬；

translations.literal: Formerly there were one hundred eighty thousand troops beyond the passes, with allotted pay of more than seven million;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly there were one hundred eighty thousand troops beyond the passes, with allotted pay of more than seven million taels;

sentences.zh: 今兵止十萬七千，合薊門援卒，非溢原數，加派五百九十萬外，新增又百四十余萬，猶憂不足，可不為稽核乎！

translations.literal: now there are only one hundred seven thousand troops, and counting Jizhou relief soldiers, they do not exceed the original number—yet beyond the additional levy of five million nine hundred thousand, new additions exceed one million four hundred thousand more, and still there is worry of insufficiency—should this not be audited!
translations.idiomatic: now there are only one hundred seven thousand troops, and counting Jizhou relief soldiers, they do not exceed the original number—yet beyond the additional levy of five million nine hundred thousand taels, new additions exceed one million four hundred thousand more, and still there is worry of insufficiency—should this not be audited!

sentences.zh: 邊報告急，非臣子言功之日，而小捷頻聞，躐加峻秩，門客廝養詭名戎籍，不階而升，悉糜俸料，臣懼其難繼也。

translations.literal: Border reports are urgent—this is not the day for ministers to speak of merit—yet small victories are frequently heard, and steep ranks are leapfrogged; retainers and servants are falsely entered on military rolls, rise without steps, and all drain salary funds—your servant fears this cannot be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Border reports are urgent—this is not the time for ministers to boast of merit—yet small victories are frequently reported, and steep promotions leapfrogged; retainers and servants are falsely entered on military rolls, rise without steps, and all drain salary funds—I fear this cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 江淮旱災，五湖之間，海岸為谷，舊谷不登，新絲未熟，上供織造，宜且暫停。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Huai region suffers drought disaster; between the five lakes the seacoast has become valleys, old grain does not ripen, new silk is not yet mature—tribute weaving for the court should for the time being be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai region suffers from drought; between the five lakes the seacoast has become valleys, last year's grain has not ripened, and this year's silk is not yet ready—tribute weaving for the court should be suspended for the time being.

sentences.zh: 銓法壞於事例，正途日壅，不可不疏通。

translations.literal: The selection law is ruined by precedents; the regular path grows daily blocked—it cannot but be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The selection law is ruined by precedents; the regular path of advancement grows daily blocked—it must be cleared.

sentences.zh: 撫按諸臣捐貲助餉，大抵索之民間，顧奉急公之褒。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators and regional inspectors donate funds to aid military pay, but for the most part they exact them from the people while seeking praise for urgent public service.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators and regional inspectors donate funds to aid military pay, but for the most part they exact them from the people while seeking praise for urgent public service.

sentences.zh: 上蒙而下削，不可不禁飭。」

translations.literal: The upper levels are deceived while the lower are squeezed—this cannot but be forbidden and corrected."
translations.idiomatic: The upper levels are deceived while the lower are squeezed—this must be forbidden and corrected."

sentences.zh: 又條陳數策，請大修北方水政。

translations.literal: He also itemized several policies and requested a major overhaul of northern water administration.
translations.idiomatic: He also itemized several policies and requested a major overhaul of northern water administration.

sentences.zh: 帝皆納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 宣府監視中官王坤以冊籍委頓，劾巡按御史胡良機。

translations.literal: Wang Kun, the eunuch supervisor at Xuanfu, impeached Regional Inspector Hu Liangji on the grounds that the registers were in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun, the eunuch supervisor at Xuanfu, impeached Regional Inspector Hu Liangji on the grounds that the registers were in disorder.

sentences.zh: 帝奪良機官，即令坤按核。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Liangji of his office and immediately ordered Kun to investigate and verify.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Hu of his office and immediately ordered Kun to investigate.

sentences.zh: 呈潤上言：「我國家設御史巡九邊，秩卑而任鉅。

translations.literal: Chengrun memorialized: "Our state appoints censors to tour the nine border regions—rank low but responsibility great.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chengrun memorialized: "Our state appoints censors to tour the nine border regions—low in rank but great in responsibility.

sentences.zh: 良機在先朝以糾逆璫削籍，今果有罪，則有回道考核之法在，而乃以付坤。

translations.literal: Liangji in the previous reign was struck from the rolls for impeaching the treacherous eunuch; if he is truly guilty now, there is the law of return-route assessment—yet he is handed over to Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Liangji in the previous reign was struck from the rolls for impeaching the treacherous eunuch; if he is truly guilty now, there is the law of return-route assessment—yet he is handed over to Kun.

sentences.zh: 且邊事日壞，病在十羊九牧。

translations.literal: Moreover border affairs worsen daily—the disease lies in ten sheep and nine shepherds.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover border affairs worsen daily—the disease lies in too many masters for too few tasks.

sentences.zh: 既有將帥，又有監司；

translations.literal: There are already generals and commanders, and also surveillance commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: There are already generals and commanders, and also surveillance commissioners;

sentences.zh: 既有督撫，有巡方，又有監視。

translations.literal: there are already supreme commanders and grand coordinators, regional inspectors, and also supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: there are already supreme commanders and grand coordinators, regional inspectors, and also eunuch supervisors.

sentences.zh: 一官出，增一官擾，中貴之威，又復十倍。

translations.literal: One official goes out, one more official adds disturbance, and the eunuch's authority is again tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Each new official adds another layer of interference, and the eunuch's authority is multiplied tenfold.

sentences.zh: 御史偶獲戾，且莫自必其命，誰復以國事抗者。

translations.literal: A censor who happens to offend cannot even be sure of his life—who will again resist on behalf of state affairs?
translations.idiomatic: A censor who happens to offend cannot even be sure of his life—who will again speak up for the state's affairs?

sentences.zh: 異日九邊聲息，監視善惡，奚從而聞之？

translations.literal: In future, news from the nine borders—good or ill of the supervisors—from what source will it be heard?
translations.idiomatic: In future, news from the nine borders—whether the supervisors are good or bad—from what source will it be heard?

sentences.zh: 乞召還良機，毋使仰鼻息於中貴。」

translations.literal: I beg that Liangji be recalled and not made to depend on the breath of eunuchs."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Hu Liangji be recalled and not made to depend on the breath of eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 帝以呈潤黨比，貶三級，出之外。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Chengrun was factional, demoted him three ranks and sent him outside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding that Wei Chengrun was factional, demoted him three ranks and sent him into exile.

sentences.zh: 良機者，南昌人也，字省之。

translations.literal: Liangji was a man of Nanchang, styled Shengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Liangji was a man of Nanchang, whose courtesy name was Shengzhi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 天啟間為御史，嘗糾魏忠賢之惡不減汪直、劉瑾。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he served as censor and once impeached Wei Zhongxian, saying his evil was no less than Wang Zhi's or Liu Jin's.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he served as censor and once impeached Wei Zhongxian, saying his evil was no less than that of Wang Zhi or Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 忠賢憾之，以年例遷廣東參議。

translations.literal: Zhongxian resented him and, under the seniority rule, transferred him to administration vice commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian resented him and, under the seniority rule, transferred him to administration vice commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 良機方按貴州，不候代而去，遂斥為民。

translations.literal: Liangji was then inspecting Guizhou; he left without waiting for his replacement and was consequently dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was then inspecting Guizhou; he left without waiting for his replacement and was consequently dismissed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年起故官，按宣、大二鎮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was restored to his former office and inspected the Xuan and Da garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was restored to his former office and inspected the Xuanfu and Datong garrisons.

sentences.zh: 年滿當代，以其敏練，再巡一年。

translations.literal: When his term was full and he should have been replaced, because of his alert competence he was allowed to inspect for one more year.
translations.idiomatic: When his term was full and he should have been replaced, because of his alert competence he was allowed to inspect for one more year.

sentences.zh: 至是，遂為坤劾罷。

translations.literal: At this point he was impeached and dismissed by Kun.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he was impeached and dismissed by Wang Kun.

sentences.zh: 時又有御史李曰輔者，亦以論中官獲譴，廷臣交章論救，不聽。

translations.literal: At this time there was also Censor Li Yefu, who likewise was punished for criticizing palace eunuchs; court ministers submitted successive memorials pleading for him, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: At this time there was also Censor Li Yefu, who likewise was punished for criticizing palace eunuchs; court ministers submitted successive memorials pleading for him, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 而御史趙東曦又疏劾坤，亦獲譴云。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Dongxi also memorialized impeaching Kun and likewise was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Dongxi also memorialized impeaching Kun and likewise was punished.

sentences.zh: 李曰輔

translations.literal: Li Yefu
translations.idiomatic: Li Yefu

sentences.zh: 曰輔，字元卿，亦南昌人也，與胡良機同里闬。

translations.literal: Yefu, styled Yuanqing, was also a man of Nanchang and a fellow townsman of Hu Liangji.
translations.idiomatic: Yefu, whose courtesy name was Yuanqing, was also a man of Nanchang and a fellow townsman of Hu Liangji.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉於鄉，為成都推官。

translations.literal: During Wanli he passed the provincial examination and served as investigating censor of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 與巡撫朱燮元計兵事，偕諸將攻復重慶。

translations.literal: With Grand Coordinator Zhu Xieyuan he planned military affairs and, together with the generals, attacked and recovered Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand Coordinator Zhu Xieyuan he planned military affairs and, together with the generals, attacked and recovered Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was promoted to censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was promoted to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時中官四出，張彜憲總理戶、工錢糧，唐文征提督京營戎政，王坤監餉宣府，劉文忠監餉大同，劉允中監餉山西。

translations.literal: At this time palace eunuchs were dispatched in four directions: Zhang Yixian superintended the funds of the Ministries of Revenue and Works; Tang Wenzheng supervised military affairs of the capital garrison; Wang Kun supervised rations at Xuanfu; Liu Wenzhong supervised rations at Datong; Liu Yunzhong supervised rations at Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At this time palace eunuchs were dispatched in four directions: Zhang Yixian superintended the funds of the Ministries of Revenue and Works; Tang Wenzheng supervised military affairs of the capital garrison; Wang Kun supervised rations at Xuanfu; Liu Wenzhong supervised rations at Datong; and Liu Yunzhong supervised rations at Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 又命王應期監軍關、寧，張國元監軍東協，王之心監軍中協，鄧希詔監軍西協，又命吳直監餉登島，李茂奇監茶馬陜西。

translations.literal: Wang Yingqi was also ordered to supervise troops at Shanhaiguan and Ningyuan; Zhang Guoyuan the eastern defense; Wang Zhixin the central defense; Deng Xizhao the western defense; Wu Zhi was ordered to supervise rations at Dengzhou and the islands; Li Maoqi to supervise tea and horses in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingqi was also ordered to supervise troops at Shanhaiguan and Ningyuan; Zhang Guoyuan the eastern defense; Wang Zhixin the central defense; Deng Xizhao the western defense; Wu Zhi to supervise rations at Dengzhou and the islands; and Li Maoqi to supervise tea and horses in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 曰輔上疏諫曰：「邇者一日遣內臣四，尋又遣用五，非兵機則要地也。

translations.literal: Yefu memorialized in remonstrance: "Recently four palace eunuchs were dispatched in one day, and soon five more were sent out—each to a military post or vital place.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yefu memorialized in remonstrance: "Recently four palace eunuchs were dispatched in one day, and soon five more were sent out—each to a military post or vital place.

sentences.zh: 廷臣方交章，而登島、陜西又有兩閹之遣。

translations.literal: Court ministers were just submitting successive memorials, when Dengzhou, the islands, and Shaanxi received two more eunuch dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers were just submitting successive memorials, when Dengzhou, the islands, and Shaanxi received two more eunuch dispatches.

sentences.zh: 假專擅之權，駭中外之聽，啟水火之隙，開依附之門，灰任事之心，藉委卸之口。

translations.literal: They borrow arbitrary power, alarm listeners inside and out, open rifts of fire and water, open doors of dependency, extinguish the will to serve, and provide excuses for shirking duty.
translations.idiomatic: They borrow arbitrary power, alarm listeners inside and out, open rifts of fire and water, open doors of dependency, extinguish the will to serve, and provide excuses for shirking duty.

sentences.zh: 臣愚實為寒心。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant is truly chilled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly chilled at heart.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐阼初，盡撤內臣，中外稱聖。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, all palace eunuchs were withdrawn, and inside and out proclaimed you sage.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, all palace eunuchs were withdrawn, and inside and out proclaimed you sage.

sentences.zh: 昔何以撤，今何以遣？

translations.literal: Why were they withdrawn then, and why are they dispatched now?
translations.idiomatic: Why were they withdrawn then, and why are they dispatched now?

sentences.zh: 天下多故，擇將為先。

translations.literal: The realm has many troubles—choosing generals should come first.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has many troubles—choosing generals should come first.

sentences.zh: 陛下不築黃金臺招頗、牧，乃汲汲內臣是遣，曾何補理亂之數哉！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not build a golden terrace to summon a Lian Po or Li Mu, but is eager to dispatch palace eunuchs—how does this aid the reckoning of order and disorder!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not build a golden terrace to summon a Lian Po or Li Mu, but is eager to dispatch palace eunuchs—how does this aid the reckoning of order and disorder!"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫曰輔廣東布政司照磨。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Yefu to registrar of the Guangdong provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted Li Yefu to registrar of the Guangdong provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 趙東曦

translations.literal: Zhao Dongxi
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dongxi

sentences.zh: 東曦，字馭初，上海人。

translations.literal: Dongxi, styled Yuchu, was a man of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxi, whose courtesy name was Yuchu, came from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-seventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，由知縣人為刑科給事中，請興屯塞下，以充軍用，不報。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, from magistrate he entered service as supervising secretary of the Ministry of Punishments section, requesting garrison colonies below the passes to supply military use—no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, from magistrate he entered service as supervising secretary in the punishments division, requesting garrison colonies below the passes to supply military use—no reply was given.

sentences.zh: 適宣塞有私和事，王坤時監宣餉，且請代。

translations.literal: Just then there was a private peace affair at Xuan garrison; Wang Kun was then supervising Xuan rations and also requested replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Just then there was a private peace affair at Xuan garrison; Wang Kun was then supervising Xuan rations and also requested replacement.

sentences.zh: 東曦上言：「宣塞失事，陛下赫然震怒，逮巡撫沈棨，罷本兵熊明遇。

translations.literal: Dongxi memorialized: "When Xuan garrison failed in duty, Your Majesty was greatly angered, arrested Grand Coordinator Shen Qi, and dismissed Minister of War Xiong Mingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dongxi memorialized: "When Xuan garrison failed in duty, Your Majesty was greatly angered, arrested Grand Coordinator Shen Qi, and dismissed Minister of War Xiong Mingyu.

sentences.zh: 乃監視王坤方會飲城樓，商榷和議，邊臣倚庇，欺蔽日甚。

translations.literal: Yet Supervisor Wang Kun was just then feasting on the city tower, discussing peace terms; border officials relied on his protection, and deception grew daily worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Supervisor Wang Kun was just then feasting on the city tower, discussing peace terms; border officials relied on his protection, and deception grew daily worse.

sentences.zh: 坤不得辭扶同罪，反侈邊烽已熄為己功，且請代。

translations.literal: Kun cannot escape the crime of abetting it, yet instead boasts that border beacons have been extinguished as his own merit, and moreover requests replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Kun cannot escape the crime of abetting it, yet instead boasts that border beacons have been extinguished as his own merit, and moreover requests replacement.

sentences.zh: 夫內臣之遣，陛下一用之，非不易之典，今即盡撤之，猶謂不早。

translations.literal: The dispatch of palace eunuchs—Your Majesty uses it once, and it is not an unchangeable institution; even if all were now withdrawn, it would still be said it was not early enough.
translations.idiomatic: The dispatch of palace eunuchs—Your Majesty uses it once, and it is not an unchangeable institution; even if all were now withdrawn, it would still be said it was not early enough.

sentences.zh: 坤顧請代，圖彌縫於去後。

translations.literal: Kun only requests replacement, plotting to paper over matters after he leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Kun only requests replacement, plotting to paper over matters after he leaves.

sentences.zh: 願陛下正坤罪，撤各使還京。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would punish Kun's crime and recall all the envoys to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would punish Kun's crime and recall all the envoys to the capital."

sentences.zh: 帝言：「宣鎮擅和，實坤奏發，何謂欺隱？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Xuan garrison's unauthorized peace was in fact exposed by Kun's memorial—how can this be called concealment?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Xuan garrison's unauthorized peace was in fact exposed by Kun's memorial—how can this be called concealment?"

sentences.zh: 調東曦外任，謫福建布政司都事。

translations.literal: Dongxi was transferred to an outside post and demoted to secretary of the Fujian provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dongxi was transferred to an outside post and demoted to secretary of the Fujian provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 異時呈潤起官，以光祿署丞終。

translations.literal: Later Chengrun was restored to office and ended as deputy director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Chengrun was restored to office and ended as deputy director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 良機起光祿典簿，終南京吏部主事。

translations.literal: Liangji was restored as registrar of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and ended as director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Liangji was restored as registrar of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and ended as director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 東曦稍遷行人司正、禮部郎中，奉使還裏。

translations.literal: Dongxi was gradually promoted to chief of the embassy service and bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, and returned home after an imperial mission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dongxi was gradually promoted to chief of the embassy service and bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, and returned home after an imperial mission.

sentences.zh: 福王時，召東曦為給事中，曰輔為御史，而二人者皆已死矣。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, Dongxi was summoned as supervising secretary and Yefu as censor—but both men were already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Zhao Dongxi was summoned as supervising secretary and Li Yefu as censor—but both men were already dead.

sentences.zh: 毛羽健

translations.literal: Mao Yujian
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yujian

sentences.zh: 毛羽健，字芝田，公安人。

translations.literal: Mao Yujian, styled Zhitian, was a native of Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yujian, whose courtesy name was Zhitian, came from Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，由知縣征授御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, from magistrate he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen, from magistrate he was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 好言事，首劾楊維垣八大罪及阮大鋮反覆變幻狀，二人遂被斥。

translations.literal: He was fond of speaking on affairs of state; first he impeached Yang Weiyuan on eight major crimes and set forth Ruan Dacheng's shifting, treacherous conduct, and the two men were thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was outspoken on state affairs and led with an impeachment of Yang Weiyuan on eight grave charges, together with an account of Ruan Dacheng's treacherous reversals; both men were expelled from office.

sentences.zh: 王師討安邦彥久無功。

translations.literal: The imperial army's campaign against An Bangyan long achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: The court's campaign against An Bangyan had dragged on without victory.

sentences.zh: 羽健言：「賊巢在大方，黔其前門，蜀遵、永其後戶。

translations.literal: Yujian said: "The bandits' nest is at Dafang; Guizhou is their front gate, and Sichuan's Zunyi and Yong are their rear door.
translations.idiomatic: Yujian argued: "The rebels' stronghold lies at Dafang—Guizhou blocks their front gate, while Zunyi and Yong in Sichuan guard their rear exit.

sentences.zh: 由黔進兵，必渡陸廣奇險，七晝夜抵大方，一夫當關，千人自廢，王三善、蔡復一所以屢敗也。

translations.literal: Advancing troops from Guizhou, one must cross the extraordinary peril of Luguang; in seven days and nights one reaches Dafang—where one man holds the pass, a thousand men are wasted; this is why Wang Sanshan and Cai Fuyi suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: An advance from Guizhou forces troops through the deadly Luguang route; even after seven days and nights to reach Dafang, a single defender at the pass can nullify a thousand men—hence the repeated defeats of Wang Sanshan and Cai Fuyi.

sentences.zh: 遵義距大方三日程，而畢節止百余裏平衍，從此進兵，何患不克？」

translations.literal: Zunyi is three days' march from Dafang, while Bijie lies only a little over a hundred li away across level ground; advancing from here, what worry is there of not conquering?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunyi is only three days from Dafang, and Bijie lies barely a hundred li away over open terrain; march from there, and how could victory be in doubt?"

sentences.zh: 因畫上足兵措餉方略，並薦舊總督朱燮元、閔夢得等。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a painted plan for fully staffing troops and arranging supplies, and jointly recommended the former grand coordinators Zhu Xieyuan, Min Mengde, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a detailed plan for troop strength and provisioning, and recommended former grand coordinators Zhu Xieyuan, Min Mengde, and others.

sentences.zh: 帝即議行，後果平賊。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately deliberated on carrying it out, and afterward the bandits were indeed pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promptly ordered the plan implemented, and the rebels were eventually crushed.

sentences.zh: 已，陳驛遞之害：「兵部勘合有發出，無繳入。

translations.literal: Thereafter he set forth the harms of the courier relay system: "The Ministry of War's travel warrants are issued but never returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he memorialized on abuses in the courier relay: "The Ministry of War issues travel warrants that are never returned.

sentences.zh: 士紳遞相假，一紙洗補數四。

translations.literal: Gentry lend them back and forth to one another; a single sheet is washed and patched four or five times.
translations.idiomatic: Officials pass them among themselves; a single document may be washed and patched four or five times over.

sentences.zh: 差役之威如虎，小民之命如絲。」

translations.literal: The power of runners is like a tiger; the lives of common people are like a thread."
translations.idiomatic: Runners wield power like tigers, while ordinary people's lives hang by a thread."

sentences.zh: 帝即飭所司嚴加厘革，積困為蘇。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered the responsible offices strictly to rectify and reform, and long-standing hardship was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered the relevant agencies to crack down and reform the system, easing burdens that had piled up for years.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，閹黨既敗，東林大盛。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch faction had already been defeated, and the Donglin was in great ascendancy.
translations.idiomatic: By then the eunuch faction had fallen, and the Donglin party was at its height.

sentences.zh: 而朝端王永光陰陽閃爍，溫體仁猾賊，周延儒回佞。

translations.literal: Yet at court Wang Yongguang was evasive and shifting, Wen Tiren crafty and treacherous, and Zhou Yanru sly and fawning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court Wang Yongguang was evasive and two-faced, Wen Tiren cunning and treacherous, and Zhou Yanru sly and obsequious.

sentences.zh: 言路新進標直之徒，尤競抨擊以為名高。

translations.literal: Among the newly advanced, ostentatiously upright men of the remonstrance offices, they especially competed in attacks to make a name for loftiness.
translations.idiomatic: Newly risen censors and memorialists, eager to appear upright, competed in denunciations to burnish their reputations.

sentences.zh: 體仁之訐錢謙益也，以科場舊事，延儒助之惡，且目攻己者為結黨欺君，帝怒而為之罷會推矣。

translations.literal: When Tiren impeached Qian Qianyi, it was on an old examination-field affair; Yanru assisted in the evil, and moreover labeled those who attacked him as forming a faction to deceive the ruler; the emperor grew angry and for this suspended the joint recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren's attack on Qian Qianyi rested on an old examination scandal; Zhou Yanru abetted the scheme, and Tiren branded his critics as a faction deceiving the throne. The emperor's anger led him to suspend the regular joint recommendation process.

sentences.zh: 御史黃宗昌疏糾體仁熱中枚卜，欲以「結黨」二字破前此公論之不予，且箝後來言路之多口。

translations.literal: Censor Huang Zongchang submitted a memorial impeaching Tiren for zealously pursuing the chancellorship, wishing to use the two words "forming a faction" to break the earlier public consensus that had not favored him, and moreover to gag the many mouths of the remonstrance offices to come.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huang Zongchang impeached Wen Tiren for scheming after the chancellorship, aiming to use the charge of "faction" to overturn prior public opposition and silence future critics in the remonstrance offices.

sentences.zh: 羽健亦憤朋黨之說，曰：「彼附逆諸奸既不可用，勢不得不用諸奸擯斥之人。

translations.literal: Yujian also resented the talk of factions, saying: "Those traitors who attached themselves to the rebels can no longer be employed; the situation compels the employment of men whom those traitors drove out.
translations.idiomatic: Yujian likewise bristled at factional rhetoric: "The traitors who sided with the rebels cannot be used—but that leaves no choice but to employ men those traitors once expelled.

sentences.zh: 如以今之連袂登進者為相黨而來，抑將以昔之鱗次削奪者為相黨而去乎！

translations.literal: If those who now advance arm in arm are called a faction coming in, will those who in the past were stripped rank after rank be called a faction going out!
translations.idiomatic: If today's men rising together are a faction arriving, were yesterday's men stripped of office one after another a faction departing?

sentences.zh: 陛下不識在朝諸臣與奸黨諸臣之孰正孰邪，不觀天啟七年前與崇禎元年後之天下乎，孰危孰安？

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not distinguish which of the ministers at court and which of the ministers of the traitor faction are upright and which are depraved; you do not observe the realm before the seventh year of Tianqi and after the first year of Chongzhen—which was perilous and which was secure?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cannot tell which court ministers are upright and which belonged to the traitor faction; you do not compare the empire before the seventh year of Tianqi with that after the first year of Chongzhen—which was dangerous, and which was safe?

sentences.zh: 今日語太平則不足，語剔弊則有余，諸臣亦何負國家哉！

translations.literal: Today to speak of peace is insufficient, yet to speak of rooting out abuses there is surplus; how have the ministers failed the state!
translations.idiomatic: We are far from peace, yet there is no shortage of abuses to expose—how have your ministers wronged the state?

sentences.zh: 一夫高張，輒疑舉朝皆黨，則株連蔓引，不且一網盡哉！」

translations.literal: When one man raises himself high, you at once suspect the whole court of being a faction; then implicating and drawing in by tendrils—will not the whole net be taken at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Let one man grow bold, and you suspect the entire court of factionalism; pursue guilt by association, and will you not sweep everyone into one net?"

sentences.zh: 帝責羽健疑揣，而以前條陳驛遞原之。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Yujian for suspicion and surmise, yet excused him on account of his earlier memorial on the courier relay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Yujian for suspicion and presumption, but pardoned him because of his earlier memorial on the courier relay.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿謝升求巡撫於永光，永光長吏部，升當推薊鎮，畏而引病以避，後推太仆則不病。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Xie Sheng sought a provincial governorship from Yongguang; Yongguang headed the Ministry of Personnel, and when Sheng was due to be recommended for Jizhen, he feared this and pleaded illness to avoid it—yet when later recommended for the Court of Imperial Studs he was not ill.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Xie Sheng asked Wang Yongguang for a provincial post. As head of the Ministry of Personnel, Yongguang was to recommend Sheng for Jizhen; Sheng feigned illness to avoid the appointment, yet showed no illness when later slated for the Court of Imperial Studs.

sentences.zh: 羽健劾升、永光朋比，宜並罪。

translations.literal: Yujian impeached Sheng and Yongguang for factional collusion; both ought to be punished together.
translations.idiomatic: Yujian impeached Sheng and Yongguang for collusion and demanded that both be punished.

sentences.zh: 永光召對文華殿，力詆羽健，請究主使之者。

translations.literal: Yongguang was summoned to audience in the Wenhua Hall and vehemently denounced Yujian, requesting that the instigator be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience in the Wenhua Hall, Yongguang fiercely denounced Yujian and demanded investigation of whoever had put him up to it.

sentences.zh: 大學士韓爌曰：「究言官，非體也。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Han Kuang said: "To investigate a remonstrance official is not proper form."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Han Kuang said: "Investigating a censor is not proper procedure."

sentences.zh: 帝不從，已而宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this, yet afterward pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, but later pardoned Yujian.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝御文華殿，獨召延儒語良久，事秘，舉朝疑駭。

translations.literal: One day the emperor held court in the Wenhua Hall and summoned Yanru alone to speak at length; the matter was secret, and the whole court was suspicious and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor presided in the Wenhua Hall and summoned Zhou Yanru alone for a long private audience; the matter was kept secret, and the whole court was uneasy.

sentences.zh: 羽健曰：「召見不以盈廷而以獨侍，清問不以朝參而以燕間；

translations.literal: Yujian said: "Summons to audience ought not to be with a full court but with solitary attendance; imperial inquiries ought not to be at court assembly but in leisurely privacy;
translations.idiomatic: Yujian protested: "An audience should fill the hall, not isolate a single minister; imperial questions belong in formal court, not in private leisure.

sentences.zh: 更漏已沈，閣門猶啟。

translations.literal: The night watches had already sunk deep, yet the gate of the privy council was still open.
translations.idiomatic: The night watches had long run down, yet the privy council gate still stood open.

sentences.zh: 漢臣有言『所言公，公言之；

translations.literal: A Han minister once said, "What is spoken as public—speak it publicly;
translations.idiomatic: As a Han minister once said, "What concerns the public, speak in public;

sentences.zh: 所言私，王者不受私』。」

translations.literal: what is spoken as private—the king does not receive what is private."
translations.idiomatic: what is private—the ruler does not accept private words."

sentences.zh: 疏入，切責。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, he was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 羽健既積忤權要，其黨思因事去之。

translations.literal: Yujian had long accumulated offenses against powerful men, and their faction sought an occasion to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Yujian had long offended the powerful, and their allies looked for a chance to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 及袁崇煥下獄，主事陸澄源以羽健嘗疏譽崇煥，劾之，落職歸。

translations.literal: When Yuan Chonghuan was imprisoned, Chief Clerk Lu Chengyuan, because Yujian had once memorialized in praise of Chonghuan, impeached him, and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chonghuan was thrown into prison, chief clerk Lu Chengyuan impeached Yujian for having once praised Chonghuan in a memorial; Yujian was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 黃宗昌

translations.literal: Huang Zongchang
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongchang

sentences.zh: 黃宗昌，字長倩，即墨人。

translations.literal: Huang Zongchang, styled Changqian, was a native of Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongchang, whose courtesy name was Changqian, came from Jimo.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，為御史，請斥矯旨偽官，言：「先帝賓天在八月二十三日。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he served as censor and requested dismissal of officials appointed under forged edicts, saying: "The late emperor ascended to Heaven on the twenty-third day of the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he became a censor and demanded removal of officials appointed under forged edicts, arguing: "The late emperor died on the twenty-third day of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 三殿敘功止先一日，正當帝疾大漸之時，豈能安閑出詔？

translations.literal: The recording of merit for the three halls stopped only one day earlier, right when the emperor's illness was critically advanced—how could he calmly issue an edict?
translations.idiomatic: Merit rolls for the three halls were issued only the day before, when the emperor lay gravely ill—how could he calmly have promulgated an edict?

sentences.zh: 凡加銜進秩，皆魏氏官也。」

translations.literal: All added titles and advanced ranks were Wei-clique appointments."
