translations.idiomatic: Every added title and promotion was a Wei-clique appointment."

sentences.zh: 得旨：「汰敘功冒濫者。」

translations.literal: An edict responded: "Cull those who falsely claimed merit in the reward rolls."
translations.idiomatic: The response was: "Purge those who falsely claimed merit in the reward rolls."

sentences.zh: 宗昌爭曰：「臣所糾乃矯旨，非冒濫也。

translations.literal: Zongchang contended: "What your servant impeaches is forged edicts, not mere false claims.
translations.idiomatic: Zongchang objected: "What I impeach is forged edicts, not mere padding of merit rolls.

sentences.zh: 冒濫猶可容，矯偽不可貸。」

translations.literal: False claims may still be tolerated; forgery and fraud cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Inflated claims might be tolerated; outright forgery cannot be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 遂列上黃克纘、範濟世、霍維華、邵輔忠、呂純如等六十一人，乞罷免。

translations.literal: Thereupon he listed and submitted Huang Kezuan, Fan Jishi, Huo Weihua, Shao Fuzhong, Lü Chunru, and sixty-one others in all, requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a list of sixty-one men including Huang Kezuan, Fan Jishi, Huo Weihua, Shao Fuzhong, and Lü Chunru, asking that they all be removed.

sentences.zh: 帝以列名多，不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the list of names was long, did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, citing the length of the list.

sentences.zh: 尋劾罷逆黨尚書張我續、侍郎呂圖南、通政使嶽駿聲、給事中潘士聞、御史王珙。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached and brought down the rebel-party ministers Zhang Woxu, Vice Minister Lü Tunan, Communications Commissioner Yue Junsheng, Supervising Secretary Pan Shiwen, and Censor Wang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached and ousted rebel-party officials: Minister Zhang Woxu, Vice Minister Lü Tunan, Communications Commissioner Yue Junsheng, Supervising Secretary Pan Shiwen, and Censor Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 又劾周延儒貪穢數事，帝怒，停俸半年。

translations.literal: He again impeached Zhou Yanru on several counts of greed and corruption; the emperor was angry and suspended his salary for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: He later impeached Zhou Yanru on multiple counts of corruption; the emperor was furious and suspended his salary for six months.

sentences.zh: 既而劾體仁，不納。

translations.literal: Thereafter he impeached Tiren, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Wen Tiren, but the memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，巡按湖廣。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year he toured and inspected Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year he was assigned as touring inspector of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 岷王禋洪為校尉侍聖及善化王長子企鋀等所弒，參政龔承薦等不以實聞，獄不決者久之。

translations.literal: Prince Min of Min, Chen Hong, was murdered by the bodyguard Shisheng and the eldest son of the Prince of Shanhua, Qi Mao, and others; Vice Minister Gong Chengjian and others did not report the facts, and the case long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chen Hong of Min was murdered by the bodyguard Shisheng and Qi Mao, eldest son of the Prince of Shanhua, among others; Vice Minister Gong Chengjian and others concealed the facts, and the case dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 宗昌至，群奸始伏辜。

translations.literal: When Zongchang arrived, the whole gang of villains at last paid for their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongchang arrived, the conspirators were finally brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 帝責問前諸臣失出罪，宗昌糾承薦等。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached the earlier ministers for the crime of omission in reporting; Zongchang impeached Chengjian and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed the earlier officials for failing to report the truth; Zongchang impeached Chengjian and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 時體仁、延儒皆已入閣，而永光意忌，以為不先劾承薦也。

translations.literal: At the time Tiren and Yanru had both entered the Grand Secretariat, yet Yongguang bore resentment and held that he had not first impeached Chengjian.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wen Tiren and Zhou Yanru had both entered the Grand Secretariat, but Wang Yongguang resented Zongchang for not having impeached Chengjian first.

sentences.zh: 鐫宗昌四級，宗昌遂歸。

translations.literal: Zongchang was demoted four ranks, and Zongchang thereupon returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Zongchang was demoted four ranks and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十五年，即墨被兵，宗昌率鄉人拒守，城全。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Jimo suffered military attack; Zongchang led the people of his district to resist and defend, and the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when Jimo came under attack, Zongchang led local defense and the city held.

sentences.zh: 仲子基中流矢死，其妻周氏及三妾郭氏、二劉氏殉之，謂之「一門五烈」。

translations.literal: His second son Ji was struck by a flying arrow and died; his wife Lady Zhou and three concubines, the Guo and two Liu ladies, died with him—they were called "five martyrs in one household."
translations.idiomatic: His second son Ji died of an arrow wound; his wife Lady Zhou and three concubines—Lady Guo and two Ladies Liu—followed him in death, earning the epithet "five martyrs in one household."

sentences.zh: 韓一良

translations.literal: Han Yiliang
translations.idiomatic: Han Yiliang

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝初在位，銳意圖治，數召見群臣論事。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor first took the throne, he was keen to seek good government and repeatedly summoned ministers to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign the Chongzhen Emperor was determined to restore good government and often summoned ministers to debate policy.

sentences.zh: 然語不合，輒訶譴。

translations.literal: Yet when words did not accord, he would at once rebuke and reprove.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever replies displeased him, he would rebuke and berate them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 而王永光長吏部，尤樂沮之。

translations.literal: Wang Yongguang, who headed the Ministry of Personnel, especially delighted in obstructing this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yongguang, as head of the Ministry of Personnel, was especially eager to thwart such exchanges.

sentences.zh: 澄城人韓一良者，元年授戶科給事中，言：「陛下平臺召對，有『文官不愛錢』語，而今何處非用錢之地？

translations.literal: Han Yiliang of Chengcheng, in the first year appointed supervising secretary of the Household Section, said: "When Your Majesty held platform audiences, there was the saying that civil officials do not love money—yet today where is there not a place that uses money?
translations.idiomatic: Han Yiliang of Chengcheng, appointed supervising secretary of the Household Section in the first year, said: "Your Majesty declared at court that civil officials should not love money—yet where today is money not spent?

sentences.zh: 何官非愛錢之人？

translations.literal: What office is not staffed by men who love money?
translations.idiomatic: What office is not filled by men who love money?

sentences.zh: 向以錢進，安得不以錢償。

translations.literal: Having advanced by money, how can they not repay with money.
translations.idiomatic: They bought their way in—how could they not pay their way out?

sentences.zh: 以官言之，則縣官為行賄之首，給事為納賄之尤。

translations.literal: Speaking by office, then the district magistrate is chief among bribe-givers, and the supervising secretary chief among bribe-takers.
translations.idiomatic: By rank, the district magistrate leads in giving bribes, and the supervising secretary leads in taking them.

sentences.zh: 今言者俱咎守令不廉，然守令亦安得廉？

translations.literal: Today remonstrators all blame prefects and magistrates for lack of integrity—yet how can prefects and magistrates be integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Critics today blame prefects and magistrates for corruption—yet how can they stay honest?

sentences.zh: 俸薪幾何，上司督取，過客有書儀，考滿、朝覲之費，無慮數千金。

translations.literal: Salaries are how much? Superiors press for collection; traveling guests bring letter-gifts; expenses for completion of term and court audience—no less than several thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Their salaries are trifling, yet superiors demand levies, traveling guests bring customary gifts, and costs for term reviews and capital audiences run to thousands of taels.

sentences.zh: 此金非從天降，非從地出，而欲守令之廉，得乎？

translations.literal: This gold does not fall from heaven, does not spring from earth—yet you wish prefects and magistrates to be integrity: is it possible?
translations.idiomatic: That money does not fall from heaven or rise from the earth—yet you expect magistrates to remain honest. Is that possible?

sentences.zh: 臣兩月來，辭卻書帕五百金，臣寡交猶然，余可推矣。

translations.literal: Your servant in two months has declined letter-presents of five hundred in gold; your servant has few associations and is still thus— the rest may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: In two months I have refused gift money totaling five hundred taels; with my few connections I still face this much—imagine the rest.

sentences.zh: 伏乞陛下大為懲創，逮治其尤者。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty greatly to punish and reform, and seize and punish the worst offenders."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to punish corruption severely and prosecute the worst offenders."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，召見廷臣，即令一良宣讀。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, summoned the court ministers to audience, and immediately ordered Yiliang to read it aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, summoned the court, and ordered Yiliang to read the memorial aloud.

sentences.zh: 讀已，以疏遍視閣臣曰：「一良忠鯁，可僉都御史。」

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, he showed the memorial all around to the Grand Secretariat ministers, saying: "Yiliang is loyal and upright; he may be appointed Censor-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: After the reading he showed the memorial to the Grand Secretaries, saying: "Yiliang is loyal and outspoken—appoint him Censor-in-Chief."

sentences.zh: 永光請令指實。

translations.literal: Yongguang requested that he be made to name specifics.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguang asked that he name names.

sentences.zh: 一良唯唯，如不欲告訐人者，則令密奏。

translations.literal: Yiliang assented evasively, as one unwilling to inform on others; then he was ordered to submit a secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yiliang hedged, as if reluctant to accuse anyone, and was told to submit a secret memorial instead.

sentences.zh: 五日不奏，而舉周應秋、閻鳴泰一二舊事為言，語頗侵永光。

translations.literal: For five days he did not memorialize, but cited one or two old affairs of Zhou Yingqiu and Yan Mingtai in speaking; his words somewhat encroached on Yongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Five days passed without a memorial; he finally cited old cases involving Zhou Yingqiu and Yan Mingtai, wording that edged toward an attack on Yongguang.

sentences.zh: 帝乃再召見一良、永光及廷臣，手前疏循環頌，音瑯然，而曰「此金非從天降，非從地出」，則掩卷而嘆。

translations.literal: The emperor then again summoned Yiliang, Yongguang, and the court ministers; holding the earlier memorial he recited it in turn, his voice clear and ringing, and when he came to "this gold does not fall from heaven, does not spring from earth," he closed the scroll and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yiliang, Yongguang, and the court again, took the memorial in hand, and recited it aloud in a ringing voice; at the line "this money does not fall from heaven or rise from the earth" he closed the scroll and sighed.

sentences.zh: 問一良：「五百金誰之饋也？」

translations.literal: He asked Yiliang: "Five hundred in gold—whose gift was it?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yiliang: "Who gave you those five hundred taels?"

sentences.zh: 一良卒無所指。

translations.literal: Yiliang in the end named no one.
translations.idiomatic: Yiliang ultimately named no one.

sentences.zh: 固問，則對如前。

translations.literal: Pressed repeatedly, he answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again and again, he gave the same evasive answer.

sentences.zh: 帝欲一良指實，將有所懲創，一良卒以風聞謝，大不懌。

translations.literal: The emperor wished Yiliang to name specifics and was about to punish and reform; Yiliang in the end pleaded that it was mere hearsay, and the emperor was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted names so he could punish offenders; Yiliang finally pleaded that his charges rested on rumor, and the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 謂大學士劉鴻訓曰：「都御史可輕授耶！」

translations.literal: He said to Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun: "Can the post of Censor-in-Chief be lightly bestowed!"
translations.idiomatic: He told Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun: "Can the post of Censor-in-Chief be handed out so lightly?"

sentences.zh: 叱一良前後矛盾，褫其官。

translations.literal: He rebuked Yiliang for self-contradiction before and after, and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Yiliang's contradictions and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 吳執禦

translations.literal: Wu Zhiyu
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhiyu

sentences.zh: 吳執禦，字朗公，黃巖人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhiyu, styled Langgong, was a native of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhiyu, whose courtesy name was Langgong, came from Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 除濟南推官。

translations.literal: He received appointment as investigating magistrate of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was named investigating magistrate of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 德州建魏忠賢祠，不赴。

translations.literal: When Dezhou built a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, he did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezhou erected a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, he refused to take part.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，征授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen, by imperial summons he received appointment as supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he was called to the capital and made supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 明年請除掣簽法，使人地相配，議格不行。

translations.literal: The next year he requested abolition of the lottery-drawing method, so that men and places might match; the proposal was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to abolish the lottery system for appointments so that officials might be matched to suitable posts; the proposal was blocked.

sentences.zh: 請蠲畿輔加派，示四方停免之期，曉然知息肩有日，不至召亂。

translations.literal: He requested remission of the extra levies in the capital region, showing the four quarters a date when exemptions would cease, so that clearly they would know relief was coming and disorder would not be provoked.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to remit surtaxes in the capital region and announce to the provinces a firm date when extra levies would end, so people would know relief was coming and rebellion might be averted.

sentences.zh: 請罷捐助搜括，毋為貪墨藏奸藪。

translations.literal: He requested abolition of donation drives and exactions, lest they become hiding places where the greedy and corrupt shelter villains.
translations.idiomatic: He urged an end to donation drives and exactions, lest they become havens where the corrupt hide their crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝以沽名市德責之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for trading in reputation and buying virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of currying favor and trading on moral posturing.

sentences.zh: 劾吏部尚書王永光比匪：「用王元雅而封疆誤，聽張道浚賄舉尹同臯而祖制紊。

translations.literal: He impeached Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang as comparable to a bandit: "Employing Wang Yuanya and the frontier was mistaken; listening to Zhang Daojun's bribed recommendation of Yin Tonggao and ancestral regulations were thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Minister Wang Yongguang as no better than a bandit: "You appointed Wang Yuanya and the frontier suffered; you allowed Zhang Daojun to bribe his way into recommending Yin Tonggao and ancestral rules were overturned.

sentences.zh: 國家立法懲貪，而永光誨貪，官邪何日正，寵賂何日清。」

translations.literal: The state establishes laws to punish greed, yet Yongguang teaches greed—when will official depravity be corrected, when will favor and bribes be cleared?"
translations.idiomatic: The state makes laws against corruption, yet Yongguang teaches corruption—when will official vice end and patronage be cleansed?"

sentences.zh: 帝以永光清慎，不納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yongguang was pure and cautious, did not accept his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the memorial, deeming Yongguang scrupulous and prudent.

sentences.zh: 請召黃克纘、劉宗周、鄭鄤，忤旨譙讓。

translations.literal: He requested summons for Huang Kezuan, Liu Zongzhou, and Zheng Man, and for opposing the imperial will was rebuked and reproved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Huang Kezuan, Liu Zongzhou, and Zheng Man be summoned to court; for defying the throne he was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 又言：「往者邊警，袁崇煥、王元雅擁金錢數百萬，士馬數十萬，狼狽失守，而史應聘、王象雲、張星、左應選以一邑抗強敵。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the past when the frontier was alarmed, Yuan Chonghuan and Wang Yuanya held millions in gold and hundreds of thousands of troops, yet in disarray lost their posts; whereas Shi Yingpin, Wang Xiangyun, Zhang Xing, and Zuo Yingxuan with a single district resisted a strong enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "When the frontier was threatened, Yuan Chonghuan and Wang Yuanya commanded millions in funds and tens of thousands of troops yet lost their posts in disgrace, while Shi Yingpin, Wang Xiangyun, Zhang Xing, and Zuo Yingxuan held a single county against a powerful foe.

sentences.zh: 故曰籌邊不在增兵餉，而在擇人。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that planning the frontier lies not in increasing troops and supplies, but in choosing men.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: frontier defense depends not on more troops and funds, but on choosing the right men.

sentences.zh: 請畿輔東北及秦、晉沿邊州縣，選授精敏甲科，賜璽書，畀本地租賦，撫練軍民自禦寇。

translations.literal: He requested that in the northeastern capital region and along the border prefectures and districts of Qin and Jin, keen, sharp jinshi of the top grade be selected and appointed, granted imperial sealed edicts, given local land tax revenues, and allowed to train soldiers and civilians to defend against bandits themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that in the northeast of the capital region and along the Qin and Jin frontiers, outstanding jinshi graduates be appointed with imperial sealed commissions, entrusted with local tax revenues, and empowered to train troops and civilians for self-defense against raiders.

sentences.zh: 邊關文武吏繕修戰守外，責以理財，如先臣王翺、葉盛輩所為。

translations.literal: Beyond repairing defenses for war and guarding, border civil and military officials should be charged with managing finances, as former ministers Wang Hao, Ye Sheng, and their like did.
translations.idiomatic: Besides fortifying defenses, frontier officials should also be charged with fiscal management, as Wang Hao, Ye Sheng, and other predecessors had done.

sentences.zh: 客兵可撤，餉省可數百萬。」

translations.literal: Guest troops may be withdrawn, and supplies saved may amount to several millions."
translations.idiomatic: Mercenary garrisons could be withdrawn, saving millions in military pay."

sentences.zh: 帝時未審執禦所論畿輔、秦、晉也，而曰：「歲賦留本地，則國用何資？」

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet grasped that Zhiyu's proposal concerned the capital region, Qin, and Jin, and said: "If annual levies remain locally, with what will state expenditures be supplied?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet understood that Zhiyu's plan covered the capital region and the Qin and Jin frontiers, and replied: "If annual taxes stay in the locality, how will the state treasury be funded?"

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 又劾首輔周延儒攬權，其姻親陳於泰及幕客李元功等交關為奸利。

translations.literal: He again impeached Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru for monopolizing power; his affinal relative Chen Yutai and retainers such as Li Yuangong engaged in illicit dealings for corrupt profit.
translations.idiomatic: He further impeached Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru for hoarding power, accusing his kinsman Chen Yutai and retainers such as Li Yuangong of corrupt dealings.

sentences.zh: 初，執禦行取入都，延儒遣元功招之，不赴，至是竟劾延儒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhiyu entered the capital on metropolitan examination assignment, Yanru sent Yuangong to recruit him; he did not go, and now at last impeached Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhiyu came to the capital on metropolitan assignment, Yanru had sent Yuangong to recruit him; Zhiyu refused, and now at last denounced Yanru.

sentences.zh: 又陳內外陰陽之說：「九邊、中原、廟堂之上，無非陰氣；

translations.literal: He again set forth a doctrine of yin and yang within and without: "On the nine frontiers, in the central plains, and above in the hall of the temple—nowhere is there not yin qi;
translations.idiomatic: He also advanced a theory of inner and outer imbalance: "On the nine frontiers, in the heartland, and at court—yin forces prevail everywhere;

sentences.zh: 心膂大臣，不皆君子。」

translations.literal: among the backbone ministers, not all are gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: among the emperor's closest ministers, not all are true gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 帝以所稱「陽剛君子」無主名，令指實。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the so-called "yang-gang gentlemen" had no names attached, ordered that specifics be named.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhiyu's "upright yang ministers" were unnamed, the emperor ordered him to name names.

sentences.zh: 執禦乃以前所薦劉宗周三人，及姜曰廣、文震孟、陳仁錫、黃道周、倪元璐、曹於汴、惠世揚、羅喻義、易應昌對。

translations.literal: Zhiyu then answered with the three men he had earlier recommended, Liu Zongzhou and others, and Jiang Yueguang, Wen Zhenmeng, Chen Renxi, Huang Daozhou, Ni Yuanlu, Cao Yubian, Hui Shiyang, Luo Yuyi, and Yi Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu named Liu Zongzhou and two others he had recommended earlier, plus Jiang Yueguang, Wen Zhenmeng, Chen Renxi, Huang Daozhou, Ni Yuanlu, Cao Yubian, Hui Shiyang, Luo Yuyi, and Yi Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 會御史吳彥芳言：「執禦所舉固真君子，他若侍郎李瑾、李邦華、畢懋康、倪思輝、程紹皆忠良當用，通政使章光嶽邪媚當斥。」

translations.literal: At this time Censor Wu Yanfang said: "Those Zhiyu recommends are indeed true gentlemen; others such as Vice Ministers Li Jin, Li Banghua, Bi Maokang, Ni Sihui, and Cheng Shao are all loyal and worthy of employment; Communications Commissioner Zhang Guangyue is fawning and wicked and ought to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Yanfang added: "Zhiyu's nominees are indeed worthy men; but Vice Ministers Li Jin, Li Banghua, Bi Maokang, Ni Sihui, and Cheng Shao are also loyal and should serve, while Communications Commissioner Zhang Guangyue is sycophantic and ought to be removed."

sentences.zh: 帝怒其朋比，執政復從中構之，遂削二人籍，下法司訊。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at their factional collusion; the chief ministers again framed matters from within, and thereupon both men were struck from the registers and sent down to the judicial offices for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged at their collusion; the chief ministers engineered the case from within, and both men were struck from the rolls and handed to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 時御史王績燦方以薦李邦華、劉宗周等下獄，而執禦、彥芳復繼之，舉朝震駭。

translations.literal: At the time Censor Wang Jican had just been imprisoned for recommending Li Banghua, Liu Zongzhou, and others, and Zhiyu and Yanfang followed in succession—the whole court was shaken and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jican was already in prison for recommending Li Banghua and Liu Zongzhou; when Zhiyu and Yanfang followed, the court was stunned.

sentences.zh: 言官為申救，卒坐三人贖徒三年。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials pleaded for rescue; in the end the three men were sentenced to three years' penal servitude commutable by fine.
translations.idiomatic: Censors pleaded for mercy; in the end all three received three years' penal servitude, commutable by ransom.

sentences.zh: 吳彥芳、王績燦

translations.literal: Wu Yanfang and Wang Jican
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yanfang and Wang Jican

sentences.zh: 彥芳，字延祖，歙縣人，為御史。

translations.literal: Yanfang, styled Yanzu, was a native of She County and served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfang, whose courtesy name was Yanzu, came from She County and served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 大淩被圍，疏論孫承宗。

translations.literal: When Daling was besieged, he memorialized discussing Sun Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Daling came under siege, he memorialized on Sun Chengzong's conduct.

sentences.zh: 又駁逆案呂純如辨冤之謬。

translations.literal: He also refuted the error of Lü Chunru's plea of innocence in the rebel-case.
translations.idiomatic: He also rebutted Lü Chunru's attempt to clear his name in the treason case.

sentences.zh: 登州用兵，請設監島中官。

translations.literal: When troops were deployed at Dengzhou, he requested establishment of a supervising eunuch on the island.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dengzhou campaign he asked that a supervising eunuch be posted to the island.

sentences.zh: 至是譴歸。

translations.literal: At this time he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was now dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 績燦，宇偉奏，安福人。

translations.literal: Jican, styled Weizou, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Jican, whose courtesy name was Weizou, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 與給事中鄧英陳奸吏私派之弊，又進賜環、起廢、容諫三說。

translations.literal: Together with Supervising Secretary Deng Ying he set forth the abuses of corrupt officials' private levies, and further advanced three proposals: restoring the jade ring, raising the dismissed, and tolerating remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: With Supervising Secretary Deng Ying he exposed corrupt officials' private exactions, and proposed three reforms: restoring honors to the disgraced, recalling the dismissed, and tolerating frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 薦張鳳翔、李邦華、劉宗周、惠世揚，遂獲罪卒。

translations.literal: He recommended Zhang Fengxiang, Li Banghua, Liu Zongzhou, and Hui Shiyang, and thereupon was punished and died.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Zhang Fengxiang, Li Banghua, Liu Zongzhou, and Hui Shiyang, was punished for it, and died.

sentences.zh: 福王時，復官。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu his post was restored.

sentences.zh: 彥芳、績燦兩人者，皆以天啟五年舉進士。

translations.literal: Yanfang and Jican, the two men, both became jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Both Yanfang and Jican received their jinshi degrees in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 彥芳授莆田知縣，績燦授興化知縣，又皆以治行高等擢崇禎四年御史，並有聲。

translations.literal: Yanfang was appointed magistrate of Putian, Jican magistrate of Xinghua; both again were promoted to censor in the fourth year of Chongzhen for superior administration, and both had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfang became magistrate of Putian and Jican of Xinghua; both were later promoted to censor in the fourth year of Chongzhen for distinguished governance and won renown.

sentences.zh: 其免官也，又皆以薦才不中，與吳執禦同論譴雲。

translations.literal: Their dismissal from office likewise arose from unsuccessful recommendations of talent, together with Wu Zhiyu in the same controversy of censure.
translations.idiomatic: They lost office for the same reason as Wu Zhiyu—recommending talent the throne would not accept—and shared his fate of dismissal.

sentences.zh: 章正宸

translations.literal: Zhang Zhenchen
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenchen

sentences.zh: 章正宸，字羽侯，會稽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhenchen, styled Yuhou, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenchen, whose courtesy name was Yuhou, came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 從學同里劉宗周，有學行。

translations.literal: He studied under his fellow townsman Liu Zongzhou and had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under his fellow townsman Liu Zongzhou and was known for learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士改禮科給事中。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a Hanlin bachelor he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 勸帝法周、孔，黜管、商，崇仁義，賤富強。

translations.literal: He urged the emperor to model himself on the Zhou and Confucius, dismiss Guan [Zhong] and Shang [Yang], exalt benevolence and righteousness, and despise wealth and power.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to follow the Zhou and Confucius, reject Legalist doctrines, exalt benevolence and righteousness, and scorn mere wealth and force.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎王應熊者，溫體仁私人也，廷推閣臣，望輕不得與。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Wang Yingxiong was Wen Tiren's private man; in court recommendation for Grand Secretariat ministers his standing was light and he was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Wang Yingxiong was Wen Tiren's protégé; in the regular Grand Secretariat recommendation his standing was too low to be included.

sentences.zh: 體仁引為助，為營入閣。

translations.literal: Tiren brought him in as aid and schemed his entry into the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren enlisted him as an ally and maneuvered him into the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正宸上言：「應熊強愎自張，何緣特簡。

translations.literal: Zhenchen submitted: "Yingxiong is forcibly obstinate and self-aggrandizing—on what grounds a special selection?
translations.idiomatic: Zhenchen memorialized: "Yingxiong is stubborn and overbearing—why should he receive a special appointment?

sentences.zh: 事因多擾，變以刻成，綜核傷察，宜存渾厚。

translations.literal: Affairs because of many disturbances, change because of harshness completed; comprehensive scrutiny injures investigation—magnanimity ought to be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Too many disturbances breed harsh remedies; excessive scrutiny wounds governance—what is needed is magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 奈何使很傲之人，與贊平明之治哉？」

translations.literal: How can one employ a fiercely arrogant man to assist in clear and enlightened rule!"
translations.idiomatic: How can a proud, truculent man help sustain enlightened rule?"

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下獄拷訊，竟削籍歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry, sent him to prison for interrogation under torture, and in the end struck him from the register and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had him imprisoned and tortured, and finally struck him from the rolls and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，召為戶科給事中，遷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year he was summoned as supervising secretary of the Household Section and promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year he was recalled as supervising secretary of the Household Section and promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 周延儒再相，帝尊禮之特重。

translations.literal: Zhou Yanru became chief minister again, and the emperor honored and treated him with special weight.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yanru returned as chief minister, the emperor honored him with exceptional deference.

sentences.zh: 正宸出其門，與搘拄。

translations.literal: Zhenchen came from his school and supported and propped him up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenchen was his protégé and supported him in turn.

sentences.zh: 歲旦朝會，帝隆師傅禮，進延儒等而揖之曰：「朕以天下聽先生。」

translations.literal: At the New Year court assembly the emperor elevated the ritual due a teacher, advanced Yanru and others and bowed to them, saying: "I entrust the realm to you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year audience the emperor treated Yanru with the ceremony due a teacher, advanced to greet him, and said: "I leave the empire in your hands, sir."

sentences.zh: 正宸曰：「陛下隆禮閣臣，願閣臣積誠以格君心。

translations.literal: Zhenchen said: "Your Majesty elevates ritual toward Grand Secretariat ministers; may the Grand Secretariat ministers accumulate sincerity to move the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenchen replied: "Your Majesty honors the Grand Secretaries; may they repay that honor with sincere devotion to move your heart.

sentences.zh: 毋緣中官，毋修恩怨，毋以寵利居成功，毋以爵祿私親昵。」

translations.literal: Do not rely on eunuchs, do not cultivate private grudges, do not take favor and profit as the basis of achievement, do not use rank and salary to favor intimates."
translations.idiomatic: Do not court eunuchs, nurse private vendettas, treat patronage as achievement, or distribute offices to cronies."

sentences.zh: 語皆風刺延儒。

translations.literal: Every word was satire aimed at Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Every line was a barbed rebuke of Yanru.

sentences.zh: 延儒欲用宣府巡撫江禹緒為宣大總督，正宸持不可，吏部希延儒指，用之。

translations.literal: Yanru wished to appoint Xuanfu grand coordinator Jiang Yuxu as Xuan-Da supreme commander; Zhenchen held that it could not be done, but the Ministry of Personnel, courting Yanru's intent, appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru wanted to make Xuanfu grand coordinator Jiang Yuxu supreme commander of Xuan-Da; Zhenchen objected, but the Ministry of Personnel, eager to please Yanru, appointed Jiang anyway.

sentences.zh: 延儒欲起江陵知縣史調元，正宸止之。

translations.literal: Yanru wished to raise Jiangling magistrate Shi Tiaoyuan; Zhenchen stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru sought to recall Jiangling magistrate Shi Tiaoyuan; Zhenchen blocked it.

sentences.zh: 延儒以罪輔馮銓力得再召，欲假守涿功復銓冠帶，正宸爭之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Yanru, because disgraced Grand Secretary Feng Quan had exerted himself to secure his second summons, wished to use guarding Zhuo as merit to restore Quan's cap and belt; Zhenchen contended against it, and the matter thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru, indebted to disgraced Grand Secretary Feng Quan for helping secure his return to power, tried to use the defense of Zhuo to restore Quan's rank; Zhenchen fought the move and it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 其不肯阿徇如此。

translations.literal: His refusal to fawn and comply was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his refusal to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，會推閣臣，救李日宣，謫戍均州。

translations.literal: Before long, in joint recommendation for Grand Secretariat ministers, he pleaded for Li Rixuan and was banished to garrison duty at Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, during a Grand Secretariat recommendation, he spoke up for Li Rixuan and was banished to military service at Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 語在《日宣傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Rixuan."
translations.idiomatic: The story is told in the Biography of Li Rixuan.

sentences.zh: 福王立，召復正宸故官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Zhenchen was summoned to restore his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu took the throne, Zhenchen was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 正宸痛舉朝無討賊心，上疏曰：「比者河北、山左各結營寨，擒殺偽官，為朝廷效死力。

translations.literal: Zhenchen grieved that the whole court lacked the will to punish the bandits, and submitted a memorial saying: "Recently in Hebei and Shandong each has formed stockades, capturing and killing false officials, exerting death-effort for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Anguished that the court showed no zeal to punish the rebels, Zhenchen memorialized: "Recently in Hebei and Shandong loyalists have raised camps, killed puppet officials, and fought to the death for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 忠義所激，四方響應。

translations.literal: Stirred by loyalty and righteousness, the four quarters respond in echo.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous fervor is stirring echoes across the empire.

sentences.zh: 宜亟檄江北四鎮，分渡河、淮，聯絡諸路，一心齊力，互為聲援。

translations.literal: It is fitting urgently to dispatch orders to the four commands north of the Yangtze, divide in crossing the Yellow and Huai Rivers, link the various routes, with one heart and united strength, mutually supporting as sound and response.
translations.idiomatic: Urge the four northern commands to cross the Yellow and Huai in concert, link all loyal routes, and act as one with mutual support.

sentences.zh: 兩京血脈通，而後塞井陘，絕孟津，據武關以攻隴右。

translations.literal: When the blood-vessels of the two capitals connect, afterward block Jingxing, cut off Mengjin, and hold Wuguan to attack Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two capitals are reconnected, seal Jingxing, cut Mengjin, and hold Wuguan to strike into Longyou.

sentences.zh: 陛下縞素，親率六師，駐蹕淮上，聲靈震動，人切同仇，勇氣將自倍。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in white mourning, personally leading the six armies, halting the imperial progress on the Huai, prestige and spirit shaking—all will keenly share the common foe, and courage will of itself double.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should don mourning garb, lead the six armies in person, and halt on the Huai—your presence would shake the realm, unite every heart in vengeance, and redouble courage.

sentences.zh: 簡車徒，選將帥，繕城塹，進寸則寸，進尺則尺，據險處要，以規中原。

translations.literal: Select chariots and foot soldiers, choose generals and commanders, repair walls and moats—advance an inch and it is an inch, advance a foot and it is a foot; hold strategic passes and key points to plan for the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: Choose troops and commanders, repair walls and moats, advance inch by inch and foot by foot, hold strategic passes, and plan the reconquest of the central plains.

sentences.zh: 天下大矣，渠無人應運而出哉？」

translations.literal: The realm is vast—will there truly be no man who responds to the age and comes forth!"
translations.idiomatic: The empire is vast—surely men will rise to meet the moment!"

sentences.zh: 魏國公徐弘基薦逆案張捷，部議並起用鄒之麟、張孫振、劉光鬥，安遠侯柳祚昌等薦起阮大鋮，正宸並疏諫，不納。

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Xu Hongji recommended rebel-case Zhang Jie; the ministry deliberated and jointly raised Zou Zhilin, Zhang Sunzhen, and Liu Guangdou; Marquis of Anyuan Liu Zuochang and others recommended raising Ruan Dacheng—Zhenchen memorialized against all together, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xu Hongji recommended Zhang Jie of the traitor roll; the ministry moved to restore Zou Zhilin, Zhang Sunzhen, and Liu Guangdou; Marquis Liu Zuochang urged recalling Ruan Dacheng—Zhenchen protested all these appointments, but in vain.

sentences.zh: 改大理丞，正宸請假歸。

translations.literal: Transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, Zhenchen requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After transfer to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, Zhenchen took leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，署舊官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu supervised the state, he held his former office by appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu became regent, Zhenchen resumed his former title.

sentences.zh: 事敗，棄家為僧。

translations.literal: When affairs failed, he abandoned his family and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed, he abandoned his family and took monastic vows.

sentences.zh: 黃紹傑

translations.literal: Huang Shaojie
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shaojie

sentences.zh: 黃紹傑，萬安人。

translations.literal: Huang Shaojie was a native of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shaojie came from Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretarial draftsman.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，因旱求言。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, because of drought the emperor sought remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year, drought prompted the emperor to invite criticism.

sentences.zh: 紹傑疏論大學士溫體仁曰：「漢世災異，策免三公，宰執亦引罪以求罷。

translations.literal: Shaojie memorialized discussing Grand Secretary Wen Tiren: "In Han times when disasters and anomalies occurred, the three dukes were dismissed by imperial rescript; chief ministers also acknowledged guilt to seek dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojie memorialized against Grand Secretary Wen Tiren: "When Han China suffered omens, the three dukes were dismissed by edict and chief ministers confessed fault to offer their resignations.

sentences.zh: 今者久旱，陛下修明政治，納讜言，可謂應天以實矣，而雨澤不降，何哉？

translations.literal: Now there is long drought; Your Majesty has cultivated enlightened government and accepted forthright words—it may be called responding to Heaven with substance—yet rain and favor do not descend; why?
translations.idiomatic: Today drought persists though Your Majesty has reformed government and welcomed counsel—you have answered Heaven in deed—yet rain still withholds its grace. Why?

sentences.zh: 天有所甚怒而不解也。

translations.literal: Heaven has some extreme anger that is not released.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven harbors a wrath that will not be appeased.

sentences.zh: 次輔溫體仁者，秉政數載，上幹天和，無歲不旱暵，無日不風霾，無處不盜賊，無人不愁怨。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Secretary Wen Tiren has held power for several years, offending Heaven's harmony above: no year without drought, no day without wind and dust haze, no place without bandits, no person without worry and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Secretary Wen Tiren has ruled for years, offending Heaven itself: drought every year, dust storms every day, bandits everywhere, misery in every household.

sentences.zh: 秉政既久，窺間益工，中外趨承益巧。

translations.literal: Having held power long, he watches for openings with increasing skill; within and without, those who hurry to comply grow more artful.
translations.idiomatic: Long in power, he has grown adept at exploiting openings; court and country compete in sycophantic ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 一人當用，則曰：『體仁意未遽爾也。』

translations.literal: When one man ought to be employed, they say: "Tiren's intent is not yet suddenly thus."
translations.idiomatic: When a man deserves appointment, officials say: "Tiren is not ready for that yet."

sentences.zh: 一事當行，則曰：『體仁聞恐不樂也。』

translations.literal: When one matter ought to be carried out, they say: "Tiren, on hearing, fears he will not be pleased."
translations.idiomatic: When a policy should proceed, they say: "Tiren would be displeased to hear of it."

sentences.zh: 覆一疏，建一議，又曰：『慮體仁有他屬。』

translations.literal: To reply to one memorial, to establish one proposal, again they say: "Fearing Tiren has another preference.
translations.idiomatic: On every memorial or proposal they add: "We fear Tiren favors someone else.

sentences.zh: 不然，則：『體仁忌諱，毋攖其兇鋒也。』

translations.literal: Otherwise: "Tiren has taboos—do not brush his fierce edge.
translations.idiomatic: Or else: "Tiren is touchy—do not provoke his wrath.

sentences.zh: 凡此召變之尤。

translations.literal: All these are chief among things that summon calamity.
translations.idiomatic: These are the greatest causes of Heaven's anger.

sentences.zh: 願陛下罷體仁以回天意。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to dismiss Tiren to turn back Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss Tiren, I beg, to restore Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 體仁罷而甘霖不降，殺臣以正欺君之罪。」

translations.literal: If Tiren is dismissed and sweet rain still does not descend, kill your servant to rectify the crime of deceiving the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: If you remove Tiren and rain still withholds, execute me for deceiving the throne."

sentences.zh: 帝方眷體仁，貶紹傑一秩。

translations.literal: The emperor was then favoring Tiren and demoted Shaojie one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, still devoted to Tiren, demoted Shaojie one rank.

sentences.zh: 體仁辨，且訐其別有指授。

translations.literal: Tiren argued in defense and moreover impeached that he had separate instructions from others.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren defended himself and accused Shaojie of acting on others' orders.

sentences.zh: 紹傑言：「廷臣言事，指及乘輿，猶荷優容，一字涉體仁，必遭貶黜。

translations.literal: Shaojie said: "Court ministers who speak on affairs, even when their words touch the imperial person, still receive generous forbearance; one word involving Tiren must meet demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojie replied: "Ministers who criticize the throne itself may still be tolerated, yet one word against Tiren brings demotion.

sentences.zh: 誰不自愛，為人指授耶？」

translations.literal: Who does not cherish himself—would he act on another's instructions?"
translations.idiomatic: Who would risk his career merely to carry out someone else's orders?"

sentences.zh: 因列其罪狀：東南不肯設立總督，庇兵部侍郎彭汝楠，致失機宜；

translations.literal: Thereupon he listed his crimes: in the southeast he refused to establish a supreme commander, shielded Vice Minister of War Peng Runan, and caused loss of opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: He then enumerated Tiren's crimes: refusing a southeastern supreme commander, shielding Vice Minister Peng Runan, and losing strategic opportunities;

sentences.zh: 用貪穢胡鐘麟為職方郎，而黜李繼貞；

translations.literal: employed the greedy and corrupt Hu Zhonglin as bureau director of appointments while dismissing Li Jizhen;
translations.idiomatic: appointing the corrupt Hu Zhonglin to the Bureau of Appointments while ousting Li Jizhen;

sentences.zh: 囑尚書閔洪學起私人唐世濟為南京總憲，錮正人瞿式耜等；

translations.literal: instructed Minister Min Hongxue to raise his private man Tang Shiji as Nanjing supreme censor, and imprisoned upright men such as Qu Shisi;
translations.idiomatic: ordering Minister Min Hongxue to install his protégé Tang Shiji as Nanjing censor-in-chief while imprisoning upright men such as Qu Shisi;

sentences.zh: 庇姻婭沈棨為宣撫，私款辱國；

translations.literal: shielded his affinal relative Shen Qi as pacification commissioner, privately treating and humiliating the state;
translations.idiomatic: protecting his kinsman Shen Qi as pacification commissioner despite private dealings that shamed the nation;

sentences.zh: 庇主考丁進，從寬磨勘。

translations.literal: shielded chief examiner Ding Jin, leniently grinding down investigation.
translations.idiomatic: and shielding chief examiner Ding Jin from full investigation.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「臣所仰祝聖明，洞燭體仁奸欺者，其說則有兩端。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "What your servant prays the sage clarity may penetrate—Tiren's treachery and fraud—the explanations have two ends.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "I pray Your Majesty sees through Tiren's deceit by two familiar tactics.

sentences.zh: 下惟朋黨一語，可以箝言官之口，挑善類之禍；

translations.literal: Below, only the word faction can gag the mouths of remonstrance officials and stir calamity upon good men;
translations.idiomatic: Downward, the charge of faction silences censors and brings disaster on the worthy;

sentences.zh: 上惟票擬一語，可以激聖明之怒，蓋僨誤之愆。」

translations.literal: above, only the word draft rescript can stir the sage clarity's anger and cover the fault of willful error."
translations.idiomatic: upward, the charge of mishandling rescripts provokes Your Majesty's wrath and conceals his own blunders."

sentences.zh: 體仁猶辨，且以朋黨為言。

translations.literal: Tiren still argued in defense and moreover spoke in terms of faction.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren defended himself again, again invoking factionalism.

sentences.zh: 紹傑遂言：「體仁受銅商王誠金，體仁長子受巡撫棨及兩淮巡鹽高欽順等金，皆萬計。

translations.literal: Shaojie then said: "Tiren received gold from the copper merchant Wang Cheng; Tiren's eldest son received gold from Grand Coordinator Qi and the two Huai salt-route supervisors Gao Qinshun and others, each in amounts of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojie then charged that Tiren took gold from the copper merchant Wang Cheng; that Tiren's eldest son took gold from Grand Coordinator Qi and Huai salt supervisors Gao Qinshun and others, each in sums of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 體仁用門幹王治，東南之利皆其轉輸。

translations.literal: Tiren employed his gate steward Wang Zhi; the profits of the southeast all passed through his transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren used his gate steward Wang Zhi to channel southeastern profits.

sentences.zh: 體仁私邸兩被盜，失黃金寶玉無算，匿不敢言。」

translations.literal: Tiren's private residence was twice burglarized, losing immeasurable gold, jade, and treasures; he concealed it and dared not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Tiren's private residence was robbed twice of untold gold and jewels, which he concealed and dared not report."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，調為上林苑署丞，遷行人司副。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, transferred him to assistant director of the Imperial Park, and promoted him to vice director of the Messenger Office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, furious, demoted him to assistant director of the Imperial Park, then transferred him to vice director of the Messenger Office.

sentences.zh: 八年，賊犯皇陵，紹傑再劾體仁誤國召寇，再謫應天府檢校。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when bandits violated the imperial tombs, Shaojie again impeached Tiren for misleading the state and summoning bandits, and was again demoted to inspector of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after rebels raided the imperial tombs, Shaojie again accused Tiren of misleading the state and inviting invasion, and was demoted again to inspector of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京吏部郎中，卒。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, where he died.

sentences.zh: 李世祺

translations.literal: Li Shiqi
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiqi

sentences.zh: 先是，七年正月，給事中李世祺論溫體仁及大學士吳宗達，並劾兵部尚書張鳳翼溺職狀。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the first month of the seventh year, Supervising Secretary Li Shiqi discussed Wen Tiren and Grand Secretary Wu Zongda, and jointly impeached Minister of War Zhang Fengyi for dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the first month of the seventh year, Supervising Secretary Li Shiqi attacked Wen Tiren and Grand Secretary Wu Zongda and impeached Minister of War Zhang Fengyi for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫福建按察司檢校。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted him to inspector of the Fujian surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted him to inspector of the Fujian surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 世祺，字壽生，青浦人。

translations.literal: Shiqi, styled Shousheng, was a native of Qingpu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi, whose courtesy name was Shousheng, came from Qingpu.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Tianqi and was appointed messenger.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of Tianqi and was appointed a court messenger.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，擢刑科給事中，陳大計之當定者二：曰兵食之計，民生之計；

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Punishments Section and set forth two great plans that ought to be settled: namely the plan for troops and provisions, and the plan for the people's livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Punishments Section and proposed two fundamental plans: military supply and the people's livelihood;

sentences.zh: 大弊之當厘者三：曰六曹之弊在吏胥，邊吏之弊在欺隱，貪墨之弊在奢靡。

translations.literal: three great abuses that ought to be rectified: namely the abuse in the six ministries lies in clerks and runners, the abuse on the frontier lies in concealment and fraud, and the abuse of corruption lies in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: and three abuses requiring reform: clerical corruption in the six ministries, deception among frontier officials, and extravagance among the greedy.

sentences.zh: 夏旱，禱雨未應，乃進修政之說三：曰恤畿甸，議催科，預儲備。

translations.literal: In summer there was drought; prayers for rain went unanswered, and he thereupon advanced three proposals for repairing government: namely cherishing the capital region, deliberating on tax collection, and preparing stores in advance.
translations.idiomatic: During a summer drought, when rain prayers failed, he proposed three reforms: relief for the capital region, reconsideration of tax collection, and advance provisioning.

sentences.zh: 帝並納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all three.

sentences.zh: 中官出鎮，世祺上言：「祖宗立法，錢谷兵馬，軍民各分事權，防專擅。

translations.literal: When eunuchs went out to command garrisons, Shiqi submitted: "By ancestral legislation, funds, grain, troops, and horses—civil and military each divide duties and powers, guarding against monopolization.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs were sent to command frontier garrisons, Shiqi memorialized: "Ancestral law divided fiscal, military, and civil authority to prevent monopoly.

sentences.zh: 內閣入奉天顏，出司兵食，內廷意旨既得而陰伺之，外廷事權又得而顯操之。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat enters to attend the Heaven-facing countenance and goes out to manage troops and provisions; once inner-court intent is obtained it secretly watches, and outer-court administrative power is again openly wielded.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat attends the throne and controls troops and supplies—inner intentions are enforced in secret while outer authority is wielded openly.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢盜弄神器，則賴聖天子躬翦除之，而奈何復躬自蹈之。」

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian stole and toyed with the divine vessel; then it depended on the sage Son of Heaven personally cutting him down—why tread that path again in person?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian usurped imperial power until the sage emperor destroyed him—why walk that path again?"

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，淫雨損山陵，昌平地動。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year, excessive rain damaged the imperial tombs, and Changping suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year, torrential rains damaged the imperial tombs and Changping was shaken by earthquake.

sentences.zh: 世祺上言：「日者輔理調燮無聞，精神為固寵之用；

translations.literal: Shiqi submitted: "Recently the assistants in harmonizing governance have been unheard of; their spirit is spent on securing favor;
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi memorialized: "The chief ministers offer no harmonizing governance; their energies go only to securing favor;

sentences.zh: 統軍衡才無術，緩急無可恃之人。

translations.literal: in commanding armies and weighing talent there is no method; in urgency and calm there is no man to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: they cannot command armies or judge talent, and no one can be trusted in crisis.

sentences.zh: 中樞決策，掩耳盜鈴；

translations.literal: Central decision-making covers its ears and steals the bell;
translations.idiomatic: Central policy-making is self-deception;

sentences.zh: 主計持籌，醫瘡剜肉。

translations.literal: the chief accountant holds the counting rods, treating sores by gouging flesh.
translations.idiomatic: the finance ministry treats sores by cutting flesh.

sentences.zh: 州縣迫功令，鞭策不前；

translations.literal: Prefectures and districts are pressed by achievement statutes and cannot advance under the whip;
translations.idiomatic: Local officials, crushed by performance quotas, cannot keep pace;

sentences.zh: 六曹窘簿書，救過不贍。

translations.literal: the six ministries are cramped by ledgers and cannot save themselves beyond remedying faults.
translations.idiomatic: the six ministries are buried in paperwork and can only patch errors.

sentences.zh: 簪筆執簡之臣，接跡囹圄；

translations.literal: Men who wear writing brushes and hold bamboo slips follow one another into prison;
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists march one after another into prison;

sentences.zh: 考槃絪軸之士，抗聲鴻舉。

translations.literal: scholars of reclusion and woven axles raise their voices in lofty flight.
translations.idiomatic: while reclusive scholars raise voices in protest.

sentences.zh: 一人議，疑及眾人；

translations.literal: One man's opinion, and suspicion extends to the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: One man speaks, and suspicion falls on all;

sentences.zh: 一事訾，疑及眾事。

translations.literal: one matter criticized, and suspicion extends to all matters.
translations.idiomatic: one fault alleged, and every affair is suspect.

sentences.zh: 黃衣之使，頡頏卿貳之堂；

translations.literal: Yellow-robed envoys strut level with the halls of vice ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch envoys strut equal to vice ministers;

sentences.zh: 貂蟬之座，雄踞節鉞之上。

translations.literal: seats of rank and tassel dominate above military seals and axes.
translations.idiomatic: courtiers in finery lord it over field commanders.

sentences.zh: 低眉則氣折，強項則釁開。

translations.literal: Lower the brow and spirit is broken; stiffen the neck and quarrel opens.
translations.idiomatic: Bow and spirit is crushed; stand firm and conflict erupts.

sentences.zh: 各邊監視之遣，已將期月，初雖間有摘發，至竟同歸模棱，效不效可概見。

translations.literal: The dispatch of supervisors to each frontier has already approached a full month; at first there were occasional exposures, but in the end all alike returned to equivocation—the effect or lack of effect can be seen at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier supervisors have been in place nearly a month; initial exposures faded into equivocation—results are plain to see.

sentences.zh: 伏願撤回各使，以明陰不幹陽之分。

translations.literal: I humbly wish to recall all envoys, to clarify that yin does not interfere with yang.
translations.idiomatic: Recall all these envoys, I beg, to restore the boundary between inner and outer power.

sentences.zh: 然後采公論以進退大臣，酌事情以衡量小臣，釋疑忌之根，開功名之路，庶天變可回，時艱可濟。」

translations.literal: Then gather public opinion to advance and dismiss great ministers, weigh affairs to measure lesser officials, release the root of suspicion and jealousy, open the road of merit and fame—then perhaps heavenly changes may turn back and the hard times be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: Then heed public opinion in appointing ministers, judge lesser officials by their deeds, end suspicion, and reopen the path to merit—only then may omens relent and the crisis be overcome."

sentences.zh: 帝以借端瀆奏，切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that he seized a pretext to insult the throne with a memorial, sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of using omens as a pretext for insolence and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳贊化劾周延儒，謂：「延儒嘗語人曰：今上，羲皇上人也。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Zanhua impeached Zhou Yanru, saying: "Yanru once said to someone: The present sovereign is a man of the age of Fuxi the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Zanhua impeached Zhou Yanru, quoting him as saying: "The present sovereign is a sage of Fuxi's age.

sentences.zh: 此成何語？

translations.literal: What kind of words are these?
translations.idiomatic: What manner of speech is this?

sentences.zh: 臣聞之世祺。」

translations.literal: Your servant heard it from Shiqi."
translations.idiomatic: I heard this from Shiqi."

sentences.zh: 帝詰世祺，則言聞之贊化。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated Shiqi, who said he heard it from Zanhua.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Shiqi, who said he had heard it from Zanhua.

sentences.zh: 帝詰責者再三，世祺執如初，乃已。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated and reproached again and again; Shiqi held to his first account, and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed them repeatedly; Shiqi held firm, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 至是論體仁絕世之奸，大貪之尤，遂貶官。

translations.literal: At this time, discussing Tiren as a traitor unmatched in the age and a chief among great greed, he was thereupon demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When he later denounced Tiren as the age's greatest traitor and greediest minister, Shiqi was demoted.

sentences.zh: 久之，起行人司副，屢遷太仆寺卿。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised as vice director of the Messenger Office and repeatedly promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Studs.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as vice director of the Messenger Office and rose to director of the Court of Imperial Studs.

sentences.zh: 遣祭魯王，事竣旋裏。

translations.literal: Sent to perform sacrifices for the Prince of Lu, when the mission was finished he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After conducting sacrifices for the Prince of Lu, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 國變，杜門不出，久之卒。

translations.literal: When the dynasty fell, he shut his door and did not go out; after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty collapsed, he secluded himself at home until his death.

sentences.zh: 傅朝佑

translations.literal: Fu Chaoyou
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chaoyou

sentences.zh: 傅朝佑，字右君，臨川人。

translations.literal: Fu Chaoyou, styled Youjun, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chaoyou, whose courtesy name was Youjun, came from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 有孝行。

translations.literal: He had filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉鄉試第一，師事鄒元標。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he placed first in the provincial examination and took Zou Yuanbiao as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign he topped the provincial examinations and studied under Zou Yuanbiao.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年成進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he became a jinshi and was appointed secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the second year of Tianqi and was appointed a secretarial draftsman.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，考選給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was selected by examination and appointed supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he passed the selection examination and became a supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 永平初復，列上善後七事。

translations.literal: When Yongping was first recovered, he listed seven matters for good governance afterward.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongping was recovered, he submitted seven proposals for consolidating the victory.

sentences.zh: 帝采納之，補授兵科。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted them and additionally appointed him to the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted them and appointed him to the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，疏劾首輔周延儒：「以機械變詐之心，運刑名督責之術。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year he memorialized impeaching Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru: "With a heart of mechanical shifting fraud, he applies the techniques of penal law and urgent supervision.
translations.idiomatic: The next August he impeached Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru: "With a devious, calculating heart he wields penal law and harsh supervision.

sentences.zh: 見佞則加之膝，結袁弘勛、張道浚為腹心；

translations.literal: Seeing the fawning, he draws them to his knee and binds Yuan Hongxun and Zhang Daojun as his intimate core;
translations.idiomatic: He elevates flatterers like Yuan Hongxun and Zhang Daojun as his inner circle;

sentences.zh: 遇賢則墜之淵，擯錢象坤、劉宗周於草莽。

translations.literal: meeting the worthy, he drops them into the abyss and drives Qian Xiangkun and Liu Zongzhou into the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: and drives the worthy such as Qian Xiangkun and Liu Zongzhou into exile.

sentences.zh: 傾陷正士，加之極刑，曰『上意不測也』；

translations.literal: He overturns and traps upright men, imposing extreme punishments, saying, "The sovereign's intent is unfathomable";
translations.idiomatic: He destroys upright men with extreme penalties, claiming "the sovereign's intent is unfathomable";

sentences.zh: 攘竊明旨，播諸朝右，曰『吾意固然也』。

translations.literal: he seizes and steals the clear imperial intent and broadcasts it to the court, saying, "My intent is surely thus."
translations.idiomatic: he steals imperial directives and spreads them through court, saying, "This is what I intended."

sentences.zh: 皇上因旱求言，則恐其揚己過，故削言官以立威；

translations.literal: When Your Majesty because of drought sought remonstrance, he feared exposure of his faults and therefore cut down remonstrance officials to establish awe;
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty sought counsel during drought, he feared exposure and silenced censors to assert his power;

sentences.zh: 皇上慎密兵機，則欲其箝人口，故挫直臣以怵眾。

translations.literal: when Your Majesty was careful and secretive about military affairs, he wished to gag mouths and therefore crushed straight officials to intimidate the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: when Your Majesty guarded military secrets, he crushed outspoken ministers to intimidate the court.

sentences.zh: 往時糾其罪惡者盡遭斥逐，而親知鄉曲遍列要津。

translations.literal: In former times those who impeached his crimes and wickedness were all driven out, while kin, intimates, and fellow townsmen filled key posts everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Those who denounced him were expelled while his kin and cronies filled every key post.

sentences.zh: 大臣之道固如是乎？」

translations.literal: Is the way of great ministers truly thus?
translations.idiomatic: Is this the conduct of a great minister?

sentences.zh: 忤旨切責。

translations.literal: Opposing the imperial will, he was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him sharply for defying the throne.

sentences.zh: 屢遷工科左給事中，陳當務十二事：一納諫，二恤民，三擇相，四勿以內批用輔臣，五勿使中官司彈劾，六勿令法外加濫刑，七止緹騎，八停內操，九抑武臣驕玩，十廣起廢，十一敕有司修城積粟，十二講聖諭六條。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to left supervising secretary of the Works Section, he set forth twelve pressing affairs: first, accept remonstrance; second, cherish the people; third, choose a chief minister; fourth, do not use inner rescripts to appoint assisting ministers; fifth, do not let eunuchs handle impeachments; sixth, do not impose excessive punishments beyond the law; seventh, stop the Embroidered Uniform Guard; eighth, halt inner-court drilling; ninth, restrain military officials' arrogance and laxity; tenth, broadly raise the dismissed; eleventh, order responsible officials to repair walls and store grain; twelfth, expound the six articles of the sage's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left supervising secretary of the Works Section, he proposed twelve urgent reforms: heed remonstrance, cherish the people, choose a chief minister, cease inner appointments of Grand Secretaries, keep eunuchs from impeaching officials, forbid illegal punishments, abolish the Embroidered Uniform Guard, halt palace drilling, restrain arrogant generals, recall the dismissed, order wall repairs and grain storage, and expound the six articles of imperial instruction.

sentences.zh: 出封益藩，事竣還裏。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to ennoble the Prince of Yi, when the mission was finished he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After an ennoblement mission to the Prince of Yi, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 九年，即家進刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, from home he was advanced to chief supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted from home to chief supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 還朝愆期，為給事中陳啟新所劾，貶秩調外。

translations.literal: Returning to court past the deadline, he was impeached by Supervising Secretary Chen Qixin, demoted in rank, and transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: He returned late to court and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Chen Qixin, demoted, and transferred to an outer post.

sentences.zh: 未行，疏論溫體仁六大罪。

translations.literal: Before departing, he memorialized discussing Wen Tiren's six great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, he memorialized on Wen Tiren's six great crimes.

sentences.zh: 略言：

translations.literal: In summary he said:
translations.idiomatic: In summary:

sentences.zh: 陛下當邊警時，特簡體仁入閣。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty faced frontier alarm, Tiren was specially selected to enter the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty specially chose Tiren for the Grand Secretariat when the frontier was threatened.

sentences.zh: 體仁乃不以道事君，而務刑名。

translations.literal: Tiren did not serve the ruler by the Way, but devoted himself to penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tiren did not serve by moral principle but by penal law.

sentences.zh: 窺陛下意在振作，彼則借以快恩仇；

translations.literal: Peering at Your Majesty's intent set on revival, he borrowed it to satisfy private enmities;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Your Majesty eager for revival, he exploited it to settle private scores;

sentences.zh: 窺陛下治尚精明，彼則托以張威福。

translations.literal: peering at Your Majesty's governance valuing sharpness, he used it to expand authority and blessings.
translations.idiomatic: seeing Your Majesty demand sharp governance, he used it to expand his power.

sentences.zh: 此謂得罪於天子。

translations.literal: This is called offending the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This offends the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽、昌平鐘靈之地，體仁曾無未雨綢繆，兩地失守，陵寢震驚。

translations.literal: Fengyang and Changping are places where the bell of spirit converges; Tiren never made provision before rain, and both places were lost, the imperial tombs shaken in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang and Changping guard the imperial tombs; Tiren made no provision, both fell, and the mausoleums were desecrated.

sentences.zh: 此謂得罪於祖宗。

translations.literal: This is called offending the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: This offends the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 燮理職在三公，體仁為相，日月交蝕，星辰失行，風霾叠見，四方告災，歲比不登，地震河決，城陷井枯，曾莫之懲，則日尋恩怨，圖報睚眥。

translations.literal: Harmonizing governance is the duty of the three dukes; Tiren as chief minister—eclipses of sun and moon, stars out of course, wind and dust haze recurring, the four quarters reporting calamity, years of poor harvest one after another, earthquakes and rivers breaking their banks, cities falling and wells drying—he never punished any of it, but daily pursued private grudges and plotted revenge for trifles.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing the realm is the chancellor's duty; yet under Tiren came eclipses, errant stars, dust storms, famine, earthquakes, broken rivers, fallen cities, and dry wells—he punished none of it but nursed petty vendettas.

sentences.zh: 此謂得罪於天地。

translations.literal: This is called offending Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: This offends Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 強敵內逼，大盜四起，高麗旦暮且陷。

translations.literal: Strong enemies press within, great bandits rise on every side, and Korea will fall morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Strong enemies press inward, rebels rise everywhere, and Korea will fall any day.

sentences.zh: 體仁冒賞冒蔭，中外解體因之。

translations.literal: Tiren falsely claimed rewards and hereditary privilege, and within and without the court dissolved because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren hoarded rewards and hereditary privileges until court and country lost cohesion.

sentences.zh: 此謂得罪於封疆。

translations.literal: This is called offending the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: This offends the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 體仁子見屏於復社諸生，募人糾彈，株連不已。

translations.literal: Tiren's son was ostracized by the Fushe scholars; he recruited men to impeach, and implicated connections without end.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren's son was ostracized by Fushe scholars; Tiren launched endless impeachments in revenge.

sentences.zh: 且七年又議裁減茂才，國家三百年取士之經，一旦壞於體仁之手。

translations.literal: Moreover in the seventh year he again deliberated cutting the quota of cultivated talent—the state's three-hundred-year method of selecting scholars was in one day ruined in Tiren's hands.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he sought to cut examination quotas, destroying three centuries of civil-service tradition.

sentences.zh: 此謂得罪於聖賢。

translations.literal: This is called offending the sages.
translations.idiomatic: This offends the sages.

sentences.zh: 同生天地，誰無本心，體仁自有肺腸，偏欲殘害忠良。

translations.literal: Born together under Heaven and Earth, who lacks a true heart? Tiren has his own entrails and wishes only to destroy the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: All men share a conscience, yet Tiren's heart seeks only to destroy the loyal.

sentences.zh: 只今文武臣僚，幾數百人，駢首囹圄，天良盡喪。

translations.literal: Only now civil and military officials number several hundred persons, heads together in prison, natural conscience entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of civil and military officials now fill the prisons, their conscience destroyed.

sentences.zh: 此謂得罪於心性。

translations.literal: This is called offending human nature.
translations.idiomatic: This offends human nature itself.

sentences.zh: 夫人主之辨奸在明，而人主之去奸在斷。

translations.literal: The ruler's discernment of treachery lies in clarity, and the ruler's removal of treachery lies in decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler discerns treachery through clarity and removes it through decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下大施明斷，速去體仁。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty greatly to apply clear decisiveness and swiftly remove Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to act with clarity and decisiveness and remove Tiren at once.

sentences.zh: 毋以天變為不足畏，毋以人言為不足恤，毋以群小之逢迎為必可任，毋以一己之清明為必可恃。

translations.literal: Do not regard heavenly changes as not worth fearing, do not regard human words as not worth caring for, do not regard the fawning of petty men as surely fit to be entrusted, do not regard one's own clarity as surely reliable.
translations.idiomatic: Do not dismiss omens, ignore counsel, trust flatterers, or rely on your own judgment alone.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，除苛政，庶倒懸可解，太平可致。

translations.literal: Proclaim a great amnesty, abolish harsh government—then perhaps the inverted hanging may be released and great peace attained.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim a general amnesty and end harsh rule, and the people's suffering may end in peace.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，除名，下吏按治。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, struck his name from the register, and sent him down to officials for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck his name from the rolls and handed him to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 逾月，體仁亦罷。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Tiren was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Tiren was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 中官杜勛雅重朝佑，令其上疏請罪，而己從中主之，可復故官，朝佑不應。

translations.literal: Eunuch Du Xun greatly valued Chaoyou and had him submit a memorial requesting guilt, while he himself would support it from within so that his former office could be restored; Chaoyou did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Du Xun, who admired Chaoyou, urged him to plead guilty so Du could restore him from within; Chaoyou refused.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，國事益棘，獲罪者益眾，獄幾滿。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year state affairs grew still more urgent; those who incurred guilt grew ever more numerous, and prisons were nearly full.
translations.idiomatic: By the winter of the eleventh year affairs were desperate, prisoners multiplied, and the jails were nearly full.

sentences.zh: 朝佑乃從獄中上書，請寬恤，語過激。

translations.literal: Chaoyou then from prison submitted a memorial requesting leniency and relief; the language was excessively harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyou submitted from prison a plea for leniency, his language excessively harsh.

sentences.zh: 會有邊警，未報也。

translations.literal: Just then there was frontier alarm, and it was not yet reported.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier alarm intervened before a response came.

sentences.zh: 明年春，責以顛倒賢奸，恣意訕侮，廷杖六十，創重而卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year he was reproached for reversing worthy and wicked, wantonly insulting and reviling; he received sixty blows at court, his wounds were severe, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he was accused of reversing worthy and wicked and insulting the throne; after sixty blows at court he died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 當時臺省競言事，言不中多獲譴。

translations.literal: At that time censors and remonstrance officials competed in speaking on affairs; when words did not hit the mark many received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Censors then competed in memorializing; many who missed the mark were punished.

sentences.zh: 章正宸、莊鰲獻、李汝璨之徒好直諫，朝佑嘗疏稱之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhenchen, Zhuang Aoxian, Li Rucan, and their like were fond of straight remonstrance; Chaoyou once memorialized praising them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenchen, Zhuang Aoxian, and Li Rucan were known for blunt counsel; Chaoyou once praised them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 莊鰲獻、李汝璨

translations.literal: Zhuang Aoxian and Li Rucan
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Aoxian and Li Rucan

sentences.zh: 鰲獻，字任公，晉江人。

translations.literal: Aoxian, styled Rengong, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Aoxian, whose courtesy name was Rengong, came from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年，由庶吉士改兵科給事中，上《太平十二策》，極論東廠之害。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen, from Hanlin bachelor he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Military Section and submitted the "Twelve Policies for Great Peace," vehemently discussing the harms of the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he moved from Hanlin bachelor to supervising secretary of the Military Section and submitted the Twelve Policies for Great Peace, fiercely attacking the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，貶浙江布政司照磨。

translations.literal: Opposing the imperial will, he was demoted to assistant registrar of the Zhejiang provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: For defying the throne he was demoted to assistant registrar in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 汝璨，字用章，南昌人。

translations.literal: Rucan, styled Yongzhang, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Rucan, whose courtesy name was Yongzhang, came from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時為刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he served as supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he served as supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 十年閏月因旱求言，陳回天四要，論財用政事之弊。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the tenth year, because of drought the emperor sought remonstrance; he set forth four essentials for turning back Heaven and discussed abuses in finances and government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year's intercalary month, when drought prompted calls for counsel, he proposed four essentials for restoring Heaven's favor and attacked fiscal and administrative abuses.

sentences.zh: 又言：「八、九年來，幹和召災，始於端揆，積於四海。

translations.literal: He also said: "For eight or nine years, offending harmony has summoned calamity, beginning at the chief ministers and accumulating throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: He argued: "For eight or nine years, disharmony at the top has summoned disaster, beginning with the chief ministers and spreading across the realm.

sentences.zh: 水旱盜賊，頻見疊出，勢將未已，何怪其然。」

translations.literal: Flood, drought, bandits, and thieves appear frequently, layer upon layer; the momentum will not yet cease—why wonder that it is so?"
translations.idiomatic: Floods, droughts, and rebels recur without end; the crisis will only deepen—why be surprised?"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，削籍歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and struck him from the register and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck him from the rolls and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 國變，衰绖北面哀號，作《祈死文》祈死，竟死。

translations.literal: When the dynasty fell, in hemp mourning he faced north and wailed aloud, composed a "Prayer for Death" to pray for death, and in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell, he donned mourning, faced north, and wailed; he wrote a Prayer for Death and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 汝璨、朝佑既死，福王時，復官。

translations.literal: After Rucan and Chaoyou had died, under the Prince of Fu their offices were restored.
