translations.idiomatic: After Rucan and Chaoyou died, their offices were restored under the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 鰲獻事福王，復官，久之卒。

translations.literal: Aoxian served the Prince of Fu, his office was restored, and after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: Aoxian served the Prince of Fu, was restored to office, and died some years later.

sentences.zh: 姜埰，字如農，萊陽人。

translations.literal: Jiang Cai, styled Runong, was a native of Laiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cai, whose courtesy name was Runong, came from Laiyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授密雲知縣，調儀真，遷禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Miyun, transferred to Yizhen, and promoted to chief clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Miyun, was transferred to Yizhen, and rose to chief clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 山陽武舉陳啟新者，崇禎九年詣闕上書，言：「天下三大病。

translations.literal: Chen Qixin of Shanyang, a military licentiate, in the ninth year of Chongzhen went to the capital and submitted a memorial, saying: "The realm has three great diseases.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qixin of Shanyang, a military licentiate, reached the capital in the ninth year of Chongzhen and memorialized: "The empire suffers three great diseases.

sentences.zh: 士子作文，高談孝悌仁義，及服官，恣行奸慝。

translations.literal: Scholars in composing essays loftily discuss filial piety, brotherly duty, benevolence, and righteousness, yet when they take office they wantonly practice wickedness and treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars preach filial piety and righteousness in their essays, yet in office practice wickedness freely.

sentences.zh: 此科目之病也。

translations.literal: This is the disease of the examination system.
translations.idiomatic: This is the disease of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 國初典史授都御史，貢士授布政，秀才授尚書，嘉靖時猶三途並用，今惟一途。

translations.literal: In the founding of the state, record clerks were appointed censors-in-chief, tribute scholars were appointed provincial administrators, and cultivated scholars were appointed ministers; in the Jiajing reign three paths were still used together—today there is only one path.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, record clerks became censors-in-chief and tribute scholars became provincial administrators; even in Jiajing three paths to office coexisted—now only the jinshi path remains.

sentences.zh: 舉貢不得至顯官，一舉進士，橫行放誕。

translations.literal: Recommended tribute scholars cannot reach eminent offices; once one becomes a jinshi, one rampages unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute scholars cannot reach high office, while jinshi graduates swagger without restraint.

sentences.zh: 此資格之病也。

translations.literal: This is the disease of qualification.
translations.idiomatic: This is the disease of rank and qualification.

sentences.zh: 舊制，給事、御史，教官得為之，其後途稍隘，而舉人、推官、知縣猶與其列，今惟以進士選。

translations.literal: By old regulation, supervising secretaries and censors could be drawn from instructors; afterward the path grew somewhat narrow, yet recommended scholars, investigating magistrates, and district magistrates still shared in it—today only jinshi are selected.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly censors and supervising secretaries could be drawn from instructors and local officials; now only jinshi are chosen.

sentences.zh: 彼受任時，先以給事、御史自待，監司、郡守承奉不暇，剝下虐民，恣其所為。

translations.literal: When they receive appointment, they first regard themselves as future supervising secretaries and censors; regional and prefectural officials hurry to wait on them, strip the people below and abuse the people, doing as they please.
translations.idiomatic: New appointees already act like future censors; prefects and magistrates fawn on them while they abuse the people at will.

sentences.zh: 此行取考選之病也。

translations.literal: This is the disease of metropolitan selection and examination appointment.
translations.idiomatic: This is the disease of metropolitan selection and court appointment.

sentences.zh: 請停科目以絀虛文，舉孝廉以崇實行，罷行取考選以除積橫之習，蠲災傷田賦以蘇民困，專拜大將以節制有司便宜行事。」

translations.literal: I request stopping the examination system to restrain empty writing, raising filial and incorrupt men to exalt real conduct, abolishing metropolitan selection and examination appointment to remove accumulated overbearing habits, remitting disaster-field land tax to relieve the people's hardship, and exclusively appointing great generals to exercise discretionary power over responsible officials as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: He urged ending the examinations, promoting filial men of integrity, abolishing metropolitan selection, remitting disaster taxes, and empowering great generals with discretionary authority."

sentences.zh: 捧疏跪正陽門三日，中官取以進。

translations.literal: Holding the memorial he knelt at the Zhengyang Gate for three days; palace eunuchs took it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt at the Zhengyang Gate for three days until eunuchs carried his memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，立擢吏科給事中，歷兵科左給事中。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and immediately promoted him to supervising secretary of the Personnel Section, and he rose through left supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: The delighted emperor made him supervising secretary of the Personnel Section and later left supervising secretary of the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 劉宗周、詹爾選等先後論之。

translations.literal: Liu Zongzhou, Zhan Erxuan, and others discussed him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou, Zhan Erxuan, and others criticized him in turn.

sentences.zh: 歙人楊光先訐其出身賤役，及徇私納賄狀。

translations.literal: Yang Guangxian of She impeached his lowly origin as a menial and his favoritism and acceptance of bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangxian of She impeached his menial origins and taking of bribes.

sentences.zh: 帝悉不究。

translations.literal: The emperor investigated none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor investigated none of these charges.

sentences.zh: 然啟新在事所條奏，率無關大計。

translations.literal: Yet in affairs Qixin's memorials and proposals were generally unrelated to great plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qixin's proposals were generally trivial.

sentences.zh: 御史王聚奎劾其溺職，帝怒，謫聚奎。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Jukui impeached him for dereliction of duty; the emperor was angry and demoted Jukui.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jukui impeached him for neglect of duty; the emperor demoted Jukui instead.

sentences.zh: 以僉都御史李先春議聚奎罰輕，並奪其職。

translations.literal: Because Censor-in-Chief Li Xianchun held that Jukui's punishment was light, his office was also taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Because Censor-in-Chief Li Xianchun deemed Jukui's punishment too light, Li lost his post as well.

sentences.zh: 久之，御史倫之楷劾其請托受賕，還鄉驕橫，始詔行勘。

translations.literal: After a long time, Censor Lun Zhikai impeached his patronage and acceptance of bribes, and returning home he was arrogant and overbearing; only then was an edict issued for investigation on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Censor Lun Zhikai charged him with patronage and bribery and arrogance at home; only then was an investigation ordered.

sentences.zh: 未上而啟新遭母憂，埰因劾其不忠不孝，大奸大詐。

translations.literal: Before it was submitted Qixin encountered mourning for his mother; Cai thereupon impeached him for disloyalty and unfilial conduct, great treachery and great fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Before the report arrived Qixin entered mourning for his mother; Cai impeached him as disloyal, unfilial, and utterly treacherous.

sentences.zh: 遂削啟新籍，下撫按追贓擬罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qixin was struck from the register; the grand coordinator and regional inspector were ordered to pursue recovered goods and determine punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qixin was struck from the rolls and the provincial authorities ordered to recover bribes and fix punishment.

sentences.zh: 啟新竟逃去，不知所之。

translations.literal: Qixin in the end fled; no one knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: Qixin fled and was never found.

sentences.zh: 國變後，為僧以卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change he became a monk and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he became a monk and died.

sentences.zh: 時帝以寇氛未息，民罹鋒鏑，建齋南城。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor, because bandit atmosphere had not ceased and the people suffered spear and arrow, established fasting in the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: Because rebels still threatened the realm and the people suffered war, the emperor ordered fasting rites in the southern city.

sentences.zh: 埰上疏諫，不報。

translations.literal: Cai memorialized in remonstrance; no report was made.
translations.idiomatic: Cai remonstrated; the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 已，陳蕩寇二策，曰明農業，收勇敢。

translations.literal: Thereafter he set forth two strategies for pacifying bandits: namely clarifying agriculture and gathering the brave.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed two strategies against bandits: strengthen agriculture and recruit the brave.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 初，溫體仁及薛國觀排異己及建言者。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wen Tiren and Xue Guanguan drove out those unlike themselves and those who offered remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wen Tiren and Xue Guanguan had purged dissenters and memorialists.

sentences.zh: 周延儒再相，盡反所為，廣引清流，言路亦蜂起論事。

translations.literal: When Zhou Yanru became chief minister again, he entirely reversed what they had done, broadly drew in the clear current, and the remonstrance offices also swarmed forth discussing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yanru returned as chief minister he reversed their policies, promoted upright men, and censors again swarmed with memorials.

sentences.zh: 忌者乃造二十四氣之說，以指朝士二十四人，直達御前。

translations.literal: Those who resented them then fabricated a doctrine of the twenty-four qi, pointing at twenty-four court gentlemen, and it reached directly before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies fabricated a "twenty-four qi" slander naming twenty-four court officials and sent it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝適下詔戒諭百官，責言路尤至。

translations.literal: The emperor happened to issue an edict admonishing and instructing all officials, reproaching the remonstrance offices especially.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict admonishing officials, especially the censors.

sentences.zh: 埰疑帝已入其說，乃上言：「陛下視言官重，故責之嚴。

translations.literal: Cai suspected the emperor had already accepted that talk and submitted: "Your Majesty regards remonstrance officials as weighty, and therefore reproaches them strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor had believed the slander, Cai wrote: "Your Majesty values censors and therefore reproaches them harshly.

sentences.zh: 如聖諭雲『代人規卸，為人出缺』者，臣敢謂無其事。

translations.literal: As for the sage's instruction saying "regulating others' faults and resigning, going out to fill vacancies for others"—your servant dares say there is no such matter.
translations.idiomatic: As for the charge of "filling vacancies for others"—I dare say it does not exist.

sentences.zh: 然陛下何所見而雲？

translations.literal: Yet what has Your Majesty seen to say so?
translations.idiomatic: Yet on what evidence does Your Majesty say so?

sentences.zh: 倘如二十四氣蜚語，此必大奸巨憝，恐言者不利己，而思以中之，激至尊之怒，箝言官之口，人皆喑默，誰與陛下言天下事者？」

translations.literal: If it is like the flying talk of the twenty-four qi, this must be a great traitor and arch villain, fearing remonstrance officials are not favorable to himself and thinking to strike at them, stirring the supreme honor's anger and gagging the mouths of remonstrance officials—everyone silent: who will speak to Your Majesty of the realm's affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: If this refers to the twenty-four qi rumor, some great villain fears censors and seeks to silence them by inflaming Your Majesty's wrath—who then will speak of the realm's affairs?"

sentences.zh: 先是，給事中方士亮論密雲巡撫王繼謨不勝任，保定參政錢天錫因夤緣給事中楊枝起、廖國遴，以屬延儒，及廷推，遂得俞旨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Supervising Secretary Fang Shiliang discussed Miyun grand coordinator Wang Jimo as not equal to the task; Baoding vice minister Qian Tianxi through pull and connections with supervising secretaries Yang Zhiqi and Liao Guolin relied on Yanru, and at court recommendation received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Supervising Secretary Fang Shiliang had judged Miyun grand coordinator Wang Jimo incompetent; Baoding vice minister Qian Tianxi, through Supervising Secretaries Yang Zhiqi and Liao Guolin, curried favor with Yanru and won appointment at court recommendation.

sentences.zh: 適帝有「為人出缺」諭，蓋舉廷臣積習告戒之，非為天錫發也。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor had the admonition about "going out to fill vacancies for others"—it was in general to warn court ministers of accumulated habits, not issued because of Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's warning about "filling vacancies for others" targeted general court corruption, not Tianxi specifically.

sentences.zh: 埰探之未審，謂帝實指其事，倉卒拜疏。

translations.literal: Cai investigated without thoroughness, held that the emperor truly pointed at that affair, and in haste submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, investigating poorly, assumed the edict targeted that case and hastily memorialized.

sentences.zh: 而帝於是時方憂勞天下，默告上帝，戴罪省愆，所頒戒諭，詞旨哀痛，讀者感傷。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor at this time was worrying and laboring for the realm, silently informing God, bearing guilt and examining his faults; the admonition he issued, in wording and intent, was grievous and painful—readers were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor then labored under care for the realm, confessed guilt before Heaven, and issued an admonition of heartbreaking sincerity.

sentences.zh: 埰顧反覆詰難，若深疑於帝者，帝遂大怒，曰：「埰敢詰問詔旨，藐玩特甚。」

translations.literal: Cai, on the contrary, repeatedly interrogated and challenged, as if deeply suspicious of the emperor; the emperor thereupon grew greatly angry and said: "Cai dares interrogate and question the edict's intent—contempt is extreme."
translations.idiomatic: Cai instead challenged the edict as if doubting the emperor himself; the emperor raged: "Cai dares question an imperial edict—this is extreme contempt."

sentences.zh: 立下詔獄考訊。

translations.literal: He was immediately sent to the imperial prison for interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent at once to the imperial prison for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 掌鎮撫梁清宏以獄詞上，帝曰：「埰情罪特重。

translations.literal: Director of the prison Liang Qinghong submitted the case record; the emperor said: "Cai's circumstances and guilt are especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Prison director Liang Qinghong submitted the case; the emperor said: "Cai's guilt is especially grave.

sentences.zh: 且二十四氣之說，類匿名文書，見即當毀，何故累騰奏牘？

translations.literal: Moreover the talk of the twenty-four qi resembles anonymous documents—on seeing them they ought to be destroyed; why repeatedly send up memorials?
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-four qi rumor resembles anonymous libel and should be destroyed—why keep memorializing about it?

sentences.zh: 其速按實以聞。」

translations.literal: Hasten to verify the facts and report."
translations.idiomatic: Verify the facts and report at once."

sentences.zh: 時行人熊開元亦以建言下錦衣衛。

translations.literal: At the time Messenger Xiong Kaiyuan was also sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Messenger Xiong Kaiyuan was also imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝怒兩人甚，密旨下衛帥駱養性，令潛斃之獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry at the two men and by secret edict ordered Prison Commander Luo Yangxing secretly to kill them in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage at both men led to a secret order to Prison Commander Luo Yangxing to kill them quietly in prison.

sentences.zh: 養性懼，以語同官。

translations.literal: Yangxing was afraid and spoke of it to his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing, afraid, confided in his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 同官曰：「不見田爾耕、許顯純事乎？」

translations.literal: His colleagues said: "Have you not seen the affairs of Tian Ergeng and Xu Xianchun?"
translations.idiomatic: They said: "Have you forgotten Tian Ergeng and Xu Xianchun?"

sentences.zh: 養性乃不敢奉命，私以語同鄉給事中廖國遴，國遴以語同官曹良直。

translations.literal: Yangxing then did not dare obey the order and privately told his fellow townsman Supervising Secretary Liao Guolin; Guolin told his colleague Cao Liangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing refused, telling fellow townsman Supervising Secretary Liao Guolin, who told colleague Cao Liangzhi.

sentences.zh: 良直即疏劾養性「歸過於君，而自以為功。

translations.literal: Liangzhi immediately memorialized impeaching Yangxing for "shifting blame onto the ruler while taking credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhi immediately impeached Yangxing for shifting blame onto the ruler while claiming credit.

sentences.zh: 陛下無此旨，不宜誣謗；

translations.literal: Your Majesty had no such edict—it is not fitting to slander;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty issued no such order, this is slander;

sentences.zh: 即有之，不宜泄。」

translations.literal: if there was such an order, it is not fitting to leak it."
translations.idiomatic: if there was, it should not have been leaked."

sentences.zh: 請並誅養性、開元。

translations.literal: He requested that Yangxing and Kaiyuan be executed together.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Yangxing and Kaiyuan both be executed.

sentences.zh: 養性大懼，帝亦不欲殺諫臣，疏竟留中。

translations.literal: Yangxing was greatly afraid; the emperor also did not wish to kill remonstrance officials, and the memorial in the end was retained in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing was terrified; the emperor did not wish to kill censors, and the memorial was withheld.

sentences.zh: 會鎮撫再上埰獄，言掠訊者再，供無異詞。

translations.literal: Just then the prison director again submitted Cai's case, saying those who interrogated under torture did so again; the testimony had no differing words.
translations.idiomatic: When the prison director resubmitted Cai's case, repeated torture had produced no change in testimony.

sentences.zh: 養性亦封還密旨。

translations.literal: Yangxing also returned the sealed secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing returned the sealed secret edict unopened.

sentences.zh: 乃命移刑官定罪，尚書徐石麒等擬埰戍，開元贖徒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered transfer to the penal officials to fix punishment; Minister Xu Shiji and others proposed Cai for garrison duty and Kaiyuan for penal servitude commutable by fine.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Ministry of Justice; Minister Xu Shiji proposed garrison duty for Cai and penal servitude for Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝責以徇情骫法，令對狀。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached them for favoring sentiment and distorting law, and ordered confrontation at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused them of bending the law and ordered a court confrontation.

sentences.zh: 乃奪石麒及郎中劉沂春官，而逮埰、開元至午門，並杖一百。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took away the offices of Shiji and Director Liu Yichun, and summoned Cai and Kaiyuan to the Meridian Gate, jointly giving them one hundred blows.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Xu Shiji and Director Liu Yichun of office and had Cai and Kaiyuan flogged one hundred strokes at the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 埰已死，埰弟垓口溺灌之，乃復蘇，仍系刑部獄。

translations.literal: Cai had already died; Cai's younger brother Gai poured water into his mouth and irrigated him, and he revived; he was still held in the Ministry of Justice prison.
translations.idiomatic: Cai seemed dead; his brother Gai poured water into his mouth and revived him; he remained in prison.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，大疫，命諸囚出外收保。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the following year a great epidemic raged; he ordered all prisoners to go outside for bail.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn a plague broke out and prisoners were released on bail.

sentences.zh: 埰、開元出，即謁謝賓客。

translations.literal: Cai and Kaiyuan went out and immediately paid calls to thank guests.
translations.idiomatic: Cai and Kaiyuan went out and immediately visited supporters to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝以語刑部尚書張忻，忻懼，復禁之獄。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke of it to Minister of Justice Zhang Xin; Xin was afraid and imprisoned them again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Minister Zhang Xin, who, afraid, returned them to prison.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月始釋埰，戍宣州衛。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year Cai was at last released and sent to garrison Xuanzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year Cai was released to garrison Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 將赴戍所而都城陷。

translations.literal: He was about to go to the garrison post when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: He was marching to his post when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王立，遇赦，起故官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he met an amnesty and was raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu took the throne, an amnesty restored his former office.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，不赴。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his father and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his father and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 國變後，流寓蘇州以卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change he wandered in Suzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall he lived in exile in Suzhou until his death.

sentences.zh: 且死，語其二子曰：「吾奉先帝命戍宣州，死必葬我敬亭之麓。」

translations.literal: Near death he told his two sons: "I received the late emperor's order to garrison Xuanzhou; when I die you must bury me on the slope of Jingting."
translations.idiomatic: Near death he told his sons: "The late emperor ordered me to Xuanzhou; bury me on Jingting Mountain."

sentences.zh: 二子如其言。

translations.literal: The two sons did as he said.
translations.idiomatic: His sons obeyed.

sentences.zh: 弟 垓

translations.literal: Younger brother Gai
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Gai

sentences.zh: 垓，字如須，崇禎十三年進士。

translations.literal: Gai, styled Ruxu, became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Gai, whose courtesy name was Ruxu, became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed messenger.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a court messenger.

sentences.zh: 埰下獄，垓盡力營護。

translations.literal: When Cai entered prison, Gai exhausted his strength in caring for and protecting him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was imprisoned, Gai did everything to protect him.

sentences.zh: 後聞鄉邑破，父殉難，一門死者二十余人。

translations.literal: Later he heard the home district was broken and his father died for the dynasty; one household had more than twenty dead.
translations.idiomatic: He later learned their home had fallen, their father had died for the dynasty, and more than twenty kin perished.

sentences.zh: 垓請代兄系獄，釋埰歸葬，不許。

translations.literal: Gai requested to replace his elder brother in prison and release Cai to return and bury; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gai asked to take his brother's place in prison so Cai could bury their father; permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 即日奔喪，奉母南走蘇州。

translations.literal: That same day he rushed to mourn, taking his mother south to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed home to mourn and fled south with his mother to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，垓為行人，見署中題名碑，崔呈秀、阮大鋮與魏大中並列，立拜疏請去二人名。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gai was a messenger, he saw on the inscription tablet in the office Cui Chengxiu and Ruan Dacheng listed together with Wei Dazhong; he immediately submitted a memorial requesting removal of the two men's names.
translations.idiomatic: As a messenger he had seen Cui Chengxiu and Ruan Dacheng listed beside Wei Dazhong on the office memorial tablet and memorialized to remove their names.

sentences.zh: 及大鋮得誌，滋欲殺垓甚。

translations.literal: When Dacheng attained his ambition, he all the more wished to kill Gai.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan Dacheng rose to power, he sought Gai's life all the more.

sentences.zh: 垓乃變姓名，逃之寧波。

translations.literal: Gai then changed his name and fled to Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Gai changed his name and fled to Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 國亡乃解。

translations.literal: Only when the state perished was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the dynasty fell was he safe.

sentences.zh: 熊開元

translations.literal: Xiong Kaiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Kaiyuan

sentences.zh: 熊開元，字魚山，嘉魚人。

translations.literal: Xiong Kaiyuan, styled Yushan, was a native of Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Kaiyuan, whose courtesy name was Yushan, came from Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 除崇明知縣，調繁吳江。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Chongming and transferred to the busy post of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was magistrate of Chongming, then transferred to the demanding post of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，征授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was summoned as supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官王應期等監視關、寧軍馬，開元抗疏爭，不納。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched eunuch Wang Yingqi and others to supervise Shanhai and Ningyuan troops and horses; Kaiyuan submitted a defiant memorial protesting and it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent eunuch Wang Yingqi to supervise Shanhai and Ningyuan forces, Kaiyuan protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 王化貞久系不決，奸人張應時等疏頌其功，請以身代死，俾戴罪立功。

translations.literal: Wang Huazhen had long been imprisoned without decision; villain Zhang Yingshi and others memorialized praising his merit and requested to die in his place, enabling him to wear guilt and establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huazhen had long languished in prison; villain Zhang Yingshi memorialized praising his merits and offering to die in his stead so Wang could redeem himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 開元疏駁之，言：「化貞家貲鉅萬，每會朝審，輒買燕市少年，雜立道旁，投熊廷弼瓦礫，嗟嘆化貞不休，以此熒惑上聽。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan memorialized in rebuttal, saying: "Huazhen's household wealth amounts to tens of thousands; each time there was court trial, he would buy youths of the Yan market, mix-standing by the road, throw tiles and stones at Xiong Tingbi, sighing and praising Huazhen without cease, thereby dazzling and confusing what the sovereign heard.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan rebutted: "Huazhen's wealth runs to tens of thousands; at every trial he hired market youths to pelt Xiong Tingbi with stones while praising Huazhen endlessly, deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 今應時復敢為此請，宜立肆化上貞市朝。」

translations.literal: Now Yingshi again dares make this request—it is fitting to set up the exposure of Huazhen in the court market."
translations.idiomatic: Now Yingshi dares repeat this plea—Huazhen should be executed and exposed in the public market."

sentences.zh: 化貞卒正法。

translations.literal: Huazhen in the end was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhen was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 時有令，有司征賦不及額者不得考選。

translations.literal: At the time there was an order that responsible officials who did not reach the levy quota could not undergo examination and selection.
translations.idiomatic: An order then barred officials who missed tax quotas from court selection.

sentences.zh: 給事中周瑞豹考選而後完賦，帝怒，貶謫之，命如瑞豹者悉以聞。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhou Ruibao underwent examination and selection and only afterward completed levies; the emperor was angry, demoted and banished him, and ordered that all like Ruibao be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhou Ruibao passed selection before finishing levies; the emperor demoted him and ordered similar cases reported.

sentences.zh: 於是開元及御史鄭友元等三人並貶二秩調外，開元不赴官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kaiyuan and Censor Zheng Youyuan and three others were all demoted two ranks and transferred outside; Kaiyuan did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan, Censor Zheng Youyuan, and two others were demoted two ranks and transferred; Kaiyuan refused the post.

sentences.zh: 久之，起山西按察司照磨，遷光祿寺監事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised as assistant registrar of the Shanxi surveillance commission and promoted to supervisor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as assistant registrar in Shanxi and promoted to supervisor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷行人司副。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to vice director of the Messenger Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became vice director of the Messenger Office.

sentences.zh: 左降官率驟遷，開元以淹久頗觖望。

translations.literal: Demoted officials were generally promoted in haste; Kaiyuan, because his stay was long, was rather discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted officials were usually promoted quickly; Kaiyuan, long in limbo, grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 會光祿丞缺，開元詣首輔周延儒述己困頓狀。

translations.literal: When a vacancy opened for vice director of Imperial Sacrifices, Kaiyuan went to Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru and set forth his distressed condition.
translations.idiomatic: When a vice directorship opened, Kaiyuan appealed to Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru about his hardships.

sentences.zh: 延儒適以他事輒命駕出，開元大慍。

translations.literal: Yanru happened on another matter to order his carriage out at once; Kaiyuan was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru abruptly left on other business; Kaiyuan was furious.

sentences.zh: 會帝以畿輔被兵求言，官民陳事者，報名會極門，即日召對。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor, because the capital region suffered military attack, sought remonstrance; officials and commoners who presented affairs registered their names at the Jiji Gate and were summoned to audience that same day.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region came under attack, the emperor invited memorials; petitioners registered at the Jiji Gate for same-day audience.

sentences.zh: 開元欲論延儒，次日即請見。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan wished to discuss Yanru's crimes and the next day requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan planned to denounce Yanru and requested an audience the next day.

sentences.zh: 帝召入文昭閣，開元請密論軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him into the Wenzhao Pavilion; Kaiyuan requested confidential discussion of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to the Wenzhao Pavilion; Kaiyuan asked to discuss military affairs in private.

sentences.zh: 帝屏左右，獨輔臣在，開元不敢言，但奏軍事而出。

translations.literal: The emperor screened off those at his side; only the assisting ministers remained; Kaiyuan did not dare speak, but memorialized on military affairs and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed attendants, leaving only the Grand Secretaries; Kaiyuan dared not speak and reported only on military matters.

sentences.zh: 越十余日，復請見。

translations.literal: After more than ten days he again requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he requested audience again.

sentences.zh: 帝御德政殿，秉燭坐，開元從輔臣入，奏言：「《易》稱『君不密則失臣，臣不密則失身』，請輔臣暫退。」

translations.literal: The emperor held court at the Dezheng Hall, sat holding a candle, and Kaiyuan entered with the assisting ministers, memorializing: "The Changes says, 'If the ruler is not secret he loses his ministers; if ministers are not secret they lose themselves'—I request the assisting ministers temporarily withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: At the Dezheng Hall, candle in hand, Kaiyuan entered with the Grand Secretaries and said: "The Changes warns that rulers and ministers who lack secrecy lose one another—I beg the Grand Secretaries to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 延儒等引退者再，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yanru and others withdrew twice; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru and the others withdrew twice; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 開元遂言：「陛下求治十五年，天下日以亂，必有其故。」

translations.literal: Kaiyuan then said: "Your Majesty has sought good government for fifteen years, yet the realm grows more chaotic daily—there must be a reason."
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan continued: "Your Majesty has sought order for fifteen years, yet chaos deepens daily—there must be a cause."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「其故安在？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Where lies the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "What cause?"

sentences.zh: 開元言：「今所謀畫，惟兵食寇賊。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan said: "What is now planned concerns only troops, provisions, and bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan replied: "Today's planning fixes only on troops, grain, and rebels.

sentences.zh: 不揣其本，而末是圖，雖終日夜不寢食，求天下治無益也。

translations.literal: Without gauging the root but taking the branches as the plan, even if one toils day and night without sleep or food, seeking order in the realm is of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Ignore the root and chase the branches, and even sleepless toil will never bring order.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦以來，輔臣至數十人，不過陛下曰賢，左右曰賢而已，未必諸大夫國人皆曰賢也。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, assisting ministers have numbered several tens of men—it is no more than Your Majesty saying worthy and those at your side saying worthy; it is not certain that all grandees and the people of the state say worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, dozens of chief ministers have served—yet worthiness is declared only by you and your intimates, not by the court and country.

sentences.zh: 天子心膂股肱，而任之易如此。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's heart, backbone, thighs, and arms—and to entrust them so easily as this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's closest ministers are entrusted far too lightly.

sentences.zh: 庸人在高位，相繼為奸，人禍天殃，迄無衰止。

translations.literal: Mediocrities in high position succeed one another in wickedness; human calamity and Heaven's punishment reach to no decline or stop.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocrities in high office breed one another's corruption; human and heavenly disasters never cease.

sentences.zh: 迨言官發其罪狀，誅之斥之，已敗壞不可復救矣。」

translations.literal: Only when remonstrance officials expose their crimes and punishments, killing or driving them out, is the damage already beyond saving."
translations.idiomatic: Only when censors expose and punish them is the damage already beyond repair."

sentences.zh: 帝與詰問久之，疑開元有所為，曰：「爾意有人欲用乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated him at length, suspecting Kaiyuan had some design, and said: "Do you mean someone wishes to be employed?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him at length, suspecting a plot: "Does someone wish to be appointed?"

sentences.zh: 開元辨無有，且奏且頻目延儒。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan denied there was any such thing, and as he memorialized he repeatedly glanced at Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan denied it, glancing repeatedly at Yanru as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 延儒謝，帝曰：「天下不治皆朕過，於卿等何與？」

translations.literal: Yanru apologized; the emperor said: "That the realm is not governed is all my fault—what has it to do with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanru apologized; the emperor said: "If the realm is disorderly, the fault is mine alone—what have you done wrong?"

sentences.zh: 開元言：「陛下令大小臣工不時面奏，而輔臣在左右，誰敢為異同之論以速禍？

translations.literal: Kaiyuan said: "Your Majesty orders great and small officials not to face and memorialize at irregular times, while assisting ministers are at your side—who dares offer differing views to hasten calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan said: "Your Majesty bars irregular audiences while the Grand Secretaries stand at your side—who dares dissent and invite ruin?

sentences.zh: 且昔日輔臣，繁刑厚斂，屏棄忠良，賢人君子攻之。

translations.literal: Moreover in former days assisting ministers used harsh punishments and heavy exactions, casting out the loyal and good, and worthy men and gentlemen attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Former ministers imposed harsh law and heavy taxes and drove out the loyal—worthy men attacked them for it.

sentences.zh: 今輔臣奉行德意，釋累囚，蠲逋賦，起廢籍，賢人君子皆其所引用。

translations.literal: Today's assisting ministers carry out virtuous intent, releasing accumulated prisoners, remitting overdue levies, raising the dismissed from the registers—worthy men and gentlemen are all those they employ.
translations.idiomatic: Today's ministers follow your humane intent, freeing prisoners, remitting taxes, restoring the dismissed—worthy men they promote.

sentences.zh: 偶有不平，私慨嘆而已。」

translations.literal: If there is occasional unfairness, it is only private sighing."
translations.idiomatic: Any remaining grievance is only private sighing."

sentences.zh: 帝責開元有私。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Kaiyuan for partiality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused Kaiyuan of bias.

sentences.zh: 開元辨，延儒等亦前為解。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan argued; Yanru and others also stepped forward to explain.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan protested; Yanru and the others defended themselves.

sentences.zh: 開元復請遍召廷臣，問以輔臣賢否。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan again requested summoning all court ministers and asking whether the assisting ministers were worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan again asked that all ministers be summoned to judge the Grand Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 「輔臣心事明，諸臣流品亦別。

translations.literal: "The assisting ministers' hearts are clear, and the ministers' ranks are also distinct.
translations.idiomatic: "The Grand Secretaries' intentions are clear and officials' ranks are distinct.

sentences.zh: 陛下若不察，將吏狃情面賄賂，失地喪師，皆得無罪，誰復為陛下捐軀報國者？」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not investigate, generals and officials will cling to personal ties and bribes, lose territory and armies yet all go unpunished—who again will for Your Majesty give body and report to the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Without scrutiny, commanders will cling to patronage and bribes, lose territory yet escape punishment—who will die for Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 延儒等奏情面不盡無，賄賂則無有。

translations.literal: Yanru and others memorialized that personal ties were not entirely absent, but bribes there were none.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru replied that patronage existed but not bribery.

sentences.zh: 開元復言：「敵兵入口四十余日，未聞逮治一督、撫。」

translations.literal: Kaiyuan again said: "The enemy army has entered the gate for more than forty days, yet not a single grand coordinator or governor has been seized and punished."
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan added: "The enemy has been within the passes forty days, yet no commander has been punished."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「督、撫初推，人以為賢，數月後即以為不賢，必欲去之而後快。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Grand coordinators and governors at first recommendation people think worthy; after several months they are thought unworthy—one must remove them before being satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Commanders seem worthy at appointment and unworthy months later—critics demand removal before they are satisfied.

sentences.zh: 邊方與內地不同，使人何以展布。」

translations.literal: The frontier differs from the interior—how can one deploy others?"
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is not the interior—how can men function under such pressure?"

sentences.zh: 開元言：「四方督、撫，率自監司。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan said: "Grand coordinators and governors on the four sides are all drawn from surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan said: "Frontier commanders all rise from surveillance posts.

sentences.zh: 明日廷推，今日傳單，其人姓名不列。

translations.literal: Tomorrow is court recommendation; today the nomination slip circulates, yet the man's name is not listed.
translations.idiomatic: Court recommendation comes tomorrow, yet today's slip omits the nominee's name.

sentences.zh: 至期，吏部出諸袖，諸臣唯唯而已。

translations.literal: When the day arrives, the Ministry of Personnel produces names from its sleeve and the ministers only assent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day, the Ministry of Personnel produces names from its sleeve and ministers merely assent.

sentences.zh: 既推後，言官轉相采訪，而其人伎倆亦自露於數月間，故人得而指之。

translations.literal: After recommendation, remonstrance officials in turn investigate, and the man's tricks also expose themselves within several months—hence people can point at him.
translations.idiomatic: After appointment, censors investigate and incompetence shows within months—hence the later denunciations.

sentences.zh: 非初以為賢，繼以為不賢也。」

translations.literal: It is not that at first he was thought worthy and afterward unworthy."
translations.idiomatic: It is not that they were worthy at first and unworthy later."

sentences.zh: 帝命之退。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 延儒等請令補牘，從之。

translations.literal: Yanru and others requested that he be allowed to submit a supplemental memorial; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru asked that Kaiyuan submit a written supplement; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，開元欲發延儒罪，以其在側不敢言。

translations.literal: At this time Kaiyuan wished to expose Yanru's crimes, but because Yanru was at his side he did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan had meant to expose Yanru but dared not while Yanru stood beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 而延儒慮其補牘，謀沮之。

translations.literal: Yanru feared his supplemental memorial and plotted to obstruct it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru feared the supplemental memorial and plotted to block it.

sentences.zh: 大理卿孫晉、兵部侍郎馮元飆責開元：「首輔多引賢者。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Justice Sun Jin and Vice Minister of War Feng Yuankuang reproached Kaiyuan: "The chief minister has drawn in many worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of Justice Sun Jin and Vice Minister Feng Yuankuang warned Kaiyuan: "The chief minister has promoted many worthy men.

sentences.zh: 首輔退，賢者且盡逐。」

translations.literal: If the chief minister falls, the worthy will all be driven out.
translations.idiomatic: If he falls, the worthy will be swept out with him.

sentences.zh: 開元意動。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan's mind was moved.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan wavered.

sentences.zh: 大理丞吳履中至，亦以開元言為驟。

translations.literal: When Vice Director of Justice Wu Lüzhong arrived, he also held Kaiyuan's words to be rash.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wu Lüzhong likewise called Kaiyuan rash.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中吳昌時者，開元知吳江時所拔士也，復致書言之。

translations.literal: Director Wu Changshi of the Ministry of Rites was a man Kaiyuan had raised when he knew Wujiang; he also sent a letter speaking of it.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Director Wu Changshi, whom Kaiyuan had promoted at Wujiang, also wrote urging restraint.

sentences.zh: 開元乃止述奏辭，不更及延儒他事。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan then stopped setting forth the memorial's wording and no longer touched Yanru's other affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan then softened his memorial and omitted further charges against Yanru.

sentences.zh: 帝方信延儒，大清兵又未退，焦勞甚。

translations.literal: The emperor was then trusting Yanru; the Qing army had not yet withdrawn, and he was greatly vexed and toiling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still trusted Yanru; the Qing army had not withdrawn, and he was exhausted with care.

sentences.zh: 得奏，大怒，令錦衣衛逮治。

translations.literal: Receiving the memorial, he was greatly angry and ordered the Embroidered Uniform Guard to arrest and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, he ordered the Embroidered Uniform Guard to arrest Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 衛帥駱養性，開元鄉人也，雅怨延儒，次日即以獄上。

translations.literal: Prison Commander Luo Yangxing was Kaiyuan's fellow townsman and had long resented Yanru; the next day he submitted the prison case.
translations.idiomatic: Prison Commander Luo Yangxing, Kaiyuan's fellow townsman and Yanru's enemy, reported the case next day.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，曰：「開元讒譖輔弼，必使朕孤立於上，乃便彼行私，必有主使者。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and said: "Kaiyuan slanders and calumniates the assisting ministers, surely wishing to leave me isolated above so that he may practice private designs—there must be an instigator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Kaiyuan slanders the chief minister to isolate me and serve some private plot—someone put him up to this.

sentences.zh: 養性不加刑，溺職甚，其再嚴訊以聞。」

translations.literal: Yangxing did not apply torture—dereliction of duty is extreme; interrogate again severely and report."
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Yangxing for failing to torture Kaiyuan and ordered harsher interrogation."

sentences.zh: 十二月朔，嚴刑詰供主謀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, under severe torture he was interrogated for the chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, torture sought the mastermind.

sentences.zh: 開元堅不承，而盡發延儒之隱，養性具以聞。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan firmly would not confess, but fully exposed Yanru's secrets; Yangxing reported everything.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan confessed no mastermind but exposed Yanru's secrets in full; Yangxing reported all.

sentences.zh: 帝乃廷杖開元，系獄。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon had Kaiyuan beaten at court and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Kaiyuan flogged at court and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 始，方士亮劾罷密雲巡撫王繼謨，參政錢天錫得巡撫。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fang Shiliang impeached and removed Miyun grand coordinator Wang Jimo, and Vice Minister Qian Tianxi obtained the grand coordinationship.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fang Shiliang had removed Miyun grand coordinator Wang Jimo, and Vice Minister Qian Tianxi won the post.

sentences.zh: 御史孫鳳毛發其事，劾給事中楊枝起、廖國遴為天錫夤緣，因言開元面奏，實二人主之，欲令邱瑜秉政，陳演為首輔。

translations.literal: Censor Sun Maofa exposed the affair, impeaching Supervising Secretaries Yang Zhiqi and Liao Guolin for pulling strings for Tianxi, and further saying Kaiyuan's face memorial was really directed by the two men, wishing to make Qiu Yu hold power and Chen Yan chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Sun Maofa exposed the affair, impeaching Yang Zhiqi and Liao Guolin for securing Tianxi's appointment and claiming Kaiyuan's audience was their plot to install Qiu Yu and Chen Yan.

sentences.zh: 御史李陳玉亦言之。

translations.literal: Censor Li Chenyu also spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Chenyu said the same.

sentences.zh: 帝以開元已下吏，不問，而責令鳳毛陳奏。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Kaiyuan had already been sent to officials, did not inquire, but ordered Maofa to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, Kaiyuan already imprisoned, ordered Maofa to submit particulars.

sentences.zh: 鳳毛死，其子訴冤，謂國遴、枝起鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Maofa died; his son pleaded injustice, saying Guolin and Zhiqi had poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Maofa died, his son claimed Guolin and Zhiqi had poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 兩人及天錫並削職下獄。

translations.literal: The two men and Tianxi were all struck from office and sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Both supervising secretaries and Tianxi were stripped of office and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 士亮又言恐代繼謨者未能勝繼謨，繼謨得留任。

translations.literal: Shiliang also said he feared the replacement for Jimo could not surpass Jimo, and Jimo was allowed to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang argued the replacement might not equal Jimo, and Jimo kept his post.

sentences.zh: 十六年六月，延儒罷，言官多救開元者，不報。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixteenth year Yanru was dismissed; remonstrance officials mostly pleaded for Kaiyuan, but no report was made.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixteenth year Yanru fell; censors pleaded for Kaiyuan in vain.

sentences.zh: 刑部擬贖徒，不許。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice proposed penal servitude commutable by fine; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice proposed commutable penal servitude; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，遣戍杭州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he was sent to garrison Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month he was banished to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，京師陷，福王召起吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Before long the capital fell; the Prince of Fu summoned and raised him to supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the capital fell; the Prince of Fu recalled him as supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 丁母艱，不赴。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 唐王立，起工科左給事中。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang was enthroned, he was raised to left supervising secretary of the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Tang he became left supervising secretary of the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 連擢太常卿、左僉都御史，隨征東閣大學士。

translations.literal: In succession he was promoted to Minister of Rites, left censor-in-chief, and followed the eastern expedition as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Rites, left censor-in-chief, and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion on the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 乞假歸。

translations.literal: He requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 汀州破，棄家為僧，隱蘇州之靈巖以終。

translations.literal: When Tingzhou fell, he abandoned his family and became a monk, hiding at Lingyan in Suzhou until the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhou fell he became a monk and lived in seclusion at Lingyan in Suzhou until his death.

sentences.zh: 方士亮

translations.literal: Fang Shiliang
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shiliang

sentences.zh: 士亮，歙縣人。

translations.literal: Shiliang was a native of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang came from She County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 歷嘉興、福州推官，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He served as investigating magistrate of Jiaxing and Fuzhou and was promoted to supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating magistrate at Jiaxing and Fuzhou, then became supervising secretary of the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 與同官朱徽、倪仁禎等謁大學士謝升於朝房，升言：「人主以不用聰明為高。

translations.literal: Together with colleagues Zhu Hui, Ni Renzhen, and others he called on Grand Secretary Xie Sheng in the morning chamber; Sheng said: "The ruler takes not using cleverness as loftiness.
translations.idiomatic: With colleagues Zhu Hui and Ni Renzhen he visited Grand Secretary Xie Sheng, who said: "A ruler is lofty when he does not rely on cleverness.

sentences.zh: 今上太用聰明，致天下盡壞。」

translations.literal: The present sovereign uses cleverness too much, causing the realm to be entirely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: This sovereign uses cleverness too much and has ruined the realm.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「款事諸君不必言，皇上祈簽奉先殿，意已決。」

translations.literal: He also said: "On the peace negotiations, gentlemen need not speak—the emperor draws lots at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors and his mind is already decided."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "On peace talks, do not speak—the emperor has decided by lot at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors."

sentences.zh: 諸人退，謂升誹謗君父，泄禁中語。

translations.literal: The gentlemen withdrew and said Sheng had slandered the ruler and father and leaked forbidden palace speech.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew accusing Sheng of slandering the throne and leaking palace secrets.

sentences.zh: 仁禎、國遴等交章論之，斥升大不道，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Renzhen, Guolin, and others submitted memorials in succession, denouncing Sheng for great iniquity and lack of the rites of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhen, Guolin, and others memorialized that Sheng had committed grave iniquity and violated ministerial propriety.

sentences.zh: 士亮及他言官繼之，疏數十上。

translations.literal: Shiliang and other remonstrance officials followed; memorials numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and other censors followed with dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，削升籍。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and struck Sheng from the register.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck Sheng from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 已而士亮連劾諸督撫張福臻、徐世蔭、朱大典、葉廷貴，及兵部侍郎呂大器、甘肅總兵馬爌，事多施行。

translations.literal: Thereafter Shiliang in succession impeached grand coordinators Zhang Fuzhen, Xu Shiyin, Zhu Dadian, Ye Tinggui, and Vice Minister of War Lü Daqi and Gansu regional commander Ma Huang—many matters were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang then impeached commanders Zhang Fuzhen, Xu Shiyin, Zhu Dadian, Ye Tinggui, Vice Minister Lü Daqi, and Gansu commander Ma Huang—many charges succeeded.

sentences.zh: 又請召舊諫臣姚思孝、何楷、李化龍、張作楫、張焜芳、李模、詹爾選、李右讜、林蘭友、成勇、傅元初，而恤已死者吳執禦、魏呈潤、傅朝佑、吳彥芳、王績燦、葛樞，帝頗采納。

translations.literal: He also requested summoning former remonstrance officials Yao Sixiao, He Kai, Li Hualong, Zhang Zuoji, Zhang Kunfang, Li Mo, Zhan Erxuan, Li Youdan, Lin Lanyou, Cheng Yong, and Fu Yuanchu, and showing favor to the dead Wu Zhiyu, Wei Chengrun, Fu Chaoyou, Wu Yanfang, Wang Jican, and Ge Shu—the emperor largely adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recall former censors Yao Sixiao, He Kai, Li Hualong, and others, and honor the dead Wu Zhiyu, Fu Chaoyou, Wang Jican, and others—the emperor largely agreed.

sentences.zh: 周延儒出督師，請士亮贊畫軍務。

translations.literal: When Zhou Yanru went out to supervise the army, he requested Shiliang to assist in planning military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yanru took field command he asked Shiliang to assist in military planning.

sentences.zh: 延儒獲譴，士亮亦削職下獄，久之釋歸。

translations.literal: Yanru incurred reproach; Shiliang was also struck from office and sent to prison; after a long time he was released and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanru was punished, Shiliang was stripped and imprisoned, later released.

sentences.zh: 福王時，復官。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 國變後卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after the fall of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 詹爾選

translations.literal: Zhan Erxuan
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Erxuan

sentences.zh: 詹爾選，字思吉，撫安人。

translations.literal: Zhan Erxuan, styled Siji, was a native of Fu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Erxuan, whose courtesy name was Siji, came from Fu'an.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 時詔廷臣舉守令，爾選言：「縣令多而難擇，莫若精擇郡守。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered court ministers to recommend prefects and magistrates; Erxuan said: "District magistrates are many and hard to choose—better to select prefects with care.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered recommendations of local officials, Erxuan argued: "Magistrates are too numerous to judge well—choose prefects carefully instead.

sentences.zh: 郡守賢，縣令無不賢。」

translations.literal: If prefects are worthy, district magistrates will all be worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Worthy prefects will produce worthy magistrates."

sentences.zh: 因請起用侍郎陳子壯、推官湯開遠，報聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested raising Vice Minister Chen Zizhuang and investigating magistrate Tang Kaiyuan; report was made.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recall Vice Minister Chen Zizhuang and investigating magistrate Tang Kaiyuan; the court noted his request.

sentences.zh: 明年，疏劾陳啟新：「宜召九卿科道，覿面敷陳，罄其底蘊。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized impeaching Chen Qixin: "It is fitting to summon the nine ministers and the censorate and supervising secretaries, face them and set forth policies, and exhaust their inner substance.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he impeached Chen Qixin: "Summon the nine ministers and censors, hear them in person, and test their substance.

sentences.zh: 果有他長，然後授官。

translations.literal: If they truly have other strengths, then afterward grant office.
translations.idiomatic: Only if they prove capable should offices be granted.

sentences.zh: 遽爾授官，非所以重名器。

translations.literal: Hastily granting office is not the way to honor name and vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Hasty appointment dishonors public office.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書謝升、大學士溫體仁不加駁正，屍素可愧。」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Xie Sheng and Grand Secretary Wen Tiren did not refute and correct—deadwood is shameful."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xie Sheng and Grand Secretary Wen Tiren failed to object—such deadwood is shameful."

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大學士錢士升以爭武生李琎搜括富戶，忤旨，引罪乞休去。

translations.literal: Before long Grand Secretary Qian Shisheng, because he contested military licentiate Li Zhen's search and exaction of wealthy households, offended the imperial will, acknowledged guilt and requested leave to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Grand Secretary Qian Shisheng, opposing military licentiate Li Zhen's exactions from wealthy households, offended the throne and resigned.

sentences.zh: 爾選上疏曰：

translations.literal: Erxuan submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Erxuan memorialized:

sentences.zh: 輔臣引咎求黜，遽奉回籍之諭。

translations.literal: The assisting minister acknowledged guilt and sought dismissal, yet immediately received an edict sending him home.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister confessed fault and sought dismissal, yet was sent home at once.

sentences.zh: 夫人臣所以不肯言者，其源在不肯去耳。

translations.literal: The reason ministers are unwilling to speak lies in their being unwilling to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers refuse to speak because they refuse to leave office.

sentences.zh: 輔臣肯言肯去，臣實榮之，獨不能不為朝廷惜此一舉也。

translations.literal: That an assisting minister was willing to speak and willing to leave—I truly honor it, yet I cannot but grieve this move for the court.
translations.idiomatic: A minister willing both to speak and to resign honors us—but the court cannot afford this loss.

sentences.zh: 琎以非法導主上，其端一開，大亂將至。

translations.literal: Zhen led the sovereign by illegal means; once that gate opens, great disorder will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen led Your Majesty by illegal means; once that gate opens, catastrophe follows.

sentences.zh: 輔臣憂心如焚，忽奉改擬之命，遂爾執奏。

translations.literal: The assisting minister's heart burned with worry; suddenly he received an order to revise the proposal and thereupon held to his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister, anguished, held to his memorial despite a revised order.

sentences.zh: 皇上方嘉許不暇，顧以為疑君要譽耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty was just praising him without cease—did he think it suspicion of the ruler and seeking reputation?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty had just praised him—was this deemed disloyal self-promotion?

sentences.zh: 人臣無故疑其君，非忠也；

translations.literal: For a minister groundlessly to suspect his ruler is not loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Groundless suspicion of the ruler is not loyalty;

sentences.zh: 乃謂吾君萬舉萬當者，第容悅之借名，必非忠。

translations.literal: yet to say our ruler is right in ten thousand acts and only flatter in borrowed name is surely not loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: yet calling the ruler infallible while flattering him is no loyalty either.

sentences.zh: 人臣沽名，義所不敢出也，乃人主不以名譽鼓天下，使其臣屍位保寵，寡廉鮮恥，亦必非國家利。

translations.literal: For a minister to trade in reputation is what righteousness dares not permit; yet if the ruler does not rouse the realm with reputation, letting his ministers hold office and preserve favor, scant in integrity and shame, that too is surely not the state's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers must not trade in reputation—but rulers must not reward flattery that keeps corrupt men in office.

sentences.zh: 況今天下疑皇上者不少矣。

translations.literal: Moreover today those who doubt Your Majesty are not few.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover many today doubt Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 將驕卒惰，尚方不靈，億萬民命，徒供武夫貪冒，則或疑過於右武。

translations.literal: Generals arrogant and soldiers lax, the imperial sword ineffective, the lives of millions supplied only to greedy military men—some may suspect excessive emphasis on force.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant generals, lax soldiers, the imperial sword unused while millions feed military greed—some suspect excessive martialism.

sentences.zh: 穿劄與操觚並課，非是者弗錄。

translations.literal: Military drill and literary composition are examined together; those who are not so are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Military drill and literary tests are judged together; others are rejected.

sentences.zh: 人見賣牛買馬，絀德齊力，徒使強寇混跡於道途，父兄莫必其子弟，則或疑緩於敷文。

translations.literal: People see selling oxen to buy horses, virtue cut short and strength equalized, merely letting strong bandits mix on the roads with fathers and elder brothers unable to be sure of sons and younger brothers—some may suspect laxity in civil culture.
translations.idiomatic: People see oxen sold for horses, merit leveled down, bandits mingling on the roads while families cannot trust their own—some suspect neglect of civil order.

sentences.zh: 免覲之說行，上意在蘇民困也，而或疑朝宗之大義，不敵數萬路用之金錢；

translations.literal: The policy of exempting court audiences proceeds—the sovereign's intent is to ease the people's hardship—yet some may suspect that the great principle of attending court is outweighed by tolls on the myriad routes;
translations.idiomatic: Exempting officials from court audiences was meant to ease hardship, yet some suspect toll revenue outweighs the duty to attend court;

sentences.zh: 駁問之事煩，上意在懲奸頑也，而或疑明啟之刑書，幾禁加等之紛亂。

translations.literal: repeated interrogations are numerous—the sovereign's intent is to punish the wicked and obstinate—yet some may suspect that clear penal codes nearly forbid aggravated penalties in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated interrogations were meant to punish the wicked, yet some suspect the penal code itself is in confusion.

sentences.zh: 其君子憂驅策之無當，其小人懼陷累之多門，明知一切茍且之政，或拊心愧恨，或對眾欷歔。

translations.literal: Gentlemen worry that driving and whipping are misplaced; petty men fear traps and entanglements on many sides; clearly knowing every expedient policy, some beat their breasts in shame, some sigh openly before the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy fear misguided policy; the base fear endless entrapment; all see expedient government and grieve openly or in secret.

sentences.zh: 輔臣不過偶因一事，代天下發憤耳，而竟郁郁以去，恐後之大臣無復有敢言者矣。

translations.literal: The assisting minister only happened to voice indignation on behalf of the realm for one matter, yet departed in dejection—fearing that hereafter great ministers will no longer dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister spoke once for the realm and left in sorrow—fearing no minister will speak again.

sentences.zh: 大臣不敢言，而小臣愈難望其言矣。

translations.literal: When great ministers dare not speak, lesser officials are still harder to expect speech from.
translations.idiomatic: If great ministers fall silent, lesser officials will hardly speak.

sentences.zh: 所日與皇上言者，惟苛細刻薄不識大體之徒，似忠似直，如狂如癡，售則挺身招搖，敗則潛形逋竄，駭心誌而爚耳目，毀成法而釀隱憂，天下事尚忍言哉！

translations.literal: Those who daily speak to Your Majesty are only petty, harsh, mean men who do not grasp the larger pattern—seeming loyal, seeming straight, like madmen, like fools; if successful they swagger forward, if defeated they hide and flee, shocking hearts and dazzling ears, destroying established law and brewing hidden worry—can the realm's affairs still be spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: Those who daily address you are petty, harsh men who seem loyal yet rave like madmen—success brings swagger, failure brings flight—destroying law and brewing hidden disaster. How can the realm endure!

sentences.zh: 祈皇上以遠大宅心，以簡靜率憲，責大臣弼違之義，作言官敢諫之風。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty with far-reaching mind and simple, quiet governance, charge great ministers with the duty of correcting errors, and create among remonstrance officials the wind of daring remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to think broadly, govern simply, demand correction from ministers, and restore bold remonstrance among censors.

sentences.zh: 寧獻可替否，毋藉口聖明獨斷，掩聖主之謙沖；

translations.literal: Better to offer what may replace what may not, than to take refuge in "the sage ruler decides alone," masking the sage ruler's humility;
translations.idiomatic: Better frank counsel than invoking imperial sole decision to silence humility;

sentences.zh: 寧進禮退義，毋藉口君恩未酬，飾引身之濡滯。

translations.literal: better to advance with ritual and withdraw with righteousness, than to take refuge in "grace not yet repaid," adorning delay in withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: better to advance by ritual and withdraw by righteousness than to plead unpaid grace while clinging to office.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不勝忄卷忄卷。

translations.literal: Your servant's foolishness cannot overcome earnest anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is earnestly anxious beyond words.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝震怒，召見武英殿，詰之曰：「輔臣之去，前旨甚明，汝安得為此言？」

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was shocked and angry, summoned him to the Wuying Hall, and interrogated him, saying: "The assisting minister's departure—the prior edict was very clear; how dare you speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor summoned him to the Wuying Hall in fury: "The chief minister's departure was clearly ordered—how dare you say this?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「皇上大開言路，輔臣乃以言去國，恐後來大臣以言為戒，非皇上求言意。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty has greatly opened the path of speech; the assisting minister departs the state because of speech—I fear later great ministers will take speech as warning; this is not Your Majesty's intent in seeking speech."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your Majesty opened the path of speech; the chief minister leaves because he spoke—I fear ministers will shun speech hereafter."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「建言乃諫官事，大臣何建言？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Offering remonstrance is the affair of remonstrance officials—what remonstrance do great ministers offer?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Remonstrance is for censors—why do great ministers remonstrate?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「大臣雖在格心，然非言亦無由格。

translations.literal: He replied: "Though great ministers rectify the heart, without speech there is no means to rectify.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Though ministers rectify the heart, they cannot do so without speaking.

sentences.zh: 大臣止言其大者，決無不言之理。

translations.literal: Great ministers speak only of great matters; there is never reason for not speaking.
translations.idiomatic: They speak on great matters; they cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 大臣不言，誰當言者？」

translations.literal: If great ministers do not speak, who should speak?"
translations.idiomatic: If ministers do not speak, who will?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕如此焦勞，天下尚疑朕乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I toil in anxiety like this—does the realm still doubt me?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I labor in such anxiety—does the realm still doubt me?

sentences.zh: 即尚方劍何嘗不賜，彼不能用，何言不靈？」

translations.literal: The imperial sword—when was it not bestowed? They could not use it—how is speech ineffective?"
translations.idiomatic: The imperial sword was bestowed—commanders failed to use it—how is that ineffective speech?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「誠如聖諭。

translations.literal: He replied: "Truly as the sage instruction says.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "As Your Majesty says.

sentences.zh: 但臣見督理有參疏，未蒙皇上大處分，與未賜何異？」

translations.literal: But your servant sees that supervisors submit impeachments yet Your Majesty has not imposed great punishment—what difference from not bestowing?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I see impeachments unanswered by great punishment—as if the sword were never given.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「刑官擬罪不合，朕不當駁乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When penal officials' proposed punishments do not accord, should I not reject them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When punishments proposed do not fit, should I not reject them?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「刑官不職，但當易其人，不當侵其事。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If penal officials are derelict, only replace the men—do not invade their function."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Replace incompetent judges—do not usurp their role."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝言一切茍且之政，何者為茍且？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You speak of every expedient policy—what is expedient?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You cite expedient policies—which ones?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「加派。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Additional levies."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Additional levies."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「加派，因賊未平，賊平何難停。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Additional levies are because bandits are not yet pacified; when bandits are pacified, how hard is it to stop?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Levies continue because rebels are not pacified; they will stop when rebels fall.

sentences.zh: 汝尚有言乎？」

translations.literal: Do you still have words?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you more to say?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「搜括抽扣亦是。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Search, exaction, and withholding are also so."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Search, exaction, and withholding as well."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此供軍國之用，非輸之內帑。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This supplies military and state use—not sent to the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That funds the army and state—not the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 汝更何言？」

translations.literal: What more do you say?"
translations.idiomatic: What else?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「即捐助亦是。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Even donation drives are so."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Donation drives too."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「本令願捐者聽，何嘗強人？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Originally it was ordered that those willing to donate might do so—when was anyone forced?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Donations were voluntary—who was forced?"

sentences.zh: 時帝聲色俱厲，左右皆震懾，而爾選詞氣不撓。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor's voice and countenance were both severe; those at his side were all shaken, yet Erxuan's tone did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's voice was fierce; attendants trembled, yet Erxuan did not bend.

sentences.zh: 帝又詰發憤諸語，及帖黃簡略，斥為欺罔，命錦衣提下。

translations.literal: The emperor again interrogated the phrases about venting indignation and the brief summary strip, denounced them as deception, and ordered the Embroidered Uniform Guard to seize and take him down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor challenged his indignant phrases and brief summary as deceit and ordered the guard to seize him.

sentences.zh: 爾選叩頭曰：「臣死不足惜，皇上幸聽臣，事尚可為。

translations.literal: Erxuan kowtowed and said: "Your servant's death is not worth cherishing; may Your Majesty favor listening to your servant—affairs can still be done.
translations.idiomatic: Erxuan kowtowed: "My death is nothing—if Your Majesty listens, affairs may yet be saved.

sentences.zh: 即不聽，亦可留為他日思。」

translations.literal: Even if you do not listen, it may be kept for reflection another day.
translations.idiomatic: Even if not, keep my words for another day.

sentences.zh: 帝愈怒，罪且不測，諸大臣力救，乃命系於直廬。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier; punishment was uncertain; the great ministers strove to rescue him, and he was ordered imprisoned in the direct quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged; ministers rescued him; he was imprisoned in the privy council quarters.

sentences.zh: 明日下都察院議罪，議止停俸。

translations.literal: The next day the case went to the Censorate to fix punishment; they proposed only suspension of salary.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Censorate proposed only salary suspension.

sentences.zh: 帝以語涉誇詡，並罪視草御史張三謨，令吏部同議。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the language involved boasting, also punished drafting censor Zhang Sanmo and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, citing boastful language, also punished drafting censor Zhang Sanmo and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to join deliberation.

sentences.zh: 請鐫五級，以雜職用。

translations.literal: They requested demotion by five ranks for use in miscellaneous posts.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed demotion five ranks to miscellaneous posts.

sentences.zh: 復不許，乃削籍歸。

translations.literal: Again not permitted; he was struck from the register and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; Erxuan was struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 自後言者屢薦，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Thereafter remonstrance officials repeatedly recommended him—all were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Censors repeatedly recommended him—in vain.

sentences.zh: 十五年，給事中沈迅、左懋第相繼薦。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Supervising Secretary Shen Xun and Zuo Maodi recommended him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Shen Xun and Zuo Maodi recommended him.

sentences.zh: 有詔召還，未及赴而都城陷。

translations.literal: There was an edict summoning his return; before he could go the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: A recall was ordered; before he could arrive the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王立，首起故官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was first raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu first restored his former office.

sentences.zh: 未上，群小用事，憚爾選鯁直，令補外僚，遂不出。

translations.literal: Before he took office, petty men held power and feared Erxuan's blunt uprightness; he was ordered to fill an outer post and thereupon did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men in power feared his blunt integrity and posted him outside; he refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 國變後，又十二年而終。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change, another twelve years passed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died twelve years after the fall of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 湯開遠

translations.literal: Tang Kaiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Tang Kaiyuan

sentences.zh: 湯開遠，字伯開，主事顯祖子也。

translations.literal: Tang Kaiyuan, styled Bokai, was the son of Director Tang Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Kaiyuan, whose courtesy name was Bokai, was the son of Director Tang Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 早負器識，經濟自許。

translations.literal: Early he bore capacity and insight and took upon himself economic statesmanship.
translations.idiomatic: He showed early talent and aspired to practical statesmanship.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，由舉人為河南府推官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, from recommended scholar he became investigating magistrate of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen he became investigating magistrate of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝惡廷臣玩愒，持法過嚴。

translations.literal: The emperor hated court ministers' laxity and held the law overly strict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor despised court laxity and enforced the law harshly.

sentences.zh: 開遠疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Kaiyuan memorialized in remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦以來，明罰敕法。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, punishments have been made clear and law enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, punishments have been sternly enforced.

sentences.zh: 自小臣至大臣，蒙重譴下禁獄者相繼，幾於刑亂國用重典矣。

translations.literal: From petty officials to great ministers, those who received heavy punishment and entered prison succeeded one another—nearly the chaos of punishments in a state that uses heavy statutes.
translations.idiomatic: From petty clerks to great ministers, imprisonment followed imprisonment—nearly the chaos of a state ruled by harsh law.

sentences.zh: 見廷臣薦舉不當，疑為黨徇；

translations.literal: Seeing court ministers' recommendations improper, he suspected factional favor;
translations.idiomatic: Improper recommendations were suspected as factional favor;

sentences.zh: 惡廷臣執奏不移，疑為藐抗。

translations.literal: hating court ministers' holding to memorials without yielding, he suspected contempt and resistance.
translations.idiomatic: firm memorials were suspected as defiant contempt.

sentences.zh: 以策勵望諸臣，於是戴罪者多，而不開以立功之路；

translations.literal: Using strategy and encouragement toward the ministers, thus many bore guilt yet no path to merit through achievement was opened;
translations.idiomatic: Urged to strive, many bore guilt yet no path opened to merit through achievement;

sentences.zh: 以詳慎責諸臣，於是引罪者眾，而不諒其致誤之由。

translations.literal: using careful scrutiny to charge the ministers, thus many acknowledged guilt, yet the causes of their errors were not understood.
translations.idiomatic: charged with excessive scrutiny, many confessed fault without understanding why they erred.

sentences.zh: 墨吏宜逮，然望稍寬出入，無絀能臣。

translations.literal: Corrupt officials ought to be seized, yet hope for slight leniency in coming and going, not cutting off able ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials should be seized, yet with some leniency so able men are not lost.

sentences.zh: 至三時多害，五方交警，諸臣怵參罰，惟急催科，民窮則易為亂。

translations.literal: When the three seasons had many disasters and the five directions all had alarms, the ministers feared impeachment and only urgently pressed tax collection; when the people were exhausted, disorder was easy.
translations.idiomatic: When disasters struck every season and alarms rose on every side, officials feared impeachment and only pressed taxes—exhausted people rebel easily.

sentences.zh: 陛下寬一分在臣子，即寬一分在民生，此可不再計決者。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is lenient one degree toward ministers, that is one degree of leniency toward the people's livelihood—this need not be reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Leniency toward ministers is leniency toward the people—this needs no further debate.

sentences.zh: 尤望推諸臣以心，待諸臣以禮，諭中外法司以平允。

translations.literal: Especially hope to extend heart to the ministers, treat ministers with ritual, and instruct inner and outer judicial offices in fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Extend your heart to ministers, treat them with ritual, and instruct all courts in fairness.

sentences.zh: 至錦衣禁獄，非寇賊奸宄，不宜輕入。
