translations.literal: As for the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison, unless bandits, traitors, or villains, they should not lightly enter.
translations.idiomatic: The guard prison should not receive anyone but traitors and felons.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，摘其疏中「桁楊慘毒，遍施勞臣」語，責令指實。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, extracted from his memorial the phrase "the pillory cruel and poisonous, spread over toiling ministers," and ordered him to name specifics.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized the phrase "cruel torture spread over toiling ministers" and demanded specifics.

sentences.zh: 乃上奏曰：

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted:

sentences.zh: 時事孔棘，諸臣有過可議，亦有勞可準；

translations.literal: The times are critically urgent; the ministers have faults that may be discussed and also merit that may be weighed;
translations.idiomatic: Times are desperate; ministers have faults to judge and merit to weigh;

sentences.zh: 有罪可程，亦有情可原。

translations.literal: there is guilt that may be measured and also circumstance that may be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: guilt to measure and circumstance to forgive.

sentences.zh: 究之議過不足懲過，而後事轉因前事以灰心；

translations.literal: In the end, debating faults is insufficient to punish faults, while later affairs turn because of earlier affairs to lose heart;
translations.idiomatic: Debating faults does not punish them; later work dies because of earlier blame;

sentences.zh: 聲罪不足服罪，而故者更藉誤者以實口。

translations.literal: proclaiming guilt is insufficient to satisfy guilt, while the deliberate use the mistaken to fill the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: denunciation does not satisfy justice; the guilty hide behind the mistaken.

sentences.zh: 綜核太過則要領失措，懲創太深則本實多缺。

translations.literal: Comprehensive scrutiny too great and essentials are lost; punishment and correction too deep and the root substance has many gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive scrutiny loses essentials; excessive punishment hollows governance.

sentences.zh: 往往上以為宜詳宜新之事，而下以為宜略宜仍之事；

translations.literal: Often what above is held to be what ought to be detailed and new, below is held to be what ought to be brief and retained;
translations.idiomatic: What the court calls innovation, the country calls needless change;

sentences.zh: 朝所為縲辱擯棄不少愛之人，又野所為推重愾嘆不可少之人。

translations.literal: those whom the court binds, humiliates, and casts aside without sparing, are those whom the wilds push forward, esteem, and sigh that they cannot be spared.
translations.idiomatic: men the court disgraces are men the country esteems;

sentences.zh: 上與下異心，朝與野異議，欲天下治平，不可得也。

translations.literal: Above and below at odds, court and country in dispute—wishing the realm governed and at peace cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: court and country at odds—peace is impossible.

sentences.zh: 蘇州僉事左應選任昌黎縣令，率土著保孤城。

translations.literal: Suzhou vice commissioner Zuo Yingxuan, serving as magistrate of Changli County, led native inhabitants to defend the isolated city.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou vice commissioner Zuo Yingxuan, as magistrate of Changli, led local militia to hold the isolated city.

sentences.zh: 事平之日，擢任監司。

translations.literal: When affairs were pacified, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乃用小過，卒以贓擬。

translations.literal: Yet because of a minor fault, in the end he was charged with corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a minor fault led to a corruption charge.

sentences.zh: 城池失守者既不少貸，捍禦著績者又不獲原，諸臣安所適從哉？

translations.literal: Those who lost cities were not much spared, while those who defended with achievement were not pardoned—where should ministers turn?
translations.idiomatic: City-losers were spared little while defenders won no mercy—what path remains for officials?

sentences.zh: 事急則鉅萬可捐，事平則錙銖必較。

translations.literal: When affairs are urgent, tens of thousands may be spent; when affairs are calm, every cash must be compared.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis millions are spent freely; in peace every coin is counted.

sentences.zh: 向使昌黎不守，同於遵、永，不知費朝廷幾許金錢，安所得涓滴而問之？

translations.literal: If Changli had not been held, like Zunyi and Yong, who knows how much of the court's money would have been spent, and whence could one ask for a trickle?
translations.idiomatic: Had Changli fallen like Zunyi and Yong, what vast sums would the court have spent—and who could begrudge a trifle afterward?

sentences.zh: 臣所惜者此其一。

translations.literal: What your servant regrets is this, the first point.
translations.idiomatic: This is my first regret.

sentences.zh: 給事中馬思理、御史高倬，值草場火發，狂奔盡氣，無救燎原，此不過為法受過耳，更欲以他罪論，則甚矣。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Ma Sili and Censor Gao Zhuo, when the pasture fire broke out, ran with all their strength yet could not stop the spreading blaze—this is merely suffering punishment under the law; to wish to judge them on other crimes goes too far.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sili and Gao Zhuo exhausted themselves fighting a pasture fire they could not stop—punishment under law is enough; further charges go too far.

sentences.zh: 今歲盛夏雪雹，地震京圻，草場不爇自焚。

translations.literal: This year in midsummer there were snow and hail, earthquake in the capital region, and the pasture burned without being kindled.
translations.idiomatic: That summer brought hail, earthquakes around the capital, and a pasture fire that lit itself.

sentences.zh: 陛下不寬刑修省，反嚴鞫而長系之，非所以召天和，稱善事也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not ease punishments and cultivate self-examination, but instead strictly interrogates and long imprisons them—not the way to summon Heaven's harmony or be called doing good.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of easing punishment and examining yourself, you interrogate and imprison them—this does not restore Heaven's harmony.

sentences.zh: 臣所惜者此其一。

translations.literal: What your servant regrets is this, the first point.
translations.idiomatic: This is another regret.

sentences.zh: 宣大巡按胡良機，陛下知其諳練，兩任巖疆，尋因過誤褫革，輿論惜之，豈成命終難反汗哉！

translations.literal: Xuan-Da touring inspector Hu Liangji—Your Majesty knew his experience; he served twice on the frontier, then was dismissed for a fault; public opinion regretted it—can a completed appointment never be reversed?
translations.idiomatic: Frontier inspector Hu Liangji, twice proven on the border, was dismissed for a fault the public regretted—can such appointments never be reversed?

sentences.zh: 臣所惜者此其一。

translations.literal: What your servant regrets is this, the first point.
translations.idiomatic: This is a third regret.

sentences.zh: 監兌主事吳澧，宵旦河干，經營漕事，運弁稽違，量行責戒，乃褫革之，又欲究治之。

translations.literal: Grain transport supervisor Wu Li toiled day and night on the river managing transport affairs; transport officers delayed and violated rules, and he imposed measured rebuke and warning—yet he was dismissed and they wished to pursue punishment further.
translations.idiomatic: Grain supervisor Wu Li toiled on the river; when transport officers violated rules he rebuked them proportionally—yet he was dismissed and threatened with further punishment.

sentences.zh: 夫兵嘩則為兵易將，將嘩則為武抑文，勇於嘩而怯於鬥，安用此驕兵驕將為也！

translations.literal: When soldiers mutiny, replace the soldiers; when generals mutiny, suppress the civil with the military—brave in mutiny yet cowardly in battle—of what use are these arrogant soldiers and arrogant generals!
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers mutiny so replace soldiers; generals mutiny so civil authority is crushed—bold in mutiny, cowardly in battle—what use are such arrogant troops?

sentences.zh: 臣所惜者此又其一。

translations.literal: What your servant regrets is this again, one more point.
translations.idiomatic: This is yet another regret.

sentences.zh: 末復為都御史陳於廷、易應昌申辨。

translations.literal: Finally he again pleaded for Censor-in-Chief Chen Yuting and Yi Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He also pleaded for Censor-in-Chief Chen Yuting and Yi Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 河南流賊大熾，開遠監左良玉軍，躬擐甲胄，屢致克捷。

translations.literal: Roving bandits in Henan raged greatly; Kaiyuan supervised Zuo Liangyu's army, personally donned armor, and repeatedly achieved victories.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan rebels raged, Kaiyuan supervised Zuo Liangyu's army in armor and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 帝以天下用兵，意頗重武，督、撫失事多逮系，而大將率姑息。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the realm used troops everywhere, greatly valued military affairs; grand coordinators and governors who failed were mostly seized and imprisoned, while great generals were generally indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: With war everywhere the emperor valued the military; failed civil commanders were imprisoned while generals were indulged.

sentences.zh: 開遠以為偏，八年十月上疏曰：

translations.literal: Kaiyuan held this biased; in the tenth month of the eighth year he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Finding this unjust, in the tenth month of the eighth year he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 比年寇賊縱橫，撫、鎮為要。

translations.literal: In recent years bandits and rebels ran rampant; grand coordinators and regional commanders were essential.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years rebels ran rampant; grand coordinators and regional commanders were essential.

sentences.zh: 乃陛下於撫臣則懲創之，於鎮臣則優遇之。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty punishes and corrects grand coordinators while treating regional commanders with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty punishes coordinators while favoring regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 試觀近日諸撫臣，有不褫奪、不囚系者乎？

translations.literal: Look at recent grand coordinators—is there one not stripped or imprisoned?
translations.idiomatic: Look at recent coordinators—is any not stripped or imprisoned?

sentences.zh: 諸帥臣及偏裨，有一禮貌不崇、升蔭不遂者乎？

translations.literal: Among commanders and subordinate officers, is there one whose ritual courtesy was not honored or whose promotion and hereditary privilege was not granted?
translations.idiomatic: Among commanders and subordinates, who lacks honors or hereditary privilege?

sentences.zh: 即觀望敗衄罪狀顯著者，有不寬假優容者乎？

translations.literal: Even those whose crimes of watching and defeat are manifest—is there one not leniently pardoned and indulged?
translations.idiomatic: Even manifest cowards and defeaters—who is not pardoned?

sentences.zh: 夫懲創撫臣，欲其惕而戒也；

translations.literal: Punishing and correcting grand coordinators is to make them wary and cautious;
translations.idiomatic: Punishing coordinators should make them vigilant;

sentences.zh: 優遇武臣，欲其感而奮也。

translations.literal: favoring military officials is to make them moved and stirred to effort.
translations.idiomatic: favoring generals should stir them to fight.

sentences.zh: 然而封疆日破壞、寇賊日蔓延者，分別之法少也。

translations.literal: Yet as frontier territories are daily broken and bandits daily spread, the method of distinction is too little.
translations.idiomatic: Yet frontiers collapse and rebels spread—the distinction is too weak.

sentences.zh: 撫臣中清操如沈棨，幹濟如練國事，捍禦兩河、身自為將如元默，拮據兵事、沮賊長驅如吳甡，或麗爰書，或登白簡，其他未可悉數。

translations.literal: Among grand coordinators, integrity like Shen Qi, executive ability like Lian Guoshi, defending the two rivers and personally becoming a general like Yuan Mo, managing military affairs and blocking the rebels' long advance like Wu Shen—or they faced the executioner's block or white bamboo impeachment; others cannot all be listed.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy coordinators like Shen Qi, Lian Guoshi, Yuan Mo, and Wu Shen faced impeachment or the block; the list is long.

sentences.zh: 而武臣桀驁恣睢，無日不上條陳，爭體統。

translations.literal: Yet military men are arrogant and domineering, daily submitting memorials, contending for precedence and protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Yet generals grow arrogant, daily memorializing over protocol.

sentences.zh: 一旦有警，輒逡巡退縮，即嚴旨屢頒，褒如充耳。

translations.literal: Once there is alarm, they hesitate and shrink back; even when stern edicts are repeatedly issued, they fill the ears like praise.
translations.idiomatic: At alarm they shrink; stern edicts pass like empty praise.

sentences.zh: 如王樸、尤世勛、王世恩輩，其罪可勝誅哉！

translations.literal: Such as Wang Pu, You Shixun, and Wang Shien—their crimes are beyond execution!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu, You Shixun, and Wang Shien deserve death many times over!

sentences.zh: 秦撫甘學闊有《法紀全疏》一疏，請正縱賊諸弁以法，明旨顧切責之。

translations.literal: Shaanxi grand coordinator Gan Xuekuo had a memorial "Complete Law and Discipline," requesting that bandit-releasing officers be corrected by law; the clear edict instead sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi coordinator Gan Xuekuo asked to punish officers who let rebels escape; the throne rebuked him instead.

sentences.zh: 然則自今以後，敗將當不問矣。

translations.literal: Then from today onward, defeated generals need not be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, defeated generals need never answer.

sentences.zh: 文臣未必無才能，乃有寧甘斥黜必不肯任不敢任者，以任亦罪，不任亦罪，不任之罪猶輕，而任之罪更重也。

translations.literal: Civil officials are not necessarily without ability, yet some would rather accept dismissal than hold office they dare not hold—because holding office is guilt and not holding is guilt, and not holding is lighter while holding is heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Able civil officials refuse office because serving is punished and refusing is punished—and serving is punished more harshly.

sentences.zh: 誠欲使諸臣踴躍任事，在寬文法，原情實，分別去留，毋以一眚棄賢才。

translations.literal: Truly wishing to make ministers leap to serve affairs lies in relaxing penal law, excusing by true circumstance, distinguishing retention and removal, and not abandoning worthy talent for one fault.
translations.idiomatic: To make ministers serve boldly, relax law, weigh circumstances, distinguish merit and fault, and not discard talent for one error.

sentences.zh: 至韎韐之夫，不使怯且欺者幸乎其間，則賞罰以平，文武用命矣。

translations.literal: As for men in leather armor, do not let the cowardly and deceitful prosper among them—then rewards and punishments will be level and civil and military will obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Among armored men, do not let cowards and frauds thrive—then rewards and punishments will balance and all will obey.

sentences.zh: 帝以撫臣不任者，無所指實，責令再陳。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the grand coordinators who were unfit had no named specifics, ordered him to set forth again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding no names, ordered specifics.

sentences.zh: 乃上言曰：

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted:

sentences.zh: 朝廷賞罰無章，於是諸臣之不肯任不敢任者罪，而肯任敢任者亦罪，且其罪反重。

translations.literal: Court rewards and punishments are without rule; thus the guilt of ministers who will not serve and dare not serve, and those who will serve and dare serve are also guilty—and the latter's guilt is even heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Without clear rewards and punishments, those who refuse office and those who accept it are both guilty—and the willing bear the heavier guilt.

sentences.zh: 勸懲無當，欲勘定大亂，未之前聞。

translations.literal: Encouragement and correction are misplaced; wishing to quell great disorder—never before heard.
translations.idiomatic: Misplaced encouragement makes quelling chaos unheard of.

sentences.zh: 從來無詘督臣以伸庸帥者，至今而楊嗣昌不得關其說；

translations.literal: Never before was a supervising minister disgraced to elevate a mediocre commander—until today Yang Sichang could not close the argument;
translations.idiomatic: Never before were civil supervisors disgraced to elevate mediocre commanders—until Yang Sichang could not prevail;

sentences.zh: 從來無抑言路以伸劣弁者，至今而王肇坤不得保其秩。

translations.literal: never before was the remonstrance path suppressed to elevate inferior officers—until today Wang Zhaokun could not keep his rank.
translations.idiomatic: never before was the remonstrance path crushed for inferior officers—until Wang Zhaokun lost his rank.

sentences.zh: 王樸恇怯暴著，聽敵飽去，猶得與吳甡並論，播之天下，不大為口實哉！

translations.literal: Wang Pu's timidity and violence were manifest; he let the enemy leave sated, yet could be discussed alongside Wu Shen and broadcast to the realm—is this not great material for talk!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu let the enemy depart sated yet ranks with Wu Shen—what scandal for the realm!

sentences.zh: 若撫臣之不肯任不敢任者，如了陜西之胡廷晏，山西之仙克謹、宋統殷、許鼎臣，何以當日處分視後皆輕？

translations.literal: As for grand coordinators who will not serve and dare not serve, such as Hu Tingyan who finished Shaanxi, Xian Kejin, Song Tongyin, and Xu Dingchen of Shanxi—why were their punishments at the time all lighter than afterward?
translations.idiomatic: Coordinators who failed like Hu Tingyan and Xu Dingchen were punished more lightly than later cases—why?

sentences.zh: 練國事、元默承大壞極敝之後，竭力撐持，何以當日處分較前更重？

translations.literal: Lian Guoshi and Yuan Mo, inheriting after great ruin and extreme exhaustion, strove to prop up support—why were their punishments at the time heavier than before?
translations.idiomatic: Lian Guoshi and Yuan Mo, inheriting ruin, strove to hold the line—why were they punished more harshly?

sentences.zh: 且近日為辦寇而誅督臣者一，逮督臣撫臣者二，褫撫臣者亦二。

translations.literal: Moreover recently for dealing with bandits one supreme commander was executed, two supreme commanders and grand coordinators were seized, and two grand coordinators were also stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Recently one supreme commander was executed for bandits, two coordinators seized, two stripped.

sentences.zh: 甚至巡方與撫臣並議，而並逮兩按臣；

translations.literal: Even touring inspectors were discussed together with grand coordinators and both touring inspectors were seized;
translations.idiomatic: Even touring inspectors were seized with coordinators;

sentences.zh: 計典與失事牽合，而並褫南樞臣。

translations.literal: examination honors were tied to failure and the southern chief minister was also stripped.
translations.idiomatic: examination honors were tied to failure and the southern chief minister stripped.

sentences.zh: 若監司、守令之獲重譴者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: As for surveillance commissioners, prefects, and magistrates who received heavy punishment, they cannot be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: Countless surveillance officials, prefects, and magistrates were heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 試問前後諸帥臣，有一誅且逮者乎？

translations.literal: Ask whether among former and later commanders there was one executed and seized?
translations.idiomatic: Name a commander who was executed or seized.

sentences.zh: 即降而偏裨，有一誅且逮者乎？

translations.literal: Even descending to subordinate officers, was there one executed and seized?
translations.idiomatic: Name a subordinate officer executed or seized.

sentences.zh: 甚至避寇、縱寇、養寇、助寇者，皆置弗問。

translations.literal: Even those who avoided bandits, released bandits, nourished bandits, and aided bandits were all left unasked.
translations.idiomatic: Those who avoided, released, fed, or aided rebels went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 即或處分，不過降級戴罪而已。

translations.literal: Even when punished, it was no more than demotion and wearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When punished at all, it was mere demotion or wearing guilt.

sentences.zh: 然則諸將之不肯任不敢任者，直謂之無罪可乎？

translations.literal: Then for generals who will not serve and dare not serve, may we directly call them without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Are generals who refuse service truly guiltless?

sentences.zh: 是陛下於文武二途，委任同，責成不同。

translations.literal: Thus Your Majesty in the two paths of civil and military entrusts equally yet holds to different standards of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty entrusts civil and military alike yet demands different standards.

sentences.zh: 明旨所謂一體者，終非一體矣。

translations.literal: The clear edict speaks of treating as one body—yet in the end it is not one body.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts speak of unity—yet civil and military are not one.

sentences.zh: 不特此也。

translations.literal: Not only this.
translations.idiomatic: Nor is that all.

sentences.zh: 按臣曾周當舊撫艱去，力障寇鋒，初非失事，乃竟從逮配，將來無肯任敢任之按臣矣。

translations.literal: Touring inspector Zeng Zhou, when the former grand coordinator entered mourning, forcefully blocked the bandit spearhead—at first not a failure—yet in the end was seized and banished; hereafter there will be no touring inspectors willing to serve boldly.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zeng Zhou blocked rebels during a coordinator's mourning yet was banished—who will serve boldly on inspection tours?

sentences.zh: 道臣祝萬齡拮據兵食，寢餌俱廢，至疽發於背，而遽行削籍，將來無肯任敢任之監司矣。

translations.literal: Circuit intendant Zhu Wanling struggled over troops and provisions, food and sleep both abandoned, until sores broke on his back—yet was abruptly struck from the register; hereafter there will be no circuit intendants willing to serve boldly.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendant Zhu Wanling labored until sores broke on his back yet was struck from the rolls—who will serve as intendant?

sentences.zh: 史洪謨作令宜陽，戰守素備，賊渡澠池，不敢薄城，及知六安，復有全城之績，而褫奪驟加，將來無肯任敢任之州縣矣。

translations.literal: Shi Hongmo as magistrate of Yiyang was always prepared for war and defense; when bandits crossed Mianchi they did not dare approach the city; as magistrate of Lu'an he again had the achievement of holding the whole city—yet stripping came suddenly; hereafter there will be no prefects and magistrates willing to serve boldly.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Shi Hongmo held Yiyang and Lu'an yet was suddenly stripped—who will hold local office boldly?

sentences.zh: 賊薄永寧，舊蜀撫張論與子給事鼎延傾貲募士，夙夜登陴，及論物故，鼎延請恤，並其子官奪之，將來無肯任敢任之鄉官矣。

translations.literal: When bandits pressed Yongning, former Sichuan grand coordinator Zhang Lun and his son, supervising secretary Dingyan, spent their wealth to recruit men and day and night manned the walls; when Lun died, Dingyan requested favor—and both father and son had office taken away; hereafter there will be no local gentry willing to serve boldly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun and his son defended Yongning at their own cost yet lost office when the father died—who will serve as local gentry?

sentences.zh: 吏部惟雜職多弊，臣鄉吳羽文竭力厘剔，致刀筆賈豎哄然而起，羽文略不為撓，乃以起廢一事，長系深求，將來無肯任敢任之部曹矣。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel has many abuses only in miscellaneous posts; your servant's fellow townsman Wu Yuwen strove to rectify them, causing clerks and brokers to rise in uproar yet Yuwen was hardly swayed—for one matter of raising the dismissed he was long imprisoned and deeply investigated; hereafter there will be no ministry clerks willing to serve boldly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuwen rectified ministry abuses and was long imprisoned for raising the dismissed—who will serve in the ministries boldly?

sentences.zh: 臣讀明旨，謂諸事皆經確核，以議處有銓部，議罪有法司，稽核糾舉有按臣也。

translations.literal: Your servant reads the clear edict, saying all affairs have been verified—punishment deliberation has the Ministry of Personnel, guilt deliberation has the judicial offices, verification and impeachment have touring inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: The edict says all was verified—yet the Ministry of Personnel, courts, and inspectors each only report upward.

sentences.zh: 不知詔旨一下，銓部即議降議革，有肯執奏曰「此不當處」者乎？

translations.literal: Once the edict descends, the Ministry of Personnel at once proposes demotion and dismissal—is there one who memorializes holding that this should not be treated so?
translations.idiomatic: Once edicts descend, the Ministry of Personnel demotes at once—who dares object?

sentences.zh: 一下法司，即擬配擬戍，有肯執奏曰「此不當罪」者乎？

translations.literal: Once it goes to the judicial offices, they at once propose banishment and garrison—is there one who memorializes holding that this should not be punished so?
translations.idiomatic: Courts at once propose banishment—who dares say the guilt does not fit?

sentences.zh: 至查核失事，按臣不過據事上聞，有原功中之罪、罪中之功，乞貸於朝廷者乎？

translations.literal: As for verifying failure, touring inspectors only report affairs upward—is there one who begs the court to spare, with merit within guilt and guilt within merit?
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors report failures—who begs the throne to weigh merit within guilt?

sentences.zh: 是非諸臣不肯分別也，知陛下一意重創，言之必不聽，或反以甚其罪也。

translations.literal: It is not that ministers are unwilling to distinguish—knowing Your Majesty is bent on heavy punishment, speech will surely not be heard, or will instead deepen guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers do not refuse to distinguish—they know the throne demands harsh punishment and silence deepens guilt.

sentences.zh: 所以行間失事，無日不議處議罪，而於蕩寇安民毫無少補。

translations.literal: Therefore on the front lines failure is daily deliberated for punishment, yet pacifying bandits and settling the people gains not the slightest supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Daily punishments on the frontiers bring no peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 則今日所少者，豈非大公之賞罰哉！

translations.literal: Then what is lacking today—is it not great public rewards and punishments!
translations.idiomatic: What lacks today is great public justice in rewards and punishments!

sentences.zh: 帝得奏大怒，命削籍，撫按解京訊治。

translations.literal: The emperor, receiving the memorial, was greatly angry, ordered him struck from the register, and the grand coordinator and touring inspector were to send him to the capital for interrogation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck him from the rolls and ordered him sent to the capital for trial.

sentences.zh: 河南人聞之，若失慈母。

translations.literal: When the people of Henan heard it, it was like losing a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Henan mourned him as if losing a mother.

sentences.zh: 左良玉偕將士七十余人合奏乞留，巡按金光辰亦備列其功狀以告。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu together with more than seventy generals and soldiers jointly memorialized begging he be retained; touring inspector Jin Guangchen also fully listed his merits in report.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu and seventy officers begged to keep him; inspector Jin Guangchen listed his merits.

sentences.zh: 帝為動容，命釋還戴罪辦賊。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved, ordered release and return to serve wearing guilt against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor released him to serve wearing guilt against bandits.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，討平舞陽大盜楊四。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year he pacified the great bandit Yang Si of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, first month, he pacified the great bandit Yang Si of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 論功當進秩，總理王家禎復薦之。

translations.literal: By merit he should be advanced in rank; Supreme Commander Wang Jiazhen again recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Merit entitled him to promotion; Supreme Commander Wang Jiazhen recommended him again.

sentences.zh: 乃擢按察僉事，監安、廬二郡軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of surveillance and supervised armies in An and Lu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice surveillance commissioner supervising An and Lu armies.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，太子將出閣。

translations.literal: That winter the heir apparent was to leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the heir apparent was to leave the palace.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「陛下言教不如身教。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your Majesty's verbal teaching is not as good as teaching by example.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Teaching by example surpasses words.

sentences.zh: 請謹幽獨，恤民窮，優大臣，容直諫，寬拙吏，薄貨財，疏滯獄，俾太子得習見習聞，為他日出治臨民之本。」

translations.literal: I request careful solitude, pity the people's poverty, favor great ministers, tolerate straight remonstrance, be lenient to clumsy officials, be light with wealth, clear stagnant prisons—so the heir apparent may habitually see and hear and have the root for governing and facing the people when he goes forth another day.
translations.idiomatic: Guard your solitude, pity the poor, favor ministers, tolerate frank counsel, spare clumsy officials, lighten levies, clear prisons—so the heir may learn to govern.

sentences.zh: 帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply accepted it.

sentences.zh: 是時，賊大擾江北，開遠數有功。

translations.literal: At this time bandits greatly disturbed Jiangbei; Kaiyuan had repeated merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits then ravaged Jiangbei; Kaiyuan won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 巡撫史可法薦其治行卓異，進秩副使，監軍如故。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Shi Kefa recommended his administration as outstandingly exceptional; he was advanced in rank to vice commissioner, supervising armies as before.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Shi Kefa praised his governance; he was promoted to vice commissioner while keeping military supervision.

sentences.zh: 十三年，與總兵官黃得功等大破革裏眼諸賊，賊遂乞降。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, together with regional commander Huang Degong and others he greatly defeated the Ge liyan bandits, and the bandits thereupon begged surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he and Huang Degong crushed the Ge liyan rebels, who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 朝議將用為河南巡撫，竟以勞瘁卒官，軍民鹹為泣下。

translations.literal: Court deliberation was about to use him as Henan grand coordinator, but he died in office from exhaustion; military and civilians all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The court was to make him Henan grand coordinator, but he died of exhaustion in office; soldiers and civilians wept.

sentences.zh: 贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs.

sentences.zh: 成勇，字仁有，安樂人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yong, styled Renyou, was a native of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yong, whose courtesy name was Renyou, came from Anle.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 授饒州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 謁鄒元標於吉水，師事之。

translations.literal: He visited Zou Yuanbiao at Jishui and took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Zou Yuanbiao at Jishui and became his student.

sentences.zh: 中使至，知府以下郊迎，勇不往，且捕笞其從人。

translations.literal: When palace envoys arrived, the prefect and below went to the suburbs to welcome them; Yong did not go, and moreover seized and flogged their attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When palace envoys arrived, the prefect welcomed them in the suburbs; Yong refused and flogged their attendants.

sentences.zh: 丁內外艱。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned both parents.

sentences.zh: 歷開封、歸德二府推官。

translations.literal: He served as investigating magistrate of Kaifeng and Guide prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating magistrate at Kaifeng and Guide.

sentences.zh: 流賊攻歸德，擊走之。

translations.literal: Roving bandits attacked Guide; he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Guide, he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，行取入京。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he entered the capital on metropolitan selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he entered the capital on metropolitan selection.

sentences.zh: 時變考選例，優者得為翰林。

translations.literal: At the time the metropolitan examination selection rule changed; the excellent could become Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Selection rules changed; top candidates could enter the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 公論首勇，而吏部尚書田唯嘉抑之，勇得南京吏部主事以去。

translations.literal: Public opinion ranked Yong first, yet Minister of Personnel Tian Weijia suppressed him; Yong obtained chief clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and left.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion favored Yong, but Minister Tian Weijia suppressed him; Yong took a Nanjing ministry post and left.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，帝御經筵，問講官保舉考選得失，諭德黃景昉訟勇及朱天麟屈。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the emperor held the classics lecture and asked the lecturers about the gains and losses of metropolitan selection recommendations; Lecturer Huang Jingfang pleaded that Yong and Zhu Tianlin were wronged.
translations.idiomatic: The next year at the classics lecture the emperor asked about selection; Lecturer Huang Jingfang pleaded Yong and Zhu Tianlin were wronged.

sentences.zh: 帝親策諸臣，天麟得翰林，而勇以先赴南京不與。

translations.literal: The emperor personally examined the ministers; Tianlin obtained Hanlin, while Yong, because he had already gone to Nanjing, did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor examined candidates personally; Tianlin entered Hanlin while Yong, already in Nanjing, did not participate.

sentences.zh: 尋用御史塗必泓言，授南京御史。

translations.literal: Soon, adopting Censor Tu Bihong's words, he was appointed Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Censor Tu Bihong's recommendation, he became a Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌奪情入閣，言者鹹獲譴。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang entered the Grand Secretariat on leave from mourning; remonstrators all received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang entered the Grand Secretariat while still in mourning; every critic was punished.

sentences.zh: 勇憤，其年九月上疏言：「嗣昌秉樞兩年，一籌莫展，邊警屢驚，群寇滿野。

translations.literal: Yong was indignant; in the ninth month of that year he submitted a memorial, saying: "Sichang has held the pivot for two years without a single plan unfolded; frontier alarms repeatedly startle, and bandits fill the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Yong memorialized that September: "Sichang has held power two years without a plan; the frontier alarms repeatedly and rebels fill the countryside.

sentences.zh: 清議不畏，名教不畏，萬世公義不畏，臣竊為青史慮。」

translations.literal: He does not fear clear criticism, does not fear name and teaching, does not fear public righteousness for ten thousand generations—your servant privately worries for the blue history."
translations.idiomatic: He fears neither public opinion, nor moral teaching, nor eternal justice—I fear for how history will judge this."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大怒，削籍提訊，詰主使姓名。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angry, struck him from the register and sent him for interrogation, demanding the instigator's name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck him from the rolls, interrogated him, and demanded who had put him up to it.

sentences.zh: 勇獄中上書言：「臣十二年外吏，數十日南臺，無權可招，無賄可納，不知有黨。」

translations.literal: Yong from prison submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant was twelve years an outer official and several tens of days on the southern censorate—no power to recruit, no bribes to accept; I know nothing of factions."
translations.idiomatic: From prison Yong wrote: "Twelve years as a local official, weeks as a censor—I had no patron to serve and no bribes to take; I know no faction."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，竟戍寧波衛。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and in the end sent him to garrison Ningbo Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor banished him to Ningbo Guard.

sentences.zh: 中外薦者十余疏，不召。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court more than ten memorials recommended him—he was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten recommendation memorials came from court and country—in vain.

sentences.zh: 後以御史張瑋言，執政合詞請擢用，帝以勇宥罪方新，不當復職，命以他官用。

translations.literal: Later, on Censor Zhang Wei's words, the chief ministers jointly requested promotion and employment; the emperor held that Yong's pardon was still fresh and he ought not resume office, ordering he be used in another post.
translations.idiomatic: Later the chief ministers asked to employ him on Zhang Wei's recommendation; the emperor said his pardon was too recent and ordered another post—

sentences.zh: 甫聞命，而京師陷。

translations.literal: He had just heard the order when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: but before he could take it the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起御史，不赴。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was raised to censor but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu made him a censor; he refused.

sentences.zh: 披緇為僧，越十五年而終。

translations.literal: He donned monastic robes and died after fifteen more years.
translations.idiomatic: He became a monk and died fifteen years later.

sentences.zh: 陳龍正

translations.literal: Chen Longzheng
translations.idiomatic: Chen Longzheng

sentences.zh: 陳龍正，字惕龍，嘉善人。

translations.literal: Chen Longzheng, styled Tielong, was a native of Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Longzheng, whose courtesy name was Tielong, came from Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 父於王，福建按察使。

translations.literal: His father Yu Wang was Fujian surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Wang was Fujian surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 龍正遊高攀龍門。

translations.literal: Longzheng studied at Gao Panlong's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Longzheng studied under Gao Panlong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年成進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi and was appointed secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the seventh year of Chongzhen and was appointed a secretarial draftsman.

sentences.zh: 時政尚綜核，中外爭為深文以避罪，東廠緝事尤冤濫。

translations.literal: At the time government favored comprehensive scrutiny; within and without all competed in harsh wording to avoid guilt, and the Eastern Depot's investigations were especially wrongful and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Government favored harsh scrutiny; officials everywhere wrote severe charges to avoid blame, and the Eastern Depot was worst of all.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，熒惑守心，下詔修省，有「哀懇上帝」語。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year Mars stayed in the Heart constellation; an edict ordered self-examination, with words "pleading earnestly to God."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, fifth month, Mars stood in the Heart; the emperor ordered self-examination, pleading earnestly to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 龍正讀之泣，上《養和》、《好生》二疏。

translations.literal: Longzheng wept on reading it and submitted the two memorials "Nurturing Harmony" and "Cherishing Life."
translations.idiomatic: Longzheng wept and submitted his Nurturing Harmony and Cherishing Life memorials.

sentences.zh: 略曰：「回天在好生，好生無過減死。

translations.literal: In summary he said: "Turning back Heaven lies in cherishing life; cherishing life is nothing beyond reducing death.
translations.idiomatic: He argued: "Restoring Heaven's favor means cherishing life—and cherishing life means sparing the condemned.

sentences.zh: 臯陶贊舜曰『罪疑惟輕』，是聖人於折獄不能無失也。

translations.literal: Gao Yao praised Shun, saying, 'When guilt is doubtful, treat it lightly'—the sage in judging cases cannot be without error.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yao praised Shun: when guilt is doubtful, judge lightly—even sages err in court.

sentences.zh: 蓋獄情至隱，人命至重，故不貴專信，而取兼疑，不務必得，而甘或失。

translations.literal: For case circumstances are most hidden and human lives most weighty; therefore one does not prize exclusive belief but takes combined doubt, does not strive for certain gain but is willing to accept occasional loss.
translations.idiomatic: Cases are hidden and lives precious—so doubt the prosecution rather than demand certainty, and accept occasional mercy over relentless punishment.

sentences.zh: 臣居家所見聞，四方罪犯，無甚窮兇奇謀者，及來京師，此等乃無虛月。

translations.literal: What your servant saw and heard at home: criminals from the four directions were not very greatly vicious or strangely plotting; yet coming to the capital, such cases were not absent in any month.
translations.idiomatic: At home I saw few truly monstrous criminals; in the capital scarcely a month passes without executions.

sentences.zh: 且罪案一成，立就誅磔，亦宜有所懲戒，何犯者若此累累？

translations.literal: Moreover once a guilt case is formed, execution and dismemberment follow at once—there ought to be some warning; why are offenders so numerous?
translations.idiomatic: Cases end in immediate execution—yet offenders only multiply. Where is the deterrent?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下懷帝舜之疑，寧使聖主有過仁之舉，臣下獲不經之愆。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to harbor Emperor Shun's doubt, rather letting the sage ruler have an overly humane act and ministers incur an uncanonical fault."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to harbor Shun's doubt—better the ruler seem overly humane than ministers fear to speak."

sentences.zh: 蓋陰指東廠事也。

translations.literal: This covertly pointed at Eastern Depot affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This covertly targeted the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 越數日，果諭提督中官王之心不得輕視人命雲。

translations.literal: After several days, an edict indeed instructed supervising eunuch Wang Zhixin not to lightly regard human lives.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the throne instructed eunuch Wang Zhixin not to treat life lightly.

sentences.zh: 其冬，京師戒嚴，詔廷臣舉堪任督、撫者。

translations.literal: That winter the capital was on alert; an edict ordered court ministers to recommend those fit to serve as supreme commanders and grand coordinators.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, with the capital on alert, ministers were asked to recommend commanders and coordinators.

sentences.zh: 御史葉紹颙舉龍正。

translations.literal: Censor Ye Shaoyong recommended Longzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ye Shaoyong recommended Longzheng.

sentences.zh: 久之，刑部主事趙奕昌請訪求天下真賢才。

translations.literal: After a long time, Ministry of Justice chief clerk Zhao Yichang requested searching the realm for true worthy talent.
translations.idiomatic: Later chief clerk Zhao Yichang asked the throne to seek true talent nationwide.

sentences.zh: 帝令奕昌自舉，亦以龍正對。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yichang to recommend himself; he also answered with Longzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yichang to name someone; he too named Longzheng.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不用。

translations.literal: The emperor used neither.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used neither man.

sentences.zh: 龍正居冷曹，好言事。

translations.literal: Longzheng dwelt in a cold post and was fond of speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Longzheng held a minor post and loved to speak on policy.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，彗星見。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, tenth month, a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬至，大雷電雨雹。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice there was great thunder, lightning, and hail.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice brought thunder, lightning, and hail.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，京師大風，天黃日眚，浹旬不解。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year a great wind struck the capital; the sky turned yellow and the sun was obscured for ten days without clearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, second month, great winds yellowed the sky and dimmed the sun for ten days.

sentences.zh: 龍正皆應詔條奏，大指在聽言省刑。

translations.literal: Longzheng on each occasion memorialized in response to edicts; the main point lay in heeding words and reducing punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Longzheng answered each omen with memorials urging the throne to listen and lighten punishments.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏，帝復下詔求言，云「拯困蘇殘，不知何道」。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year the emperor again issued an edict seeking remonstrance, saying, "To rescue hardship and revive the wounded—I know not what way."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth summer the emperor again sought counsel: "To rescue the distressed—I know not how."

sentences.zh: 龍正上言：「拯困蘇殘，以生財為本，但財非折色之謂。

translations.literal: Longzheng submitted: "To rescue hardship and revive the wounded, take generating wealth as root—but wealth is not what is meant by converted silver.
translations.idiomatic: Longzheng replied: "Relief begins with real wealth—not converted silver levies.

sentences.zh: 以折色為財，則取於人而易盡，必知本色為財，則生於地而不窮。

translations.literal: Taking converted silver as wealth, one takes from people and it is easily exhausted; one must know grain-in-kind as wealth, then it is born from the earth and is inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: Silver taken from the people is soon exhausted; grain from the earth is inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 今持籌之臣曰設處，曰搜括，曰加派，皆損下之事，聚斂之別名也。

translations.literal: Today the men holding counting rods speak of arrangement, of search and exaction, of additional levies—all are matters that harm those below, aliases for exaction and accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Today's financiers speak of arrangement, exaction, and surtaxes—all names for squeezing the people.

sentences.zh: 民日病，國奚由足？

translations.literal: The people daily grow sick—how can the state be sufficient?
translations.idiomatic: The people grow poorer daily—how can the state be rich?

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜專意墾荒，申明累朝永不起科之制，招集南人巨賈，盡墾荒田，使畿輔、河南、山東菽粟日多，則京倉之積，邊軍之餉，皆可隨宜取給。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that one should concentrate on opening wasteland, clarify the regulation of successive reigns that newly opened land never pays tax, gather great merchants of the south, fully open wasteland fields, make beans and grain in the capital region, Henan, and Shandong daily increase—then the capital granaries' stores and frontier armies' pay may all be supplied as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Open wasteland, uphold the old rule that new fields pay no tax, recruit southern merchants to farm idle land in the capital region, Henan, and Shandong—then granaries and frontier pay need not depend on distant transport.

sentences.zh: 或平糴，或拜爵，或中監，國家命脈不專倚數千里外之轉運，則民間加派自可盡除。」

translations.literal: Whether fair-price sale, ennoblement, or eunuch supervision—the state's life-vein need not rely solely on transport thousands of li away; then additional levies among the people may be fully removed."
translations.idiomatic: Fair sales, honors, or supervised farming could follow—then the realm need not depend on transport from afar and surtaxes could end."

sentences.zh: 然是時中原多殘破，有田不得耕，龍正執常理而已。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the central plains were much broken; there was land yet could not be plowed—Longzheng held only to constant principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the central plains lay in ruins and fields could not be tilled—Longzheng spoke from principle alone.

sentences.zh: 翌日復進《用人探本疏》，帝皆優容焉。

translations.literal: The next day he again submitted "Memorial on Probing the Root of Employing Men"; the emperor was all leniently tolerant.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he submitted Probing the Root of Employing Men; the emperor received it leniently.

sentences.zh: 給事中黃雲師劾其學非而博，言偽而辯，又以進墾荒議為陵競。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Huang Yunshi impeached him: learning wrong yet broad, words false yet eloquent—and further held that advancing the wasteland-opening proposal was overbearing competition.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Huang Yunshi impeached his learning as shallow but showy and his wasteland proposal as presumptuous.

sentences.zh: 帝不問。

translations.literal: The emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 時議欲用龍正為吏部，御史黃澍以偽學詆之。

translations.literal: At the time deliberation wished to use Longzheng in the Ministry of Personnel; Censor Huang Shu slandered him as false learning.
translations.idiomatic: Some wished to appoint him to the Ministry of Personnel; Censor Huang Shu denounced him as a false scholar.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，左遷南京國子監丞。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year he was transferred down to vice director of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, first month, he was demoted to vice director of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 甫抵家而京師陷。

translations.literal: He had just reached home when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: He had just reached home when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王立於南京，用為祠祭員外郎，不就。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing, he was appointed outer court attendant of sacrifices but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu appointed him sacrifices attendant; he refused.

sentences.zh: 南京不守，龍正已得疾，遂卒。

translations.literal: When Nanjing was not held, Longzheng was already ill and thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell, Longzheng was already ill and died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：崇禎時，僉壬相繼枋政，天下多故，事之可言者眾矣。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: In the Chongzhen reign, crafty men succeeded one another in holding government; the realm had many troubles and matters that could be spoken of were many.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Under Chongzhen, crafty men held power in succession; the realm was troubled and much deserved to be said.

sentences.zh: 許譽卿諸人，抨擊時宰，有直臣之風。

translations.literal: Xu Yuqing and others, attacking the ministers of the time, had the wind of straight ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuqing and his fellows attacked the ministers of the day with a censor's integrity.

sentences.zh: 然傅朝佑死杖下，姜埰、熊開元得重譴，而詹爾選抗雷霆之威，顧獲放免。

translations.literal: Yet Fu Chaoyou died under the rod; Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan received heavy punishment, while Zhan Erxuan resisted thunderbolt authority yet was released and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chaoyou died under the rod; Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan were heavily punished; yet Zhan Erxuan defied imperial wrath and was spared.

sentences.zh: 言天子易，言大臣難，信哉。

translations.literal: To speak of the Son of Heaven is easy; to speak of great ministers is hard—how true.
translations.idiomatic: Criticizing the emperor is easy; criticizing great ministers is hard—how true.

sentences.zh: 湯開遠以疏遠處僚，侃侃論事，憤惋溢於辭表。

translations.literal: Tang Kaiyuan, from a distant outer post, spoke frankly on affairs; indignation and regret overflowed in his words and tables.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Kaiyuan, from a distant post, spoke frankly while grief and anger filled his memorials.

sentences.zh: 就其所列國勢，亦重可慨矣夫！

translations.literal: Judging from the national situation he set forth, it is also greatly worthy of sighing!
translations.idiomatic: Judging from the state of the realm he described, how deeply it moves one to sigh!
